https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: HHA Marks World Maritime Day with inaugural outdoor evening event
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
More than 100 businesspeople, charities and local politicians came together in Essex as a trust port hosted its first ever Stakeholder Summer Drinks Reception.
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) hosted the inaugural event in a marquee on the Green in Harwich on Thursday, September 24, bringing together top minds from across the Essex and Suffolk maritime and wider logistics spheres, alongside representatives from local community groups and councils.
The event marked World Maritime Day, highlighting the critical importance the sector plays to economies, and served as an opportunity to premier a new video on HHA’s role in enabling the UK’s international trade.
Helen Rudd, Sustainability and Partnerships Director at HHA, said:
“It was fantastic to welcome so many people to Harwich as we celebrated the important role the maritime industry plays in our daily lives.
“The Haven is vital to the UK’s prosperity and our role as its guardian would not be possible were it not for the wider chain of businesses and organisations championing British maritime.
“Our Stakeholder Summer Drinks Reception was a celebration of each and every one of them while helping us introduce others in our local community to the role we play here at HHA.
“A huge thank you to everyone who joined us for such a lovely evening.
“We’re also incredibly grateful for the lovely weather, with the clear blue skies making for a perfect backdrop for us all to wave goodbye to summer.”
Aside from the video premiere, guests were also treated to canapes and fizz. A raffle was also hosted to raise money for HHA’s charity of the year, CVS Tendring.
The raffle, alongside sales of honey produced atop HHA’scorporate office, Harbour House, raised an impressive £550 for the charity.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: People’s Emergency Briefing to screen in Harwich
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority is supporting a screening of a 50-minute film highlighting the impact of the climate and nature crisis.
The People’s Emergency Briefing is being screened for free at the Electric Palace Cinema in Harwich on Wednesday, September 23.
The documentary, presented by Chris Packham, explores the imminent implications of the climate and environmental crisis and its impact on health, the UK’s food supply and the economy.
While shining a light on the issue, it proposes positive ways to combat it, showing the huge benefits of seeking a greener future.
Linzi Jobber, Sustainability Manager at HHA, said: “This is an important documentary that helps us understand the scale of the climate and environmental challenges we face, and why action is needed.
“Maintaining and preserving the Haven and its unique environment is a responsibility we take very seriously, so this is a cause close to our hearts.
“We hope the screening encourages people to have open conversations about the challenges ahead, but also the positive solutions and actions we can take together to build a more resilient and sustainable future.”
Ticket information can be found at www.electricpalace.com .

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Harwich Haven Authority seeks next generation of maritime talent through new graduate programme
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) is giving budding mariners, engineers, communications specialists and office staff the chance to get hands-on experience on one of the UK’s busiest and most important waterways.
The two-year programme will see graduates experience multiple departments and contribute to real projects, solve genuine business challenges and help shape the future of the organisation.
Vanessa Mann, Head of People & Culture at HHA, said:
“At Harwich Haven Authority we live and breathe our employee value proposition – where work means more.
“That means not only providing opportunities for the next generation to enter our industry, but to truly immerse them in the world of maritime and the genuine impacts our work has on our communities, the economy and the environment.
“That includes supporting our operational teams in bringing the world’s biggest ships into port, maintaining our fleet of vessels, crafting internal and external communications or crunching numbers in the finance department.
“We want every graduate to experience the vast scope of opportunities available to them in the fantastic world of maritime.”
As part of the programme, each graduate will receive an executive sponsor, an individual development plan and quarterly development reviews alongside formal training and a structured rotations plan.
HHA has a long history of supporting those in early careers through their award-winning apprenticeship scheme and is a proud member of ‘The 5% Club’ – businesses with at least 5% of its staff in ‘earn and learn’ positions.
Applications for the four available graduate positions are now open until Sunday, October 4.
More information on how to apply can be found at www.hha.co.uk/about/careers.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: 2026-04 Ballast Water Discharge
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Mariners are reminded of Harwich Haven Authority Byelaws 1994 No. 33 Discharge of Ballast:
“ Except in a case of emergency a vessel is prohibited from discharging water ballast into the harbour without the consent of the Harbour Master .”
Vessels must contact Harwich VTS (via VHF 71 or hha.vts@hha.co.uk ) in advance for permission to discharge ballast water and return a completed ‘Request to Discharge Ballast Water’ form (VTS.16), which can be download from http://hha.co.uk/operations/downloads/ .
Either a valid International Ballast Water Management Certificate or evidence of exemption status must be submitted with the form. Harwich VTS will then confirm if permission has been granted.
For further information refer to MSN 1908 and MGN 675 The merchant shipping (control and management of ships’ ballast water and sediments) regulations 2022 as amended.
This Port Information Notice replaces 2018-03, which is now withdrawn.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Royal Navy joins forces with Freeport East and Harwich Haven Authority to showcase region’s maritime resilience
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
HMS Severn docked at Harwich
Freeport East and Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) welcomed the Royal Navy to Harwich today [12 August 2026], bringing together senior figures from industry, local government and the maritime sector to showcase the future of regional resilience and security.
The event, Resilience in Harwich with the Royal Navy , took place on Wednesday 12 August at the Pier Hotel in Harwich and coincided with the docking of a Royal Navy River Class Offshore Patrol Vessel, HMS Severn, at Harwich – marking a rare visit that gave guests the opportunity to tour the ship.
Hosted jointly by Freeport East and HHA, and attended by a network of business, civic and industry leaders, the session brought the Royal Navy’s Naval Regional Command and Presentation team to Harwich to set out their vision for a ‘Hybrid Navy’, which would blend crewed platforms, autonomous systems and data and digital technology to deliver operational effect around the UK coastline.
Attendees heard directly from the Royal Navy about its plans for the region – including the county’s affiliation with the new Type 31 frigate HMS Venturer, formalised in 2024 and the first such link between Essex and a warship in 30 years. Currently under construction in Scotland and due to enter service later this decade, HMS Venturer connects more than 1.8 million people across Essex, from Colchester to Southend, with the Royal Navy’s next generation of frigates.
Freeport East’s Steve Beel addressed the strategic importance of Harwich to the UK’s maritime and defence footprint.
Steve Beel, CEO at Freeport East, said:
“It has been our pleasure to host the Royal Navy here in Harwich today and to have the opportunity to bring local industry and political leaders together to hear about the future of maritime resilience in the region. Harwich has always punched above its weight when it comes to maritime activity, from the days of Christopher Jones, the Harwich-born captain and part-owner of the Mayflower, through to the Kindertransport in the Second World War and on to being a prime link for millions of passengers to the European continent.  Days like this are a reminder that this coastline still matters both strategically and economically to the whole United Kingdom.”
Dr Jo North, CEO at Harwich Haven Authority, added:
“Harwich has always been a place where maritime expertise, innovation and collaboration come together, so it is a privilege to welcome the Royal Navy and so many partners to the Haven. As the organisation responsible for the safe navigation of one of the UK’s busiest and most strategically important waterways, Harwich Haven Authority know that strong partnerships and shared knowledge are at the heart of building a resilient and thriving maritime future.
“Bringing together industry, government and defence gives us the opportunity to share ideas, explore new technologies and strengthen the relationships that will support our region for years to come. By working together, we can unlock new opportunities for innovation, economic growth and skills, while ensuring our ports and coastal communities continue to play a vital role in the UK’s prosperity.”
Naval Regional Commander of London and Eastern England, Commodore Timothy Green CBE ADC said:
“I am delighted to join HMS SEVERN in Harwich this week.  This warship visit is an ideal opportunity to engage with the Maritime and Security communities in Essex and meet many Civic and Defence Industry leaders.
“Essex has a long and proud history of supporting the Royal Navy and this region remains a key maritime county with one of the largest coastlines in the UK.  Furthermore, Harwich remains a strategically vital port for both the region and the whole of the UK.
“I know that HMS SEVERN’s visit will further strengthen the very strong bonds between the Royal Navy and Essex.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Sea-Changers Harwich Haven Fund Launched
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Linzi Jobber, Sustainability Manager (left) and Jenni Murphy, Environment Manager (right) from HHA
A new grant fund to support marine conservation projects around the coastal borders of Suffolk and Essex has been launched by Harwich Haven Authority (HHA).
The Trust Port has partnered with national charity Sea-Changers to launch the new Harwich Haven Fund, starting with an initial £10,000 donation.
It will support projects in HHA’s area of responsibility – ranging from citizen science to direct action – alongside engagement and education initiatives that teach people about conservation, stewardship and sustainability to help preserve the area for the next generation.
Small grants of up to £500 are available year-round, while the main grant scheme for amounts up to £2,500 is open until the end of September.
Linzi Jobber, Sustainability Manager at HHA, said: “We’re delighted to be partnering with Sea-Changers to support the people and projects taking positive action to protect our marine environment.
“Investing in grassroots innovation is an important way to encourage fresh thinking and practical solutions that will help shape the future of our Haven.
“This partnership reflects our commitment as a Trust Port to bring environmental stewardship and supports our wider ambition to drive a more sustainable future for our coastal communities.”
The new fund is the latest in a plethora of sustainability and social value initiatives introduced by HHA – with successes including its popular Coastal Discoveries beach school programme delivered in partnership with Boskalis Westminster and the popular Swim Safe scheme, now in its seventh year.
As well as monetary contributions, successful applicants to the fund may also benefit from future additional, relevant support from HHA, particularly in the marine space.
Rachel Lopata MBE, Co-Founder of Sea-Changers, added: “We’re delighted to be partnering with Harwich Haven Authority to create this fund, which reflects the kind of place-based, practical conservation work that makes a real difference for UK coastal and marine environments.
“By backing local action and community-led projects, we can help protect biodiversity, strengthen awareness, and create lasting benefits for people and nature along this important stretch of the coast.”
Applications to the Sea-Changers Harwich Haven Fund can be made online via www.sea-changers.org.uk/harwich-haven .

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: New Company formed to deliver dredging in the Haven
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) and leading dredging and marine services provider Boskalis Westminster have announced the formation of a new joint venture company, Suffolk Dredging LLP.
The new company brings together HHA’s extensive knowledge of the Haven and Boskalis Westminster’s expertise in dredging and marine operations, creating a strong platform to support the long-term maintenance and resilience of one of the UK’s most important waterways.
As part of its launch, Suffolk Dredging LLP has been awarded Harwich Haven Authority’s maintenance dredging contract, taking responsibility for maintaining the navigable depths required to support safe and efficient vessel movements throughout the Haven for the next 5 years.
The joint venture has also been awarded the licence for the Tiamat, an innovative dredging system developed by HHA, creating opportunities to deploy this technology internationally and supporting the future growth ambitions of the new company.
The creation of Suffolk Dredging LLP represents a significant milestone for both organisations, combining local operational knowledge with world-leading dredging capabilities. The partnership is expected to enhance operational efficiency, support innovation in dredging practices and strengthen the long-term sustainability of maintenance dredging operations within the Haven.
Jake Storey, Chief Financial Officer at Harwich Haven Authority, said:
“The formation of Suffolk Dredging LLP marks an exciting new chapter for Harwich Haven Authority. By bringing together our expertise with Boskalis’ global experience, we have created a partnership that will deliver high-quality maintenance dredging services for the Haven while also creating opportunities to develop and commercialise innovative technologies such as Tiamat.”
Paul de Jong, Managing Director of Boskalis Westminster, said:
“We are delighted to be partnering with Harwich Haven Authority in Suffolk Dredging LLP. This joint venture combines complementary strengths and creates a platform for delivering safe, efficient and innovative dredging solutions, both within the Haven and potentially in new markets around the world.”
The award of both the maintenance dredging contract and the Tiamat licence provides Suffolk Dredging LLP with a strong foundation from which to support navigation, drive innovation and pursue future growth opportunities.
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) and Boskalis are also working together to deliver the innovative BUDS (Beneficial Use of Dredged Sediment) project – working with local conservationists on a pioneering initiative that will reuse dredged sediment from harbour maintenance to restore saltmarsh habitat and enhance coastal protection around the Haven.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Harwich Haven Authority to implement NCOS UKC system
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority to implement NCOS UKC system
Harwich Haven Authority is set to further bolster its impressive safety record with the implementation of DHI Seaport’s NCOS ONLINE Dynamic Under Keel Clearance (UKC) system.
The trust port – responsible for managing the waterways into two of Britain’s busiest ports – has signed a deal with DHI Seaport to implement the technology across three phases.
It is hoped the technology will help boost the port’s capacity as it looks to continue welcoming the world’s biggest and deepest draught vessels exceeding 17m.
The system is currently being built with the first phase expected to go live before the end of this year.
Louise Fennessy, Deputy Harbour Master (Pilotage) at HHA, said: “It is hugely exciting to introduce this world-leading technology to HHA.
“We continue to welcome the world’s deepest vessels to our ports thanks to initiatives like our 2023 Channel Deepening Project – helping the Haven stand out as the UK’s premier place for container trade. This is the latest step in continuing this progress.
“This new system will help us more safely and accurately determine the UKC required to cater for these larger vessels, further minimising disruption and increasing reliability for our customers.
“We look forward to continuing our work with DHI Seaport as the implementation process progresses.”
DHI Seaport is currently developing a detailed model of the Harwich harbour area and its approaches – which will also bring together live data on tides, swell and wind alongside the latest bathymetrics.
The system will be integrated with HHA’s existing VTS Kongsberg system, enabling vessel data to be automatically transferred into NCOS ONLINE
Training will be provided by DHI Seaport to HHA’s VTS duty officers and pilots throughout the first four-month period.
DHI Seaport representatives will also be on site for around one week each month to provide support, answer questions and assist with the implementation process.
Simon Brandi Mortensen, Managing Director of DHI Seaport, said: “Harwich Haven Authority is in our view already leading the way by  adopting cutting edge technology for improving their port operations.
“DHI Seaport is deeply honoured to have been chosen as their trusted digital systems provider for dynamic UKC and optimised vessel traffic scheduling at the Port of Felixstowe.”
Stage Two has been earmarked for Q1 2027 and will include a gradual and carefully managed transition from the current static 10% UKC requirement to a dynamic UKC within the harbour area.
Stage Three will see Ipswich integrated into the system before a final integration stage across the remaining HHA ports.
Ports who have already successfully implemented the NCOS system include the Port of Brisbane in Australia, whose CEO Neil Stephens said: “NCOS Online has added significant value to the Port of Brisbane through the last decade.
“I have no doubt that this partnership between DHI Seaport and Harwich Haven Authority will deliver similar benefits to the customers and stakeholders of the UK’s largest container port.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Popular free Swim Safe sessions expand into Suffolk
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A free initiative which has taught thousands of north Essex children how to stay safe at sea is expanding into Felixstowe as it celebrates its seventh year.
Swim Safe, delivered in partnership with Swim England and Harwich Haven Authority, will run from early July until the end of August on both the Tendring and East Suffolk coasts.
It comes as Harwich Haven Authority celebrates Maritime Safety Week, beginning July 6 – a national awareness week promoting water safety.
The Swim Safe sessions are open to children aged 7 to 14, providing vital and potentially lifesaving knowledge to stay safe in, on and around open water.
Linzi Jobber, Sustainability Manager at Harwich Haven Authority, said: “We are proud to continue supporting Swim England’s Swim Safe programme, helping thousands of local children gain vital water safety skills and confidence in open water.
“Expanding these popular sessions into Suffolk is a huge milestone and reflects the popularity of these hugely important, potentially lifesaving courses.
“At Harwich Haven Authority, we want to ensure our waters are safe for everyone to enjoy and supporting young people to understand how to stay safe in and around the water is a key priority for us.
“The Swim Safe programme is an excellent initiative that gives children practical lifesaving knowledge while encouraging them to enjoy the water responsibly. We’re delighted to play a part in making these opportunities available to families across our community.
“We would encourage parents and guardians to sign children up for this summer’s sessions and help more young people benefit from this fantastic programme.”
Swim Safe was first launched in Cornwall in 2013 before being introduced to Harwich in 2019.
More than 3,000 children have taken part locally since.
Sessions are available for both school groups and the public and take place at Dovercourt Bay Beach in Essex and opposite the Felixstowe Leisure Centre.
Children must be able to swim at least 25 metres unaided to take part in the sessions.
Adam Goymer, National Water Safety Manager at Swim England, said: ”Swim Safe, now in its 13th year, provides children with the opportunity to apply their self-rescue skills learnt during indoor swimming lessons into an outdoor environment.
“Supported by a trained Swim Safe instructor, children take part in four games, bringing the Water Safety Code to life, before entering the water to complete a safe self-rescue circuit of in-water skills.
“Swim Safe is a fun way to get children ready for safe swimming in open water.”
More information on available dates and how to book a session can be found at www.swimsafe.org.uk .

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Suffolk tech firm scoops award with HHA for cutting-edge ‘digital twin’ technology
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A Suffolk technology company and Harwich Haven Authority have scooped a national AI award for Capella – a ‘digital-twin’ that helps simulate vessel operations in the Haven.
The team from Entopy, which is based in Newmarket, won the AI SME Business of the Year award jointly with the harbour authority and the University of Essex at the The AI Summit London, the UK’s premier gathering for AI professionals and innovators.
The cutting-edge Capella system can simulate and predict ship movements in the Haven as they make their way to Felixstowe, helping the authority guide them safely and efficiently into port.
Toby Mills, CEO of Entopy, said: “We were delighted to recieve the joint award win and for Capella to be recognised with this honour.
“The Port of Felixstowe and the operations in the Haven are crucial to UK PLC and with 40% of all UK containerised trade coming into the port, the impacts on the economy are substantial.
So to be part of an innovative project which digitalises operations to make them more effective and efficient is a privilege and we have enjoyed every step of the journey so far with Harwich Haven Authority.”
Every vessel movement across the Haven is resource heavy – requiring link-up between multiple organisations and the coordination of the availability of pilots, safe boarding conditions, tidal windows, berth availability, all under compliance to strict channel-passing rules.
The new technology will help reduce any disruption in the system, improving forecasting, automating situational awareness and optimising efficiency.
Harbourmaster Will Barker said: “This innovative technology gives valuable insight into the movements of vessels in the haven, helping us to strengthen supply chain performance in and out of the Port of Felixstowe.
“Capella helps identify the optimal arrival time for each vessel and enables ‘just-in-time arrival’, avoiding costly delays and allowing vessels to optimise speeds, reduce fuel costs and emissions.
“The technology supports both forward planning and live operations, continuously flagging emerging issues to ensure everything runs smoothly.
“It’s a brilliant piece of technology and we are so pleased it has been recognised by the judges at the AI summit.
“We would like to thank Entopy for their hard work and expertise in bringing this cutting-edge technology to fruition.”
The National AI Awards judges praised the project as: “A great example of AI being utilised beyond point solutions into a holistic approach in order to provide an intelligence engine to a complex operational activity.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Female mariners say working on the water is the ‘best’ job they’ve ever had
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A trio of mariners have called on more women to consider careers in maritime to mark an international awareness day.
The three mariners from Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) have shared their stories to celebrate International Day for Women in Maritime, a globally recognised day every May 18 aiming to advance gender equality.
Each of the three have their own unique stories that brought them to the industry, although all three share one thing in common – they were not made aware of the incredible opportunities available to them in the maritime industry at school.
Among them is experienced sailor Sally Hesketh, who swapped a career in TV working on shows like The Voice to become an Assistant Coxswain working on HHA’s pilot launch boats, helping get pilots out to sea before they bring some of the world’s biggest vessels into port.
Her varied maritime career to date has also seen her building fast crafts for the military and working for the British Antarctic Survey.
“You would think TV and sailing are very different,” she said. “But they are also very similar. There’s lots of time pressures, irregular hours and you find yourself working with a real variety of people.
“A friend of mine had sailed from Portsmouth to New York and the Caribbean – and she told me about a website where people could post their profiles to find work and learning opportunities in sailing. I thought it sounded too good to be true but decided to give it a go.
“I ended up learning how to sail on a boat in Woodbridge and I caught the bug. I bought myself a little wooden boat and sailed to the Isles of Scilly and back.
“I love it. It’s a great job – people always say that every day is different in their job, and they might think that’s not the case working on a pilot launch as you’re doing the same journey every day. But it really is – every pilot launch job you do is different with their own unique challenges and there’s always something new to learn.”
Marine Apprentice Isabel Curle is also no stranger to adventure, having previously worked seasons in Greece.
Her role sees her helping out across different departments, whether that’s maintaining HHA’s fleet of boats or assisting pilots on their launches.
“I grew up in Harwich seeing the ships coming in but never thought I’d one day be working on the water,” she said.
“I didn’t even know it was a career option. It’s not something that’s ever promoted to you as a young woman.
“It’s the best job I’ve ever had. I absolutely love it.
“I would say that previous roles I’ve worked in have had superiorist views when it comes to gender – but that really isn’t the case at HHA. They prioritise your work ethic, not your gender.
“I would highly recommend it. My advice would be to throw yourself out there – so many of us started without any prior experience in the sector but feel empowered. I’m really excited for the future.”

A floating barge bakery is all fired up after support from HHA helped a social enterprise secure a new oven.

What is the Bread and Roses Barge?
The Bread and Roses Barge is a community interest company operating on the Thames Sailing Barge, May .
The vessel, first built in 1891, is based in St. Osyth and is operated by an all-female team who have transformed her into a floating support hub for women who have experienced trauma.

When the Bread and Roses team were looking for a new oven to open the barge to the public, they turned to our Harwich Haven Authority Fund – operated in partnership with Essex Community Foundation.
We were delighted to support them, contributing £1,409 towards the specialist oven, which is specially designed for micro bakeries.
The Bread and Roses team are now planning to open the barge for baking sessions, with plans to eventually take the May on tours of other ports in the region and extend their support network further once intensive work has been done.
What the Bread and Roses Barge said

“It has been amazing. There’s a genuine enthusiasm for learning how to bake.
“We fired the oven up for the first time in January and it is so, so good – the bread bakes beautifully.
“It is the perfect oven to have on board and has been especially designed for micro bakeries like us.
“The groups have really enjoyed it – we’ve got a large table on board and it’s been amazing watching everyone stood around it, buzzing with excitement.
“Thank you to HHA for their support.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: The Tunnel That Never Was
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich’s most ambitious idea… and greatest April Fool
In the years after the First World War, Harwich faced tough times: high unemployment, dwindling trade and limited transport links. Enter local councillor and civil engineer John Elliott, a man full of bold ideas and even bigger ambition.
His solution? A tunnel beneath the estuary linking Harwich to Felixstowe – cutting out the long 30-mile detour via Manningtree and opening up the region to trade, travel and opportunity.
It was a visionary plan, but not everyone was convinced. Fellow councillors questioned the cost and practicality, and after months of heated debate, the idea stalled. Elliott, however, refused to let it go, campaigning tirelessly and even promoting the tunnel as a way to create jobs during a time of widespread unemployment.
Then, in April 1926, things took a bizarre turn.
Invitations were sent to newspapers and motorists across the country, announcing the grand opening of the Harwich–Felixstowe Tunnel. Hundreds of cars arrived in Harwich expecting celebrations, a ceremonial procession… and a brand-new tunnel.
There was just one problem:  it didn’t exist!
With no tunnel entrance, no ceremony and no explanation, confused visitors turned back or stayed to enjoy the spectacle. The now-infamous “phantom tunnel” was soon declared one of the biggest April Fool’s hoaxes of its time, fooling hundreds.
While the stunt briefly reignited interest, it ultimately marked the end of the tunnel dream. Plans were quietly abandoned, along with a proposed ferry crossing.
As for John Elliott, he moved on to other ventures…but the mystery remains: who was behind the hoax? Elliott never confirmed his involvement, and the truth was buried with him.
Nearly a century later, the story of the “Tunnel That Never Was” remains a fascinating glimpse into local ambition, ingenuity… and a prank that put Harwich firmly on the map.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Harwich Haven Authority Launches Project to Restore Saltmarsh at RSPB Nature Reserve and Boost Coastal Resilience
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) is pleased to announce the launch of the BUDS (Beneficial Use of Dredged Sediment) project – working with local conservationists on a pioneering initiative that will reuse dredged sediment from harbour maintenance to restore saltmarsh habitat and enhance coastal protection around the Haven.
Rather than disposing of dredged sediment at sea, BUDS will repurpose mud from Harwich harbour and distribute it in Copperas Bay, near Wrabness, to restore saltmarsh, stabilise shorelines, and support biodiversity, including native plants such as sea lavender and samphire, along with habitat for saltmarsh and estuarine wildlife.
“This project will safeguard the Haven’s vital navigation channel while turning routine dredging into a nature-positive opportunity,” said Harwich Haven Authority’s Harbour Engineer, Jim Warner.
“Maintaining the Haven’s navigation channel is essential to the national economy and supports thousands of local jobs, whilst ensuring the smooth operation of one of the UK’s busiest ports.”
“Through the BUDS initiative, we’re able to reuse the sediment from this work to help restore and protect the Haven’s vulnerable saltmarsh. This approach delivers long-term benefits for both local communities and the wildlife that depends on these coastal habitats.”
Saltmarsh is a rare and special habitat in the UK that teems with wildlife, but much has been lost due to sea level rise and change of land use. Dredged sediment will help to restore eroded saltmarsh which regularly floods with seawater and creates the unique habitat found there. In time, the restored saltmarsh will repopulate with small salt tolerant plants that help to catch more mud and silt, continually growing and expanding this special habitat.
Work will also benefit many species of bird, some of which are threatened, by providing habitat rich in food for overwintering wading birds including Black-tailed Godwits, Redshank, Turnstones, Curlew, Grey Plovers, Knot and Dunlin. Flocks of wildfowl including Wigeon, Teal, Pintail, Mallard, Shelduck and Dark-bellied Brent Goose will also benefit during winter months.
The saltmarsh that will be restored is sizeable at just over 76.5 hectares in size, equivalent to 107 football pitches.
Works at Copperas Bay is due to take place between 20 February and 20 March 2026. The programme will involve pumping of sediment by dredging contractor Boskalis Westminster, following the installation of temporary bunds and placement of coir rolls by construction contractor Amicus Civil Engineering to initially keep sediment in place, followed by vegetation and habitat restoration.
Rick Vonk, Site Manager at RSPB Stour Estuary said: “Re-using dredged sediment is a clever way of using a natural solution to solve the problem of saltmarsh loss. We look forward to seeing the results of the work with HHA, and how it will help wading and wildfowl birds thrive at RSPB Stour Estuary in the future.”
Dr Natalie Hicks, from the School of Life Sciences at the University of Essex, said: “University of Essex researchers are delighted to be involved in assessing the recovery of the saltmarsh following the addition of dredged sediment.”
“There is a real potential for this novel approach to enhance saltmarsh restoration and future proof our coastlines, particularly under rising sea levels due to climate change.
“Saltmarshes play a key role in supporting biodiversity, protecting our coasts and taking up and storing carbon, so this restoration and protection may prove pivotal in tackling climate change. This project demonstrates how industry, conservation organisations and academia can work together to protect and restore our coasts for the future.”
Theadora Sherriff, a Masters student at the University, together with colleagues Professor Graham Underwood, Dr Natalie Hicks and Dr Nicola Slee, will undertake an ambitious fieldwork campaign to monitor the saltmarsh, and the repopulation of saltmarsh plants, over the weeks and months follo

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: New Marine Biosecurity Plan launched to help protect the Stour and Orwell Estuaries
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A new Marine Biosecurity Plan has been launched to help protect the Stour and Orwell Estuaries from the growing threat of invasive non-native species.
The plan sets out good practice measures to reduce the risk of the introduction and spread of harmful species, which could cause serious damage to both marine animal and plant life. They also pose potentially significant economic impacts to ports, marine industries and recreational activities.
Both the Stour and Orwell Estuaries are designated as a Special Protection Area (SPA) for overwintering birds, a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Ramsar site for wetland habitats.
The plan has been led and funded by a partnership of Natural England, Harwich Haven Authority, Port of Ipswich (Associated British Ports), the Port of Felixstowe (Hutchison Ports) and Trinity House, and delivered by consultancy firm APEM.
Jenni Murphy, Environment Manager at Harwich Haven Authority, said:
“The Stour and Orwell Estuaries are vital for navigation, industry, recreation and the natural environment.
“This plan shows what can be achieved when organisations work together and share knowledge to better protect the Haven.
“Everyone who uses these waters has a role to play in effective marine biosecurity, and this plan provides clear, practical guidance to support that.”
The actions and guidance contained in the plan have been shaped through a series of local workshops involving a wide range of organisations, individuals and sectors operating across the estuaries, ensuring the measures are realistic, achievable and supported by those who use or have an interest in the Haven.
Alex Baker, Senior Officer – Marine, from Natural England’s West Anglia Area Team , said:
“The spread of invasive non-native species can cause significant harm on Marine Protected Areas such as the Stour and Orwell Estuaries Special Protection Area.
“Natural England is grateful to the partnership for the work that has gone into producing this biosecurity plan for the Stour and Orwell.
“We welcome the launch of the new plan and hope that it will provide a useful resource for stakeholders and users of the rivers wishing to avoid the harmful impacts of spreading invasives species into these habitats.’’
The Stour and Orwell Marine Biosecurity Plan is available to view and download from the Harwich Haven Authority website here:  https://hha.co.uk/marine-biosecurity/

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: HHA raises over £7,000 for Charity of the Year
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
The HHA team has celebrated an incredible year fundraising for our chosen charity of 2025, Home-Start Harwich.
Colleagues from across the business have played their part in raising money for the charity, raising an amazing £7,726 across multiple events and fundraisers.
Who are Home-Start Harwich?
Home-Start Harwich is a charity in the heart of our community making a genuine difference to the lives of children and their families locally.
It provides direction, training and guidance to parents and children through 1:1 parenting support, group sessions, workshops and play opportunities.
The charity has helped countless families in our town and surrounding villages since its formation in 1996.
We have supported them for several years now – and it has been our privilege to help them as our Charity of the Year.
What we did
Our colleagues raised money across 10 events over the year, from our annual Eurovision sweepstake to bakesales and a charity five-a-side football tournament which raised more than £1,100 alone.
The year ended on a high with our second-ever Ha’penny Pier Christmas tree lights switch-on, raising money for Home-Start Harwich alongside a night of carols, sea shanties and festive treats.
Almost all of those events were match funded by HHA, adding more than £1,000 to our annual total.
We have also provided funding to the charity’s Forest School and Outdoor Play and Stay services for several years – and will continue to do so.
What Home-Start Harwich said
Wendy Taylor, Manager at Home-Start Harwich, said: “We are so grateful to everyone at HHA for their continued support – having the support of local organisations is so important to charities like ourselves and highlights what a good community is all about.
“Their team have been out and about raising money for us all year, much of which will go to spreading some magic to families this Christmas.
“A lot of our funding comes through grants which are ringfenced to certain services, but the support from organisations like HHA are unrestricted, meaning the money they raise can go to support all the families we work with.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: New Chief Executive for Harwich Haven Authority

Harwich Haven Authority are pleased to announce that Jo North has been appointed as the organisation’s new Chief Executive, effective of Monday 1 June 2026.
She replaces outgoing CEO Sarah West, who left the business in December 2025.
Jo joins HHA from her current role as Director of Innovation at the Port of Tyne and will be relocating from the North East to Harwich area ahead of taking up her new position.
Current Interim Chief Executive, Jake Storey, will continue in his role until Jo starts with us. At that point, Jake will resume his previous role as Chief Financial Officer.
Jo brings a wealth of experience across innovation and sustainability, customer negotiations, stakeholder engagement, and digital and technology strategy. Her expertise also includes areas such as AI, cybersecurity, and connectivity.
On her appointment she said:
“I am delighted to be joining Harwich Haven Authority and am very much looking forward to working with colleagues across the organisation to support innovation, sustainability and long-term resilience, while continuing to deliver safe and reliable services for our customers and partners.
The Authority has a clear purpose and an exciting future and as a trust port, delivers real and positive impact for its local communities. I am excited to build on its strong reputation and to support its future ambitions.
I enjoyed my time at the Port of Tyne and thank my colleagues for their support in delivering a number of exciting initiatives which made a real difference to the region. I am grateful for their support as I start the next step in my career.”
Chair of the Harwich Haven Authority Board, Debbie Francis, added:
“In Jo, we believe we have identified the candidate who is the best fit for the Authority’s priorities in the period ahead and who will complement the strengths of the existing Executive team. Jo brings senior leadership experience from complex, safety-critical environments, a strong track record in stakeholder engagement and partnership working, and deep expertise in innovation, sustainability and long-term strategy within the port and transport sectors. Her approach aligns closely with the priorities we set for the role and the direction of travel for the Authority.”
Earlier in her career, Jo held senior leadership roles at East Coast Trains, including Deputy Managing Director and Customer Services Director and at Northern Rail where she was Commercial Director.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: 2026-01: Use of Exhaust Gas Cleaning Systems
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
In accordance with UK regulations as detailed below:
All exhaust gas cleaning systems (EGCS), (also referred to as scrubbers) used within Harwich Haven Authority’s statutory harbour limits must be fully functioning and certified as compliant with IMO standards.
Vessels operating hybrid scrubbers within Harwich Haven Authority’s statutory harbour limits must be used in closed loop mode.
All vessels discharging wastewater from open loop scrubbers must be able to demonstrate to the Harbour Master compliance with The Merchant Shipping (Prevention of Air Pollution from Ships) Regulations 2008 (Schedule 2A) as amended and section 2 of MSN 1819 (M&F) as amended as follows:
“2.1 The master of any ship must ensure that waste streams from the use of exhaust gas cleaning systems equipment are not discharged into any port, harbour or estuary unless it is thoroughly documented that the waste streams will have no adverse impact on the ecosystem of the port, harbour or estuary.”
“2.2 The master of any ship within United Kingdom waters that is to use an exhaust gas cleaning system shall provide documentation that demonstrates that waste streams discharged to the sea will have no adverse impact on the ecosystem of that port harbour or estuary”
Documentation should be provided to the Maritime & Coastguard Agency (MCA) via environment@mcga.gov.uk and to Harwich Haven Authority via marine.admin@hha.co.uk for consideration by the Harbour Master and Environment Manager at least two working days in advance of likely entry into Harwich Haven Authority’s jurisdiction.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: HHA to provide £40m in support to local communities
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) is setting its sights on generating record-breaking social value for the communities and environment in which it operates.
Responsible for the waters surrounding major ports like Felixstowe and Harwich, HHA is aiming to generate £40 million in social value by 2030. The announcement comes as the organisation finalises its calculations for social value output in 2025, which are on target to exceed 2024’s record of £5.1 million.
In total, HHA has delivered £13.3m in social value since 2022 – and is now looking to accelerate that progress and strengthen its commitment to achieving its long-term goal.
Linzi Jobber, Sustainability Manager at HHA, said:
“We have already made significant progress as the first trust port to put social value at the very heart of our operations. Now we’re setting our sights on something bigger. We want our work to have a positive, tangible impact on communities and the local environment, whether that’s investing in community projects, creating more jobs for local people, opening more apprenticeship positions or reducing our carbon footprint. This target is ambitious, but we are confident in our abilities to make a genuine difference and inspire others to do the same.”
HHA partners with the Social Value Portal, using its TOMs framework (Themes, Outcomes and Measures), to attribute monetary value to the activities it undertakes. This can include initiatives like employing local people and cutting carbon emissions. HHA targets five categories of social value – Jobs, Growth, Social, Environment and Innovation.
The two main areas it operates in, Tendring and East Suffolk, both have higher levels of deprivation than the East of England average of 17.8% at 42.7% and 20.5% respectively.
Highlights of their work so far include spending more than £1.3m in the local economy in 2024 alone, and creating 108 full-time jobs for local people in the same year.
It also reduced its Co2 emissions by more than 4,865 tonnes – worth £1.2m alone.
Helen Rudd, Strategy & Partnerships Director at HHA, added:
“The benefit of being a trust port  is that we reinvest all of our profits back into our local area. The results of our earlier Local Needs Analysis has shown us the places and communities that need our support the most – and we look forward to increasing our efforts to reach them year-on-year. Together, we want to ensure all those living in and around the haven feel the impacts of our work.”

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Harwich Haven Authority Begins Beneficial Use of Dredging (BUDs) Project at Levington to Restore Saltmarsh and Strengthen Natural Flood Defences
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) has begun an innovative project working with Suffolk Yacht Harbour, where dredged sediment from routine marina maintenance is being repurposed to help restore a rapidly eroding saltmarsh and enhance biodiversity along the River Orwell.
The Beneficial Use of Dredging (BUDs) programme has recently started at Levington, delivered on the ground by Amicus Civil Engineering and Suffolk Yacht Harbour, which will pump mud dredged from its moorings into the restoration area. The site, which is located along Levington Creek, has experienced steady erosion for decades. The carefully engineered placement of material, supported by the installation of coir bunds by Amicus Civil Engineering and funded by HHA, will help rebuild the saltmarsh platform, bolster natural flood defences, and create new habitat for a range of coastal wildlife.
The land is owned by Suffolk Yacht Harbour, with management of the adjacent nature reserve by Suffolk Wildlife Trust, which is strongly supportive of the scheme due to the ecological gains it is expected to deliver, particularly for overwintering waders such as redshank, dunlin, knot, black tailed godwit and golden plover.  Redshanks may even return to breed on the saltmarsh habitat in time if the habitat restoration enables some areas to remain above mean high water spring tides.
“ This work at Levington is a great example of how we can turn essential dredging operations into tangible environmental benefit,” said Jim Warner, Construction & Dredging Manager at Harwich Haven Authority. “By partnering with Suffolk Yacht Harbour, Suffolk Wildlife Trust and Amicus, we’re able to reuse locally dredged sediment to rebuild valuable saltmarsh habitat that has been disappearing for decades. This nature-based approach not only strengthens the shoreline and improves flood resilience but also creates important new opportunities for wildlife to thrive — especially the seabirds that depend on these fragile ecosystems.”
Suffolk Yacht Harbour’s Jonathan Dyke said
“We welcome the assistance of Harwich Haven Authority in providing additional infrastructure support to retain dredged silt over a wider area enabling the retention of more sediment which will accelerate the restoration of the saltmarsh.”
Suffolk Wildlife Trust’s South East Suffolk Sites Manager, Andrew Excell said
“Increases in the connectivity and height of the restored saltmarsh will have significant benefits for roosting wading bird and waterfowl species as they rest and recuperate energy in large flocks in relative safety during periods of high tide on the estuary. The estuary is internationally recognised for its importance in supporting many thousands of birds in winter months. Estuarine habitats like this in locations away from human disturbance are critical in helping survival of these species, especially in the colder winter months when they desperately need to conserve energy. Project works to help improve this type of dynamic habitat are much welcomed in such a strategically important wildlife-supporting location.”
The Levington works include the installation of coir bunds, controlled sediment placement and long-term habitat restoration. Monitoring of the site’s development will continue throughout 2025 and 2026, including assessments of sediment settlement, vegetation establishment and breeding habitat use by returning bird species.
In February 2026, another phase of the project will begin at Copperas Bay on the River Stour, in partnership with RSPB and Essex Wildlife Trust.
The BUDs project forms part of HHA’s wider commitment to pioneering sustainable dredging practices and delivering nature-positive outcomes across the Haven. By supporting saltmarsh recovery and promoting biodiversity, the Authority aims to demonstrate how operational port activities can coexist with – and actively enhance – the ecological health of the estuary.

2025 Essex rarities - photos & descriptions needed
Matt Turner
Fri, 23/10/2026 - 06:14
A request for help
One of the tasks of our records team is to put together the available supporting evidence for the rare species that have been seen around the county during the year, and then to forward that evidence to the ID Panel for review. Many of you who have been fortunate enough to find a rare species submit a description and photos through our web site, which is very helpful, and for some of the records photos can be lifted from WhatsApp groups. However, each year we find quite a number of records for rare species that have been submitted through our website, or on eBird or BirdTrack, but frustratingly we don’t have any further information to support them, which means that they can’t be reviewed by the ID Panel and can’t be included in the annual bird report.
Therefore, we are asking for your help to gather the required supporting evidence, either a photo or a description, for the ‘missing’ records. Please take a look at the table below and let us know if you have a photo or could write a description for any of the records listed. If so, we would be most grateful if you could submit it either via our website  here or by emailing the County Recorder at ebwsrecords@gmail.com
There are however two species that we have a more general request for. In 2025 there were a lot of records submitted for both Black Brant (77 records) and for Glossy Ibis (200 records); there was quite an influx of Glossy Ibis in 2025. With so many records from different locations for two species that tend to stay for a while, but to move around while they are here, it is hard to know exactly how many individual birds there were. Any photos, with dates, that you have for either Black Brant or Glossy Ibis that have not already been submitted would be very welcome - please email them to ebwsrecords@gmail.com . Knowing the dates that they were seen in particular locations will help to confirm how many birds there were.
Thanks in advance for your help

https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.title: Bird Sound Identification
https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.text:
Bird Sound Identification
Matt Turner
Mon, 28/09/2026 - 07:04
As part of the UEA Soundscapes Monitoring Project, researchers have been running approximately 60 recording devices across the UK for the past three years. The recordings collected have been processed through BirdNET, an automated bird sound identification tool. As part of this process, they need to assess how well BirdNET performs under different conditions, including different seasons (breeding and non-breeding) and times of day.
To do this, they are appealing for volunteers to manually validate a subset of BirdNET’s identifications. This involves listening to a random sample of audio clips and identifying which species are present. These will then be compared to the BirdNET output for that clip. An online platform has been developed to make this process as straightforward as possible and you can access it at  https://audiochecker.uea. ac.uk/
Every validated recording helps improve shared understanding of automated bird sound identification and strengthens the scientific value of the dataset. There is no expectation that you validate a large number of clips in one sitting; indeed, we would suggest that regularly returning to the programme for short bouts rather than listening to lots of clips in one go might be more effective.
Thank you for your help with this exciting project.

SWIFTS NEED OUR HELP!
One of the sights and sounds of summer, the Swift, has declined by 70%
since 1995 and is now designated as a 'Red List' species, meaning that
it is officially at risk of extinction in the UK.
This massive decline in the population is due to the following reasons:
the loss of essential roof nesting sites
the application of pesticides has significantly reduced vital insect food
extreme weather events are presenting further challenges
Save our Essex Swifts  was launched by long-standing Essex Birdwatching Society member, Richard Chew, in April 2026. You can follow them on Facebook by clicking here  and you can find their website at  saveouressexswifts.weebly. com
Are you interested in providing Swift nestboxes on your house?
The Essex Birdwatching Society has recently awarded a grant to Save
our Essex Swifts to begin the implementation of a vital project providing additional nest sites for Swifts in the County. This grant will enable the purchase of Swift nestboxes and call systems to supply to Essex residents for installation on their homes.
For further information on this vital project, or to make an application for some Swift nestboxes and a call system, please contact Richard by email at saveouressexswifts@gmail.com   or via the Save our Essex Swifts  website contact form or Facebook DM.

https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.title: Accessing EBwS Records
https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.text:
Accessing EBwS Records
Matt Turner
Thu, 17/09/2026 - 07:41
EBwS is the natural home of bird recording in Essex and has been since 1949. Maintaining the bird records for the county and making them available to interested parties, such as local authorities, the scientific community, environmental consultants and the general public is therefore a key part of what we do.  The records that we collect through this website and the records that we collate from other sources are made available in a number of different ways:
Recent Sightings can be seen on our Bird Reports page. This list is compiled from records submitted directly to our website.
We publish an annual Essex Bird Report (EBR) for the county. Copies of the EBR are sent to all EBwS members free of charge. It is compiled from the consolidated data received from a range of difference sources including this website, spreadsheets submitted from members directly to the County Recorder, and bird recording platforms such as BirdTrack and eBird . Copies of the EBR that are more than 3 years old are available for download in PDF format from the publications section of this website.
We share our records annually with the Essex Field Club (EFC). The EFC holds all natural history records for Essex which are received from the county recorders for all of the various taxa, such as moths and butterflies, amphibians, invertebrates, etc. The EFC makes that data available to local authorities and environmental consultants primarily for when they are conducting environmental impact assessments and similar studies.
Anyone who wishes to obtain the data for a particular location and/or species should contact the EFC via their website  and make a request through their Data Search Service .

https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.text:
Autumn 2026 Bird Photography Competition
Matt Turner
Wed, 16/09/2026 - 07:03
The EBwS Autumn 2026 Bird Photography Competition is now open for entries. The rules are as follows:
Photographs must be wild bird related and taken in Essex between 1st September 2026 and 30th November 2026.
Participants can submit a maximum of three photographs (all separate species) and the competition is open to all (you don't have to be a member to enter). Please note, if you submit multiple entries we will accept the first three photos you send in.
Photographs must be submitted via email to  ebwsphotos@gmail.com . All entries received will be acknowledged with an autoreply message. The closing date for entries is Monday 30th November at 9pm - photos received after this time will not be accepted.
A panel of judges will select their favourite photos to be entered into the public vote to find a winner.* The winner will be announced during December's 'Birds of Essex' LIVE on YouTube. In the event of a tie, the judges decision will be final.
Entries may be published in our 'Essex Birding' journal, credit will be given to the photographer who retains copyright.**
Please remember, the bird's welfare is of utmost importance. Always keep your distance and never disturb birds or wildlife when taking photographs. Please note that photographs of  schedule one birds  (click for list of species) on a nest or feeding young will not be accepted for entry.
All entries are anonymous until the results have been announced - even the judges don't know the photographer's names until that point! Therefore, and in order to keep the fun spirit of the competition, we request that anyone who makes it through to the voting stages refrains from publicising their entry on social media platforms and asking for people to vote for them. We reserve the right to withdraw any photo that we feel has not been entered within the fun and friendly spirit of this competition. Thank you.
All entries will be considered and can be taken with a camera, phone or digi/phone-scoped. The winner will receive a framed copy of their photograph along with a certificate. A short video featuring all entries will be shown during 'Birds of Essex' in December and will also be uploaded to the EBwS YouTube channel**.
We're looking forward to receiving your photos - good luck!
*EBwS reserve the right to use the winning photograph to advertise future competitions, subject to permission. Credit will be given to the photographer who retains copyright.
**If you don't wish your photos to be considered for publication or featured in the video please let us know when you submit them.

https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.title: Photo Comp Voting 'Fair Play'
https://www.ebws.org.uk/rss.xml.text:
Photo Comp Voting 'Fair Play'
Matt Turner
Wed, 09/09/2026 - 17:37
We launched the bird photography competition a few years ago and it has proved to be increasingly popular as time has passed. The competition was always intended to be fun, with entrants remaining anonymous and the public choosing their favourite photos to proceed through the various tournament style knockout stages. It takes a lot of work in the background to run the competition, but we always enjoy doing so as we never know which photograph is going to win, and the results as the competition progresses always throw up a few surprises.
Therefore, we are sending this message to ask everyone who enters the competition to please do so with the same ethos. We ask everyone to please refrain from using social media accounts to appeal for votes. If we can keep all entries anonymous then the voting is a true reflection of people's thoughts, and the final results will be unbiased and genuine. The rules for the next competition will be changed slightly to reflect this, and ultimately if biased voting continues we will either reserve the right to withdraw photos from the competition at any stage, or we'll stop running it altogether which we don't want to do.
We hope you understand us sending out this message, and we thank everyone who has entered past and present competitions and all those who've taken the time to vote.

https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.title: Report: Southend 2-3 Boreham Wood
https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.text:
Fixtures
Southend United Vs. Boreham Wood - Fri, Nov 20th 2026, 19:45
Despite an improved second-half performance, three first-half goals from Boreham Wood proved the difference at Roots Hall, with Southend United losing 3-2 to the league leaders.
The visitors raced into a 3-0 lead by half-time thanks to a flurry of goals in the space of 14 minutes.
Oliver Bainbridge opened the scoring, drilling past Joe Duncan at his near post after being threaded through by Regan Booty.
The midfielder then set up Boreham Wood’s second as well, floating in a cross to the far post where Ben Whitfield slid in.
Former Shrimper, Zak Brunt added a third just past the half-hour mark from close range after being picked out by Whitfield.
Kieron Dyer’s substitutes made a difference in the second half, and two of them linked up to bring Blues back into the game, with Tyreece Simpson heading in Maxwell McKnight’s cross.
Instantly afterwards, the Shrimpers scored another with debutant Rico Richards’ drilled effort going in off the foot of the post.
Kick-Off
The away side had the first attempt of the game after just three minutes when Tylor Golden picked Kyle McAdam’s pocket and found Whitfield, whose shot from 20 yards went wide.
Just before the quarter of an hour mark, the Wood again threatened, and this time Joe Duncan had to make an excellent save to keep the game goalless.
Regan Booty’s free kick from 25 yards was whipped over the wall and forced a fine diving save from Duncan to push away. The danger wasn't yet clear though, with a backheel from Golden having to be headed off the line by McAdam.
The corner that then followed led to another scare with Charlie O’Connell getting free at the back post, but Wales international Duncan was again on hand to make a save.
After 19 minutes, Blues were finally breached with Bainbridge scoring his first goal of the campaign.
Booty threaded a clever pass into the left back, who had ghosted in behind the Shrimpers defence, and he cut inside onto his right foot and drilled a low effort past Duncan and into the bottom near corner.
Ten minutes later, Duncan again had to make another impressive stop, scrambling across his goal line to deny Matt Rush from close range after Tarryn Allarakhia had played a low ball across the six-yard box.
However, the danger hadn’t passed, with the visitors keeping possession and recycling play to double their lead.
Booty got his second assist of the evening as he floated a cross towards the far post where Whitfield was on hand to slide in and make it 2-0.
Four minutes later, the Wood’s lead was extended to three with former Shrimper Brunt returning to Roots Hall with a goal.
He initially played a ball over the top that released Whitfield in behind; the Barrow loanee was forced wide by Duncan, but he spotted the run of Brunt into the box and teed up his fellow midfielder, who slotted in a simple finish from six yards out.
Half-Time: Southend United 0-3 Boreham Wood
The Shrimpers made a triple substitution at half-time and, after 65 minutes, two of those who were introduced linked up to pull one back for Blues.
McKnight was found by Omochere, and he delivered a first-time cross which picked out Simpson whose downward header snuck under Ted Curd and in.
A second assist in Southend colours for McKnight and a third goal for Simpson, who both got goal contributions against Aldershot Town on Saturday.
This sparked some belief in the Shrimpers, and two minutes later another substitute got his name on the scoresheet – Richards on his debut.
Omochere was again involved; after receiving the ball from Dan Cox, the Bristol Rovers loanee played a pass on the turn to Richards, who let it run across his body before drilling a shot back across goal that went in off the foot of the post.
However, despite this, the Shrimpers were unable to score an equaliser and fell to a fourth defeat of the season.
Full-Time: Southend United 2-3 Boreham Wood
We return to action in midweek with a trip to Gloucestershire

https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.text:
Friday night football returns to Roots Hall as Southend United face their toughest test of the season so far as the unbeaten league leaders Boreham Wood travel to South Essex.
The Shrimpers returned to winning ways last weekend with a 2-1 comeback against Aldershot Town and will be looking to record back-to-back home wins for the first time since September.
THE VISITORS
The Enterprise National League leaders, Boreham Wood, have bounced back superbly from last season’s promotion final defeat to enjoy a faultless start to this campaign.
Most of last season’s squad has stuck around, which, along with a few new faces, has set the groundwork for another strong campaign.
They did, however, lose exciting playmaker Abdul Abdulmalik to Swedish first division side Djurgårdens for a National League record sale of £1.5 million.
Despite the departure of the 18-goal midfielder in August, the Wood are on course to enjoy an even better season this time around.
They are still unbeaten this term, with their last league defeat in the regular season coming in a 4-1 drubbing at Solihull Moors on Easter Monday.
This season got off to a slightly frustrating start, conceding in the 12 th minute of stoppage time to draw 3-3 at home to Tamworth.
This was then followed by a five-game winning run before being held to a draw by Eastleigh in mid-September.
After losing 3-0 to Wigan Athletic in the Emirates FA Cup a fortnight ago, the Wood almost lost their unbeaten league record last weekend, but Lewis Richardson rescued a point against Yeovil Town with ten minutes to play; they were also aided by a late Yeovil penalty miss in the 84 th minute.
WHEN WE’VE MET BEFORE
The Shrimpers have only won one of our last five contests with Boreham Wood – a 4-2 victory at Roots Hall on Easter Monday 2024 which pushed the Wood closer to relegation to the sixth tier.
Last season, Josh Walker came off the bench to score his first goal since the opening day to rescue a point at Meadow Park, whilst at Roots Hall, former Shrimper Matt Rush was on target in a 2-0 defeat.
In total, Blues have won four of the six meetings the two sides have had at Roots Hall, with the first coming in the FA Cup in 1973/74.
PLAYED FOR BOTH
Three former Shrimpers now ply their trade with the Wood.
Matt Rush and Zak Brunt, who have the most goals and assists in the division respectively, and defender Ollie Kensdale.
In the Southend ranks, Ben Goodliffe previously represented Boreham Wood.
FROM THE HEAD COACH
The gaffer is urging for a fast start from his side and for the 9,400 plus Shrimpers to get behind the team under the lights.
"We've got to be full of intensity and purpose and if we do that, with our crowd, it can make Boreham Wood very uncomfortable."

Southend United Vs. Oxford City - Wed, Nov 18th 2026, 14:00
Southend United Under-19s returned to winning ways with a 5-1 National League U19 Alliance Academy South Division victory over Oxford City at Garon Park.
Nikolay Zlatev put the Shrimpers in front after just three minutes and, despite failing to capitalise on further first-half chances, Thomas Telford, Daniel Banjoko and Matthew Blake scored after the interval, adding to an own goal from City defender Louie Stowell, as Danny Heath’s side won for the first time in four league outings.
“I thought the boys were outstanding,” declared the U19s Head Coach. “We were the better team. We came in at half-time and we were only 1-0 up, but if we’d come in five or six up, there couldn’t have been any complaints.”
“We could have been a bit more ruthless with our finishing, but they also defended really well and the goalkeeper made some good saves, and they put in some good blocks to stop us scoring goals, so I was really pleased,” he added.
Heath made three changes to the team that had started the 4-2 defeat at Slough Town, which included welcoming back left-back Mitchell Ward from injury. He replaced Lucas Johnson, with Daniel Dempsey coming in for Olly Hyams and Zlatev appearing instead of Josh Colyer.

Ward’s corner from the right took a touch off a defender and, from the next corner, delivered from the opposite flank by Brandon Dadson, Southend took the lead. The ball was only cleared as far as Zlatev eight yards from goal, and he stroked it through a crowded area to net his fourth Shrimpers goal of the campaign.
Within a few further minutes it could have been 2-0, but Blake’s ferocious strike from the edge of the penalty box was pushed out by City goalkeeper Dan Starkey, and the custodian also tipped away Onuh’s teasing right-wing delivery with the match still in its infancy.
In the 12th minute, Blake brought down Telford’s cross-field pass and sent a skidding shot into the gloves of Starkey from 20 yards out, and the in-form front-man was denied once again by the visiting goalkeeper just seconds later after planting a powerful downward header goalwards from another Onuh cross.
Southend continued to dominate, and only quick-thinking by Starkey stopped Zlatev from latching onto Blake’s through-ball after a quarter-of-an-hour. It wasn’t until the 19th minute that Oxford threatened for the first time as Jack Green inadvertently blocked Georgios Tzengko’s goalbound attempt.
Blake, who entered the match having scored six times in his previous four U19s appearances, should have extended that sequence on the half-hour, but his one-on-one finish from Telford’s pass clipped the top of the crossbar.

https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.title: Ladies: Southend United 6-0 Rayleigh
https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.text:
Southend United progressed to the Third Round of the BBC Essex Women's Cup with a 6-0 victory over Rayleigh in new Head Coach Adam Walker's first match in charge.
Niamh Carpenter’s first goal for the Shrimpers put the hosts in front after just eight minutes at Garon Park, and Tilly Jones doubled the advantage four minutes later. However, despite a four-tier gap in the two teams’ league positions, Rayleigh fought hard and limited the damage to two goals at the interval.
Jones made it 3-0 eleven minutes into the second half before completing her hat-trick in the 64th minute. Substitute Hannah Stone added the fifth nine minutes later before Jones netted her fourth of the afternoon to round out the scoring with thirteen minutes remaining.
Forward Abbey Dell served a one-match suspension after accumulating her fifth yellow card of the season in last week’s 1-0 win at Wormley Rovers, but goalkeeper Libby Mason was available, enabling Lauren Johnson to return to more familiar defensive duties.
Abbie Rex made her 150th competitive appearance in Southend United colours, with 134 games for the senior side and 16 at youth level over the past decade, whilst Emily Pert was named amongst the substitutes after missing 26 months through injury.
It was apparent from the early exchanges that Jones would be a threat to Rayleigh from the left-hand side, and in the sixth minute she dragged a left-footed shot narrowly wide from 15 yards out. Sixty seconds later, her attempted finish from close-range was forced out for a corner.
It was from the ensuing Sophie Stack flag-kick that Southend would take the lead. With the visitors desperately attempting to clear the danger, Darcy Drewitt laid the ball off to  Carpenter , positioned 25 yards from goal, and her fierce shot took a slight deflection on its way past Amber Andrews in the Rayleigh goal.
Drewitt cushioned the ball into the path of Jones three minutes later, but her shot was pushed out by Andrews at the near post. There was, however, nothing the goalkeeper could do to prevent the former Brentwood Town youngster from scoring a minute later as a defensive misjudgement led to  Jones  lashing into an empty net.
Jones could have made it three in the 13th minute as she fired into the side-netting from the right-hand apex of the six-yard box, and less than a quarter-of-an-hour had been played when Maizie Kelly directed her shot over following a measured pass from Stack.
After that initial flurry, the Shrimpers began to find it more difficult to break down a resolute Rayleigh defence, although the away team were indebted to Andrews on 20 minutes after Johnson strode into midfield before picking out Drewitt with her pass and the custodian dived bravely at her feet to save.
Andrews was positioned immaculately to deny Kelly at the near post on the half-hour after the Southend forward had flicked the ball up and hooked it over her right shoulder, whilst Jodie Murphy made an important challenge in the penalty area in the 37th minute to poke the ball away from a Rayleigh attacker.
The opening period ended with further frustration for the Shrimpers as Andrews again thwarted Jones following a Hannah Warner pass in the first minute of stoppage time before Drewitt whipped a 25-yard free-kick narrowly wide of the left-hand upright.
Despite holding a two-goal lead, Southend will have entered the second half intent to tidy up some of their play and show a more clinical nature in front of goal, and Walker made three changes as Reyes Humbles, Katie Burbridge and Stone came on for Carpenter, Murphy and Issy Boyd.
Within a minute of the restart Drewitt had nodded off-target from a Burbridge free-kick and, although Suzie Carter sent a 20-yard effort wide with the outside of her right foot for Rayleigh, Kelly went close again at the opposite end as Andrews gathered another attempt from Drewitt’s diagonal pass.
Southend finally scored their third goal in the 56th minute following more good work from the industrious Warner

https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.title: Report: Southend 2-1 Aldershot Town
https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.text:
Fixtures
Southend United Vs. Aldershot Town - Sat, Nov 14th 2026, 15:00
Southend United came from behind win 2-1 and earn an important three points against Aldershot Town.
Anisius Lewis had put the Shots ahead after six minutes, but a red card for dangerous play by John Gilbert proved to be pivotal, as the Shrimpers moved into the ascendency.
Kyle McAdam’s header and Tyreece Simpson’s left-footed strike flipped the scoreline, before Southend saw out the game to come away with a well-fought victory.
The Shrimpers made four changes to the XI who fell to defeat at Wealdstone, headlined by a starting debut for former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford full-back Maxwell McKnight who replaced the suspended Vontae Daley-Campbell.
The other enforced changed was Jack Sims’ return between the sticks following Joe Duncan’s call-up to the Wales senior squad, while Dan Cox and Sahid Kamara started in place of Ash Palmer and Oli Coker respectively.
Kick-off
The Shots took the lead early when Lewis escaped in behind the Shrimpers defence, and with Sims caught in no-man’s land, the striker lofted the ball over his head and into the unguarded net.
The game remained cagey in the first quarter of an hour, before Darren Oldaker’s shot drew a Shrimpers corner, and Ben Goodliffe nearly headed in at the back post, but for the intervention of Michael Stickland who got a touch with his own head to send it over the bar.
An almost identical opportunity followed in the 22nd minute, with Goodliffe and Strickland battling for the ball. It appeared as though it was the Shots defender who nodded narrowly wide of the post, but the referee awarded a goal-kick.
After another corner was half-cleared, Hartigan lofted the second ball into the box, and Leon Chambers-Parillon rose highest to nod at goal, only for Nick Hayes to catch.
Aldershot’s first entry into the penalty area since their opener then saw them reduced to 10 players, as Gilbert recklessly charged through Sims with a high boot, leaving the referee with no choice but to send him off.
The Shots briefly went down to nine players after Hayes required treatment, and after working the ball across the final third, Oldaker had space to shoot through a crowd of bodies. The effort deceived Hayes, but thundered off the bottom of the post before the visitors cleared their lines.
When Promise Omochere received the ball to feet from Kamara, he backed into and rolled his marker in trademark fashion before firing an effort towards goal, but on this occasion it was dragged wide of the far post.
The next opportunity came from a counter attack started from Kyle McAdam retrieving the ball next to his defensive corner flag. The Shrimpers switched play to the right flank where Kamara took up the loose ball and ghosted in-field, before his left-footed shot was guided straight at Hayes from 20 yards.
Omari Patrick was next to test Hayes with a 20-yard effort of his own, and this time the Shots custodian couldn’t hold the effort, but Kamara’s squared pass on the rebound was cut out and cleared.
As the half ticked into added time, another turn and shot from Omochere and a distance effort from Chambers-Parillon both missed the target, and ultimately meant the Shrimpers headed into the break a goal down.
Half-Time: Southend United 0-1 Aldershot Town
The Shrimpers changed shape at the break and brough Tyreece Simpson on for Kamara to move to two up front, and immediately the Shrimpers piled on the pressure. First Patrick’s curled shot thundered off the bar after looping over Hayes, before Omochere’s improvised volley also clipped the woodwork.
Another dangerous delivery from McKnight yielded another opportunity for Omochere, but this time his effort drifted agonisingly over the bar.
There was a heart in mouth moment as Lewis escaped Hartigan on the right wing and charged into the penalty area, but his composure let him down as he side-footed the ball tamely wide of the near post.
