https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.title: Maxwell McKnight Joins The Shrimpers
https://www.southendunited.co.uk/rss.xml.text:
Southend United are delighted to announce the signing of Maxwell McKnight on a one-year deal with a Club option for a second.
The versatile defender, who can play on either side of the defence and is known for his turn of speed, has spent time in the Tottenham Hotspur academy and has also featured for Brentford B across the last few years.
The 22-year-old has racked up almost 100 appearances for Spurs Youth and has even featured in the UEFA Youth League against Olympic Marseille, Sporting Lisbon and Eintracht Frankfurt.
“I’m really happy, it’s really good to get it over the line and done and I can’t wait to get started,” said McKnight, who is also looking forward to running out at Roots Hall this afternoon.
“It will be a great experience. To play in front of the fans and to represent a big club like this, it’s huge.”
Born in Colchester, the defender joined the Tottenham Hotspur Academy aged 11 before going on to regularly feature for their Youth teams and earning 45 appearances with 11 goal contributions in the U18 Premier League.
McKnight made his debut for Spurs Under-21s in September 2022 before going on a UEFA Youth League campaign that involved a 3-0 win over Olympic Marseille.
The defender then signed his first professional contract with the club in April the following year at 18 years old. He then spent a couple of seasons in the Premier League 2, including winning the League in 2023/24.
He went on to join Brentford B in September 2025 on a one-year deal, providing an assist in the Bees’ 2-1 win over AFC Wimbledon in pre-season and making 5 appearances in the Premier League Cup.
“I’m delighted to welcome Max to the Club,” said Head Coach Kieron Dyer. “He’s a very versatile defender who can be an overlapping full back or one who inverts and helps dominate inside the game.
“He is very physically fit and is someone who can come straight into the team."
Welcome to the Club, Max!

https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Match Report: Telford United 1-1 Chelmsford City (Telford win 6-5 on penalties)
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
Chelmsford City’s FA Trophy run ended on penalties at AFC Telford United, after a 1-1 draw in which Green’s long-range strike was cancelled out by Cawthorne before half-time, and neither side could find a winner in an end-to-end second half.
Mark Cooper’s side travelled to Shropshire to begin their FA Trophy campaign. City arrived eighth in the National League South, with just one league defeat in their opening 16, and off a 2-1 home win over Farnborough and a 2-2 draw with Ebbsfleet United. Telford, 11th in the National League North, were unbeaten in their last five league games. There was no replay or extra time, so a draw meant penalties.
City made no changes to the starting line-up, but it was also the day that Ben Worman returned to the club on a short-term loan from National League side Solihull Moors.
City started brightly. Barham got the ball into the box from the right, almost giving Odegah a header on goal. On 5 minutes Clarke passed to Green, who sent the ball into the box from the left, but nobody was there. City won a free kick soon after, taken by Green, but it fell comfortably into the keeper’s hands. Barham made another great run down the right on 10, but again nobody was there to meet him. Telford had their first moment on 12, with good work on the left, but their ball into the box found nobody, and Ralph luckily chested it back to Marriott.
City took the lead on 20 minutes. A Barham free kick was cleared by Telford’s defence, but Green took a shot from 40 yards out and scored an absolute screamer, hitting the post before dropping into the net. 1-0 to City.
Telford then started to keep the ball around our box, until a foul on Miley by Moult on 29 relieved the pressure. Marriott made a fantastic diving save on 32 as Walker had a shot on goal from the left. City’s defence kept Telford out of the box, and Clarke made a great tackle and had a shot from the halfway line, but it had too much power and swayed to the left.
Telford equalised on 35 minutes. Ralph headed a corner away, but the ball fell back to Telford and Cawthorne found the back of the net to make it 1-1. On 40 minutes Cranston pulled down Barham on the left, giving City a free kick, taken by Green, but the Telford defence headed it away. On 45 Odegah did brilliantly to get away from Cawthorne down the left and, bearing down on goal with Barham open in the box, opted to shoot, but his effort was blocked.
At half-time Crowther replaced Green, who sustained an injury from an earlier tackle in the first half.
On 48 minutes City gave away a free kick when Olopade took down a Telford player, but fortunately it went just wide on the right. Odegah was booked on 50 and gave away another free kick, with the ball falling into the City box and being cleared by Crowther. Telford looked dangerous on 52 as a ball was launched in from the left, but Ralph headed it away for a corner. It landed in the path of Clarke, who drove the ball all the way to Telford’s box and had a shot that went just wide.
Olopade gave away another free kick on 55, which was launched into the box. A Telford player got a head on it, but Marriott saved brilliantly. Olopade was booked, and on 57 minutes Worman replaced him.
Benning was booked after taking down Odegah twice in twenty seconds, which gave City a free kick. Clarke took it and, after a battle in the box, the ball fell to Tompkins, who put it in the net, but the referee called it back for a foul on a Telford player.
On 61 minutes Marriott launched the ball out for Barham and Odegah, who linked up well, and Barham had a chance on goal, but it was blocked by Hall. Clarke, Odegah and Egbo linked up well on 63 and Egbo launched the ball in from the right, but it went wide. Ralph gave away a free kick on 64, which just hit the side-netting on the right.
On 69 minutes Barbrook played Barham down the left, who got a cross into the box for Odegah to have a shot, but the Telford defence blocked well. Marriott made another fantastic save on 75,

https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Welcome to City Ben Worman!
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
We are delighted to announce the signing of Midfielder Ben Worman from National League side Solihull Moors on a short-term loan deal.
The 25-year-old arrives at the Dunmow Group Community Stadium with plenty of experience having previously represented Cambridge United, Gateshead, Cork City and Weymouth.
The midfielder helps to give us legs in the middle of the park while also providing creativity to the side!
Worman began his career at Cambridge United and is still the youngster ever player to put on a U’s shirt, at 16 years old in 2017. Two years later his first loan spell actually came at Chelmsford City. Unfortunately he did not feature in a league game.
Following his departure from Cambridge United in 2023, Worman joined League of Ireland Premier Division side Cork City before returning to England in January 2024 to sign for National League side Gateshead.
The midfielder enjoyed a successful spell with the Heed, making 78 appearances across all competitions and helping the club lift the Isuzu FA Trophy at Wembley in 2024. Worman started the final against Solihull Moors and went on to make 52 appearances during the 2024/25 campaign.
His performances earned him a move to Solihull Moors in the summer of 2025, where he continued to gain valuable National League experience throughout the 2025/26 season.
Worman now returns to Chelmsford City, having previously joined the Clarets on loan from Cambridge United in November 2019, looking to bring his experience and quality to Mark Cooper’s midfield as City continue their Enterprise National League South campaign.
Welcome back to Chelmsford City, Ben!

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: BRENTWOOD TOWN FC EXTENDS LONG-STANDING PARTNERSHIP WITH SHEPHERD NEAME IN NEW THREE-YEAR DEAL
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town Football Club is delighted to announce the extension of its long-standing partnership with Shepherd Neame, with both parties agreeing to a new three-year sponsorship deal.
The agreement represents another significant chapter in a relationship that has continued to benefit both organisations, strengthening the connection between the club and one of the UK’s most established brewing and pub businesses.
Shepherd Neame has been a valued partner of Brentwood Town FC for a number of years, playing an important role in supporting the club and its ongoing development, both on and off the pitch.
The new agreement will see the partnership continue for a further three years, building on the foundations already established and creating further opportunities for both organisations to work together.
Founded in 1698, Shepherd Neame is Britain’s oldest brewer, with a rich heritage spanning more than 325 years. Based in Faversham, Kent, the independent family business is renowned for producing a wide range of award-winning beers, alongside operating 280 pubs across London and the South East.
With a shared appreciation for tradition, community and bringing people together, the continued relationship reflects the importance of strong partnerships and the positive impact they can have.
Brentwood Town FC Chairman, Jez Dickinson, said:
“Shepherd Neame have been fantastic supporters of our football club for a number of years, and we’re delighted to extend this partnership for a further three years. We really value their continued support and look forward to building on our relationship together.”
Dougie Dick, Business Development Manager at Shepherd Neame, added:
“We are delighted to continue our partnership with Brentwood Town and look forward to more success on and off the field.”
Brentwood Town FC would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Dougie and everyone at Shepherd Neame for their continued support and commitment to the club.
We look forward to working together over the next three years and continuing what has already been a hugely positive partnership.
Our Club. Your Town. Brentwood Town.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Ramsgate punish Brentwood with three-goal first-half display
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town suffered defeat at the Brentwood Arena on Saturday afternoon, as Ramsgate capitalised on a clinical first-half performance to secure all three points.
The visitors took an early lead through Raphe Brown before Alfie Paxman doubled their advantage with a strike from the edge of the area. Top scorer Callum Jones then added a third before the interval, leaving the Blues with a mountain to climb after the break.
Brentwood showed plenty of attacking intent throughout, creating opportunities at both ends of the contest, but were unable to find a breakthrough against a resolute Ramsgate defence. Aiden Prall also produced an important second-half penalty save to deny Paxman a second goal, although the visitors ultimately did enough to see out their three-goal advantage.
Brett Munyard made five changes to the starting XI from the previous weekend’s trip to Three Bridges. Jayden Gipson and Tommy Davis formed the central defensive partnership, while Malachi Linton and Freddie Sears were introduced into the frontline. Ollie Peters also made his first appearance in a Blues shirt in midfield.
Ramsgate made a flying start and found themselves ahead inside the opening two minutes. A corner delivered by Paxman was met by Billy Munday, whose header was initially kept out by a stretching save from Prall. However, Brown reacted quickest to the rebound, looping his header over the goalkeeper and into the net.
The Blues looked to respond quickly, with Sears seeing his half-volley inside the area take a deflection before being gathered by Rams goalkeeper Jonny Henly.
A spell of patient build-up play from Brentwood almost produced an equaliser moments later. Gipson advanced through midfield before unleashing a strike from distance, which narrowly missed the target and whistled past the left-hand post.
The hosts continued to enjoy possession and looked to work their way back into the contest. Linton produced one of their best opportunities of the opening period after breaking through the middle on the counter-attack, before unleashing a long-range effort that forced Henly into a low save.
However, it was Ramsgate who found the net again. Paxman picked up possession on the edge of the area and struck towards goal, with his effort getting beyond Prall and crossing the line to double the visitors’ advantage.
Brentwood almost responded immediately as Linton fizzed a dangerous delivery across the face of goal, but Sears was unable to keep his effort down, firing over the crossbar.
The visitors then added a third before the interval. Paxman produced a perfectly weighted pass to pick out Jones, who made no mistake in finding the far corner to leave the Blues facing a three-goal deficit at the break.
Brentwood emerged with renewed intent after the restart and looked to find a route back into the game. An in-swinging corner from Max Hudson was met by Gipson, whose header flashed across goal, before Cerulli sent a free-kick over the crossbar.
Just before the hour mark, Ramsgate were handed the opportunity to extend their lead further when Benedict Bioletti was brought down inside the penalty area.
Paxman stepped up to take the resulting spot-kick, but Prall produced an excellent diving save to his left to deny the midfielder and keep the scoreline at 3-0.
The visitors continued to pose a threat from set-pieces, with another dangerous delivery from Paxman finding Munday from a centrally positioned free-kick. His header, however, drifted narrowly wide.
The Blues continued to push in search of a consolation goal during the closing stages, with substitute Bradley Sach seeing a close-range header collected by Henly.
Wyan Reid also tested the Ramsgate goalkeeper with a low, driven effort, but Henly was equal to it as the visitors successfully defended their advantage to take all three points back to Kent.
Brentwood Town are back in action on Tuesday night, as they travel to Burgess Hill Town in the Isthmian League Premier Division.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Brentwood Town FC Announces Partnership with Grassroots Suicide Prevention
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town Football Club is proud to announce a new charity partnership with Grassroots Suicide Prevention as part of November being Men’s Health Month, strengthening the club’s commitment to supporting the wellbeing of its players, supporters and wider community.
The partnership aims to use the power and reach of football to encourage conversations around men’s mental health, raise awareness of suicide prevention and help break down the stigma that can often prevent people from speaking openly about how they are feeling.
Men’s mental health remains an important issue, and football clubs have a unique opportunity to bring people together, create supportive and safe environments and remind individuals that they are never alone.
The statistics surrounding suicide highlight just how important this work is. According to our new partner, approximately 115 people die by suicide every week in the UK, while research suggests that one in four people will experience suicidal thoughts at some point during their lifetime.
Suicide is also the leading cause of death among people under the age of 35. These figures underline the importance of breaking down stigma, encouraging open conversations and making sure people know that support is available.
It is a reminder that a simple conversation, asking someone how they really are or taking the time to listen could make a life-changing difference.
As part of the partnership, we will be hosting a dedicated fundraising fixture against Ramsgate on Saturday 14 November, as our closest home fixture to International Men’s Day. The match provides an opportunity to raise funds for Grassroots Suicide Prevention and awareness for men’s mental health.
The club is encouraging supporters, players and the wider community to get behind the fixture and help make a difference to an issue that affects so many people.
Grassroots Suicide Prevention is dedicated to equipping people with the knowledge and confidence to help prevent suicide, providing education and support to create communities where people feel able to talk and seek help when they need it.
A key resource developed by Grassroots Suicide Prevention is its Stay Alive app, a free and confidential suicide prevention tool designed to support people experiencing suicidal thoughts, as well as those worried about someone else.
The app provides a range of practical resources, including personalised safety plans, access to local and national support services, guidance on recognising warning signs and advice on how to support someone who may be struggling. It also features a ‘LifeBox’, allowing users to save meaningful photos, videos and memories, alongside wellness tools and personal reminders of their reasons for living.
Available on both Apple and Android devices, Stay Alive provides an accessible resource that can help people find support when they need it most.
· The app is completely free, with no advertising or paid features.
· 1 million+ downloads since its launch in 2014.
· Available in 22 languages.
Through this partnership, Brentwood Town Football Club hopes to reinforce an important message: It’s okay to talk, it’s okay to ask for help, and no one should ever feel they have to face things alone.
Football is a common ground which brings communities together. Let’s use that same sense of togetherness to make sure nobody feels they have to face their struggles alone.
Together, we can all help make a difference.

cinch has become one of the UK’s leading online car retailers, helping customers buy quality used and nearly new cars entirely online, while also establishing a strong reputation for supporting sport through a number of high-profile partnerships.

Following two consecutive promotions, there is tremendous momentum behind the team, and support from a nationally recognised brand such as cinch will help us continue building the foundations for future success. We look forward to developing a strong relationship over the coming season.”

At cinch, we’re passionate about supporting the communities we serve, and we’re looking forward to working with Brentwood Town throughout the 2026/27 season. We wish the players, coaches and everyone involved with the club every success for the year ahead.”

https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.title: Rest in Peace Lloyd Scott MBE
https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.text:
Dagenham & Redbridge Football Club is saddened to learn of the passing of former player Lloyd Scott MBE.
Lloyd enjoyed a career in football as a goalkeeper, representing Leyton Orient, Watford and Blackpool before going on to play for Dagenham and Redbridge Forest.
Away from football, Lloyd became nationally recognised for his extraordinary charity fundraising efforts, raising more than £5 million for charitable causes over the course of three decades.
Having been diagnosed with leukaemia in 1987 while working as a firefighter, Lloyd overcame the illness and dedicated much of his life to helping others facing similar battles.
His fundraising career saw him take on some of the most unusual and physically demanding challenges imaginable.
In 2002, Lloyd captured the nation’s attention when he completed the London Marathon wearing a 120lb deep-sea diving suit. Taking five days, eight hours and 29 minutes to cross the finish line, he raised money for Cancer and Leukaemia in Childhood (CLIC), inspiring others with his determination following his own battle with the illness.
That was just one of many remarkable achievements. Lloyd climbed Mount Everest, completed an ultra-marathon in Death Valley, cycled almost 3,000 miles across Australia on a penny-farthing and undertook an underwater marathon in Loch Ness, which took 12 days to complete.
In 2009, he walked from Land’s End to John O’Groats dressed in a life-sized Tyrannosaurus rex costume, raising £175,000 for Teenage Cancer Trust.
He also completed the London Marathon in a suit of armour while pulling a 200lb dragon, took on the challenge dressed as Indiana Jones while pulling a giant boulder, and tackled the Three Peaks Challenge in his famous diving suit in 2020, raising almost £50,000 for Lord’s Taverners.
His contribution to charity was recognised in 2005 when he was awarded an MBE.
Lloyd’s determination, generosity and willingness to push himself to extraordinary limits made him an inspiration to people across the country. His legacy extends far beyond football, touching the lives of countless people and families through his fundraising work.
Everyone at Dagenham & Redbridge sends their deepest condolences to Lloyd’s family, friends and all those who knew him.
Rest in peace, Lloyd.

Essex Women's Captain Grace Scrivens will captain England Women A for their red-ball fixture during their tour of India.
England Women A have named their captains for their upcoming multi-format tour of India.
Following a successful return to action last summer including her best bowling figures of 6-11 in the Vitality Blast, Surrey bowler Ryana MacDonald-Gay will captain the three-match T20 series that opens the tour in Pune.
In the three-match 50-over series that follows in Mumbai, Surrey wicket-keeper batter Kira Chathli takes up the reins, as she did throughout the return series at home last summer.
And for the four-day red-ball match that concludes the tour, Essex's Grace Scrivens will lead the side at the Wankhede Stadium.
There are also two changes to the squads that were previously announced due to injuries.
Warwickshire bowler Issy Wong is recovering from a stress injury in her right foot. Her place in the 4-day squad is taken by Alexa Stonehouse, while the white-ball squads will travel with one fewer player.
And Lancashire batter Emma Lamb has been withdrawn from both 50-over and 4-day squads following surgery on a back injury. Her place has been taken by 19-year-old Durham batting all-rounder Grace Thompson.

https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.title: Where Are They Now? Essex Men's Winter Round-Up
https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Men's players are continuing their cricketing commitments around the world, representing various teams and franchises across a range of formats and competitions.
Charlie Allison has been playing in Australia for Willetton Premier Cricket Club in Western Australia, where he has scored 38 from 62 balls and 37 from 36 balls.
The 21-year-old batter has now paused his time in Australia after landing in Rome, Italy, ahead of the Italian T10 League. Allison will represent Napoli Knights alongside his brother, former Eagle and current Worcestershire bowling allrounder Ben Allison.
Essex Men's Vice-Captain Sam Cook has been part of the England Lions camp in the Caribbean, most recently featuring in an 80-run victory over West Indies A. Cook bowled nine overs, taking 1-40 in the 50-over contest.
The seamer has also been named in the England Men's Test squad for the upcoming series against South Africa, which begins in December.
Jordan Cox has continued his involvement with the England Men's squad during their ODI series against Australia. Despite defeat in the opening game, the wicketkeeper-batter recently starred in England's first ODI victory in Adelaide for more than 15 years.
Cox showcased his impressive 360-degree range of stroke play around the Adelaide Oval, scoring 67 from just 49 deliveries. Like Cook, he has also been named in England's Test squad for the upcoming series against South Africa .
Simon Harmer continues to represent the Proteas in Test cricket, with South Africa now taking on Bangladesh following their impressive series victory over Australia, in which the Essex allrounder played a vital role with the ball.
Harmer is currently featuring in the ongoing first Test against Bangladesh, with his figures standing at 0-83 from 16 overs. He is due to bat at number 9 with South Africa 287/4 trailing by 113 runs.
Mackenzie Jones represented Scotland at the Hong Kong Sixes tournament before travelling to Australia to feature in grade cricket.
The tall right-arm seam bowler has since represented Lane Cove Cricket Club, recording figures of 0-18 from eight overs and scoring an unbeaten 56 from 87 deliveries.
Michael Pepper is preparing for the International League T20, which begins on Saturday 21 November. The wicketkeeper-batter will once again represent Abu Dhabi Knight Riders following last season's campaign, during which he scored 175 runs across five innings at an average of 35.00.
Noah Thain is currently in South Africa, representing Claremont Cricket Club. The right-handed allrounder has featured at the top of the order, batting both at number three and as an opener. His highest score so far has been 70 from 71 deliveries, while his bowling figures include 0-26 from four overs.
Paul Walter has been enjoying an excellent run of form in the Abu Dhabi T10 League, scoring 51 from 22 deliveries, 62 not out from 26 and 82 not out from just 29 balls for the Arabian Aces.
These impressive performances provide excellent preparation ahead of Walter's upcoming involvement in the ILT20, where he will represent Sharjah Warriorz. Like Pepper, his campaign gets underway on Saturday 21 November when the tournament begins.
All other members of the Essex Men's squad continue to follow their individual winter programmes, working alongside the Club's coaching and medical staff as preparations gather pace ahead of the 2027 season.
Further updates will follow in the coming weeks and into the new year as more members of the squad head overseas for their own off-season cricketing commitments.

At MR Cricket MR Hockey, we recognise the importance of having equipment and clothing designed specifically for female cricketers. That's why we stock a growing range of women's cricket equipment, alongside a comprehensive teamwear offering featuring ladies-specific fits and styles. From training to match day, our aim is to ensure every player feels comfortable, confident and looks great on the pitch.
We look forward to working alongside Essex Cricket and the clubs involved for an exciting season ahead!"

https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.title: Lest We Forget: Essex Cricket Remembers Forever and Always
https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Cricket Remembers and Honours Those Who Made the Ultimate Sacrifice.
As we mark Armistice Day on 11 November, Essex Cricket takes a moment to remember the former players and Club representatives who served their country during the two World Wars, including those who made the ultimate sacrifice.
As the Club celebrates its 150th Anniversary, we reflect on the lives and contributions of those who represented Essex on the cricket field before going on to serve their country. Their courage, dedication and sacrifice will never be forgotten.
The First World War
Following Britain's declaration of war on 04 August 1914, professional cricket continued for a short period, although the conflict quickly began to affect the domestic game.
Essex played six further matches before bringing their 1914 season to a close at Weston-super-Mare on 01 September, defeating Somerset by 10 wickets. It proved to be the final appearance for Geoffrey Davies, who had scored a career-best 118 in the match. Just over a year later, he was killed in action on the Western Front, aged 22.
During the war, Essex continued to organise around 30 matches each season against local clubs and military opposition, helping to keep cricket alive during a difficult period.
Several players who had represented the County subsequently joined the armed forces. Among those who lost their lives were:
First XI Representatives
Captain Geoffrey Boisselier Davies (1892–1915)
One of the most promising cricketers of his generation, Davies represented Essex between 1912 and 1914. A talented all-rounder, he scored 852 runs and claimed 83 wickets during his final season, underlining his considerable potential.
Commissioned into the 11th Battalion of the Essex Regiment, he rose to the rank of Captain before being killed while leading his men into action at Hulluch, France, on 26 September 1915, during the Battle of Loos.
His loss was particularly significant to Essex Cricket, with Wisden suggesting that, had he survived the war, he would have developed into an England player.
Second Lieutenant Henry David Keigwin (1881–1916)
Born in Lexden, Keigwin was a talented batsman who represented Essex in four first-class matches between 1906 and 1907. He also played for Cambridge University and was a prolific scorer during his time at Peterhouse College.
Having moved to Africa, he returned to Britain during the war and volunteered to serve with the Lancashire Fusiliers. He was killed near Thiepval on 20 September 1916, during the Battle of the Somme.
Lieutenant Frank Street (1870–1916)
Street made nine appearances for Essex between 1898 and 1899, scoring two half-centuries, including knocks of 76 against Leicestershire and 60 against Hampshire.
Despite being older than the usual age for military service, he volunteered to join the Royal Fusiliers. He was killed by a sniper's bullet at Ovillers-la-Boisselle, France, on 07 July 1916, aged 46.
Lieutenant Edward Charles Coleman (1891–1917)
Born in Southend, Coleman was an accomplished wicketkeeper who represented Essex in two matches during the 1912 season, taking a catch and completing a stumping.
He served with the Royal Fleet Auxiliary and was killed in action at Salonika on 02 April 1917, aged 25.
Second Lieutenant Ralf Hubert Robinson (1885–1917)
Robinson kept wicket for Essex on four occasions in 1912 before joining the Rifle Brigade. He was awarded the Military Medal for his service but was subsequently killed near Ypres on 23 August 1917.
Major Douglas Tosetti (1877–1918)
A member of the Essex Second XI between 1900 and 1903, Tosetti served with the 8th Battalion of the Royal Berkshire Regiment.
Having previously been wounded at Loos, he continued to lead his men and was awarded the Military Cross. He was killed on 21 March 1918, the opening day of the German Spring Offensive.
Lieutenant James Valiant (1884–1917)
Valiant represented Essex in one first-class match in 1912 and was also a ground bowler. Commissioned into the Royal Welch Fusil

Fleming flew to Perth last week, where the England Men’s white-ball team is preparing for their ODI and T20 series against Australia, to finalise selection and preparation plans for the South Africa Test tour alongside Managing Director of England Men’s Cricket, Rob Key, National Selector, Marcus North, and Men’s Performance Director, Ed Barney.

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Sport in Essex takes centre stage with new initiative to boost health and wellbeing
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Essex United by Sport will help residents lead more active lives and improve access to physical activity.
A major new initiative has launched in Essex to help residents lead healthier lives. Essex United by Sport will bring together partners from across the county. Together they will use the power of sport to improve health and tackle inequalities.
Essex is home to world-class sporting facilities, elite teams and inspirational athletes. Essex United by Sport will build on these strengths to celebrate sporting achievements. It will bring people of all ages together and create opportunities to take part.
Essex United by Sport is powered by Essex County Council. It is delivered in partnership with Active Essex and their partners. Active Essex is the lead for sport and physical activity in Essex.
The programme will focus on:
sport for all – ensuring every resident can engage in sport
sport for communities – using sport to bring people together and strengthen local neighbourhoods
sport for health – helping residents live longer, healthier and happier lives
sport for the future – helping residents fulfil their potential and contributing to Essex’s economy.
While progress has been made, more than half a million adults in Essex still do not get the recommended 150 minutes of physical activity each week. This shows more needs to be done to help people get active.
Councillor Chris Hossack, Essex County Council Cabinet Member for Residents and Communities said:
“Sport and physical activity have the power to improve lives, strengthen communities and create opportunities for people of all ages. Essex United by Sport will bring together partners from the sport, health, education, criminal justice and voluntary and community sector, to ensure more residents can access those benefits, regardless of their background, location or ability.
“From supporting healthier lifestyles and improving mental health, to developing skills and inspiring future generations, this programme will help unlock the full potential of sport across Essex.”
The programme was launched at the Essex Sport Arena, University of Essex, on Tuesday 3 November.
Pupils from Braiswick Primary School joined players and coaches for a basketball game. Guests heard from speakers representing the council, Sport England and the sporting community. Topics included the role Essex United by Sport will play in creating healthier, more connected communities.
Lewis Richardson, Olympic medallist and Essex athlete attended the launch, and said:
“Sport has given me opportunities, experiences and life skills that have shaped who I am today. Every young person should have the chance to experience those benefits, regardless of where they live or their background. Essex United by Sport is about creating those opportunities and inspiring the next generation to get active, build confidence and achieve their potential.”
For further information, visit activeessex.org/essex-united-by-sport

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Green Spaces and Parks Activated to bring Communities Together
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Find Your Active HERE signs launch in Harlow and Thurrock to help residents move more in their local spaces.
Residents in Harlow and Thurrock are being encouraged to get active closer to home, thanks to the launch of Find Your Active Here signs. The initiative, launched at the beginning of August, aims to help local people discover simple, free and accessible ways to be active for community connection and belonging.
In partnership with Harlow Town Council, Thurrock Council and local organisations such as Time for Change, the Find Your Active Here signs are being piloted in two of the Sport England Place Partnership areas, Harlow (The Stow and Harlow Town Park) and Thurrock (Daisy Field, Tilbury).
A community hub with wide open space, The Stow Sports Ground is perfect for playful movement, group activities, and family fun. In addition, Harlow Town Park is a huge 164‑acre green space with gardens, play areas, trails, table tennis tables, a paddling pool, a skate park, and of course the outdoor gym. Both locations are an ideal space to encourage activity for every age, ability and confidence level.
Daisy Field is a local green space at the heart of Tilbury, serving as a focal point for the neighbourhood, frequently hosting local youth sports, wellness hubs, and community outreach. Daisy Field makes up a whole host of local, nearby green spaces that also include an outdoor gym, pump track, skate park, playground and walking circuit.
Danielle Warnes, Active Essex Relationship Manager for West Essex said; “We believe that being active doesn’t have to mean joining a gym or signing up for a class. Sometimes, the best place to move more, feel better, and enjoy the outdoors is right on your doorstep. Harlow is bursting with regeneration and this builds on the momentum to enhance local assets and give back to the community.”
The bright and visible signs include a QR code which signposts users to solo activities, or ways to get active with family, friends or neighbours. A host of inclusive options and organised sessions taking place in the green space, or nearby areas, can also be discovered. Since the placement of the signs at the beginning of the month, over 200 residents have already been inspired.
Juliette Raison, Active Essex Relationship Manager for South West Essex added: “Greater Essex is made up of 21% of green infrastructure and so many spaces are underutilised. It is our hope that these signs bring communities to these areas and encourage both informal and formal activity to take place. Being active outdoors brings so many added benefits for our mental health, social connection and wider physical health too.”
The introduction of the signs are part of the wider Find Your Active, Move for your Mind campaign that spans Greater Essex and is powered by Mind in Essex. The campaign highlights the powerful connection between physical activity and mental wellbeing, and acts as a gentle reminder that being active can be simple, uplifting, and part of your everyday life.
Find out more: www.activeessex.org/find-your-active/here/

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex ActivAte Marks Another Successful Half Term
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Celebrating another successful delivery of its Essex ActivAte half term programme, supporting children, young people and families across Essex with free enriching activities and nutritious meals. Funded by Essex County Council, the half‑term clubs run during the smaller school breaks in February, May and October, providing 2–3 days of high‑quality support for those who need it most.
In 2025, Essex ActivAte delivered significant impact, with 15,050 attendees across all three half terms, and 13,728 funded spaces provided across the three holiday periods. These figures highlight the ongoing demand for accessible, high quality holiday provision for families under financial pressure.
Essex ActivAte clubs are delivered by a trusted network of local providers and run Monday to Friday (unless specified). They offer children an engaging mix of physical activity, enrichment sessions and fun food education. The programme prioritises children eligible for income‑related free school meals and those from low‑income working families, as well as young people who may be vulnerable to inactivity or social isolation without access to this vital support.
For many families, school holidays can be a challenging time. Essex ActivAte clubs give children a safe, welcoming environment to stay active, try new experiences, socialise and enjoy a nutritious meal, while also offering much needed respite for parents and carers. Clubs play a crucial role in supporting children’s physical and mental wellbeing, ensuring they have opportunities to move, learn and build confidence during school breaks.
Local providers and parents continue to emphasise just how essential this support is:
“Children feel accepted and welcomed in our non‑judgemental environment, and parents and carers really value having a couple of hours’ respite. Local SEND provision like this is vital for families and the wider community.” -Provider from Chelmsford
“Thank you so much for the free activities, my girls had an amazing time, you’ve literally saved me to be honest with you! Money can be really tight sometimes.” -Parent from Tendring
With many households experiencing increased cost‑of‑living pressures, free holiday programmes like Essex ActivAte are more important than ever. Not only do they relieve financial strain, but they also ensure that children across Essex have access to high‑quality, meaningful experiences that support both learning and wellbeing.
For more information about the programme and future club dates, visit the Essex ActivAte website.

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex Sporting Stars Rally Behind Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind Campaign
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
In July last year, Active Essex were thrilled to announce an extension of their Find Your Active campaign, Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind.
Powered by Essex Public Health Find Your Active: Move For Your Mind brings about a new chapter from the successful Find Your Active campaign; a county-wide movement, inspiring people of all ages and abilities across the County to discover and enjoy ways to get moving – whether that be getting out in the garden, a short walk, social bike ride or a friendly game of football. It celebrates the fact that everyone can enjoy the huge benefits of moving more, it’s just about finding what’s right for you.
And in January, the campaign made more exciting strides as it launched a new partnership with Mind in Essex, to champion the powerful connection between physical activity and mental wellbeing. The partnership aims to create more opportunities for people across Essex to explore movement in ways that feel enjoyable and accessible.
As the campaign continues to gain momentum, we’re pleased to welcome Paris 2024 Bronze Medal winner, and professional boxer – Lewis Richardson, and British Para Swimmer and World Champion – Ellie Challis into the Active Essex family as our Athlete Ambassador’s for 2026.
Lewis, spent 2025 as our Athlete Ambassador, visiting his old school to deliver an inspiring talk and lead a boxing session, spoke with our Director, Jason Fergus in an interview for International Olympic day. He also helped us task the county with getting active during National School Sports Week and on National Fitness Day. His passion when sharing his story, and his dedication to inspiring the next generation truly inspired us as he went above and beyond in his role as an advocate for Active Essex.
Lewis has had a breakthrough year since the Paris 2024 games where he was the only Team GB boxer to medal, and after a stellar amateur career which led him to Olympic Bronze, has now turned pro. Since making the move to professional boxing, with his debut bout taking place at Ipswich Town’s Portman Road stadium, Lewis has taken part in two fights, finishing as winner in both. He explained;
I’m really excited to be an athlete ambassador for the Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind campaign. Movement has always been a huge part of my life, whether that’s for performance-related purposes or just staying active day to day. Mental strength is really important to me, and I’ve felt first-hand how much better I am mentally when I’m able to move. I’ve also seen the positive impact it’s had on the people around me, it can be a snowball effect, but it all starts with moving.
Ellie is one of Britain’s most decorated young para-swimmers, with a host of Paralympic and World Championship medals to her name, Ellie is also a record breaker, holding the Women’s SB2 50m Breaststroke world record. Ellie’s early-life adversity is well known, she contracted meningitis at 16 months old, resulting in amputations of both legs above the knee and both arms below the elbow.
Despite this, she has forged a remarkable sporting career, regularly sharing her message of resilience, determination, and overcoming barriers. Ellie is also an ambassador for the Meningitis Trust and has been in the role since the age of 5. As an ambassador for the charity, she helps other children adjust to life after limb loss. A previous winner of the Young Sports Personality of the Year award, Ellie has achieved so much at just the age of 21.
“I’m really excited to be working with Active Essex on their Find Your Active Move Your Mind campaign this year. Movement is super important to me because it made physio fun and I met so many friends through being active and swimming. I love seeing people try new sports and ways to be active whilst also having fun.”

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Unlocking community strength
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Active Essex and community partners strengthen voluntary sector organisations, through place-based support
Active Essex, working alongside community partners through Essex County Council’s Your Essex Community programme is accelerating efforts to build the capability and resilience of voluntary and community organisations across the county.
The place-based support offer is ensuring that local groups have the tools, skills and resources they need to meet the diverse needs of residents. By bringing organisations together, the programme is creating the conditions for stronger collaboration, shared learning and greater collective impact.
Community aspirations are being reflected across the place-based module through local training opportunities, peer learning events, and bespoke development support. Recognising that no two places in Essex are the same, Active Essex has worked closely with partners to understand where unmet support needs exist and how we can work together to build resilience and capacity in local voluntary sector organisations. This approach is uncovering deeper insights into local challenges, while helping remove barriers that often limit organisational growth.
Louise Voyce, Active Essex Relationship Development Lead, said:
“We’re proud to support this work and we aim to help build a thriving, connected and resilient sector that meets the needs of local communities.
Based on initial research from 138 voluntary community sector organisations, plus a series of listening exercises, we found that the biggest unmet support needs for the sector were sustainable income generation, access to free and low-cost training, help creating new partnerships and building networks and volunteer recruitment and capacity.
By working with local community organisations and Active Essex partners, we have already been able to excel in providing support to the sector and the impact we’ve seen over the past 6 months, has been great.”
To date, 94% of delegates that have participated in a Your Essex Community place-based support offer, have rated their experience as very satisfied with 82% stating they gained key takeaways that they could apply directly into their work. Similarly, over 100 individuals attended fundraising and small grant workshops learning how to write stronger applications, maximise awarded funding and strengthening governance and organisational confidence.
One participant from North Essex shared:
“It made me realise the number of options to apply for. It gave me focus and clarity on our next steps for applying for funding.”
Active Essex’s commitment to strengthening the voluntary community sector continues. As the organisation moves into 2026, further opportunities will be developed as part of this programme. These include Meet the Funder events, large grant workshops and sessions on partnership building and long-term sustainability.
For more information on the place-based offer and the Your Essex Community initiative, or to apply to deliver infrastructure support for the next phase of programme visit:  www.activeessex.org/your-essex-community/

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex responds to mental health crisis with new movement-focused partnership
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Find Your Active: Move for your Mind joins forces with Mind in Essex to help residents discover the powerful link between physical activity and better mental health.
Today (19 January), a new partnership launches in Essex to help residents improve their mental wellbeing by increasing their physical activity. Find Your Active: Move for your Mind and Mind in Essex unite trusted mental health expertise with a county‑wide drive to make movement enjoyable, accessible, and achievable for all.
The Find Your Active campaign, by Active Essex, first launched five years ago to help residents move more following the pandemic. This next phase, powered by Essex Public Health and delivered in partnership with Mind in Essex, focuses specifically on the mental wellbeing benefits of physical activity and aims to support people to take small, achievable steps that make a meaningful difference.
Mind in Essex is a network of local mental‑health charities working across the county to support people experiencing emotional or psychological difficulties. It brings together several independent Mind organisations – Mind in West Essex, Basildon Mind, South East and Central Essex Mind, Mid and North East Essex Mind, and Thurrock and Brentwood Mind – to create a more joined‑up, accessible system of support. Their shared aim is to make it easier for people to find help close to home, reduce stigma around mental health, and offer services ranging from counselling and crisis support to community groups and training, strengthening mental‑health provision for communities throughout Essex.
Through the partnership, residents will benefit from:
Guidance and resources on how movement can support mental wellbeing
Opportunities to join gentle, beginner‑friendly or community‑based activity sessions
Support from local Find Your Active Place Navigators and Mind in Essex ambassadors
Signposting to mental wellbeing activities and services across the county
With 1 in 10 adults and 1 in 6 children in Essex experiencing a mental health problem each year, the partnership arrives at an important time. Research shows that even 10 minutes of movement can lift mood, reduce stress, and build emotional resilience.
Cllr John Spence, Essex County Council Cabinet Member for Children’s Services, Adult Social Care, Public Health and Integration said: “Physical activity isn’t just about physical health, its positive impact on mental wellbeing is clear. Moving in any form refreshes the mind as well as the body. The Move for your Mind addition to the already successful Find Your Active campaign highlights how vital activity is for those facing mental health challenges. I encourage all residents to explore and find the activity that works for them.”
David Sollis, CEO of South East and Central Essex Mind, commented: “We are delighted to be partnering with Find Your Active: Move for your Mind. By combining our mental health expertise with their commitment to accessible activity, we hope to empower more people across Essex to discover movement that supports their wellbeing. This partnership will help us reach individuals who may be struggling and offer them practical, meaningful ways to feel better.”
The Find Your Active campaign partnership will continue throughout 2026, to expand opportunities, strengthen community support, and promote the role of movement in maintaining good mental health.
For more information on the partnership, to explore local activity opportunities, or to access mental wellbeing support, visit: www.activeessex.org/find-your-active

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Nominees and distinguished guests come together to celebrate success at the Essex Activity Awards!
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
The annual Essex Activity Awards took place on Thursday 4 th December, at Hatfield Place, bringing together over 150 shortlisted nominees and invited guests to celebrate the remarkable achievements in physical activity, sport, and wellbeing across the county.
Organised by Active Essex, the annual event highlights and recognises the outstanding contributions made by individuals, communities, schools, clubs, and workplaces that inspire and promote the importance of physical activity and movement in Greater Essex.
Hosted by ITV News Presenter Charlie Frost and Paralympic Gold Medallist Danny Crates, the evening saw awards given out across several categories. While some winners were chosen by a private panel of judges, others were decided through a public vote and the Young Sports Personality of the Year award by a selection of the Active Essex #MoveWithUs Ambassadors, ensuring the community’s voice was heard.
Michelle Agyemang, who helped the Lionesses to an inspirational Euro’s title in July, was crowned Essex Sports Personality of the Year. Unable to attend the evening, in a video sent in for the evening, Michelle explained; “ It’s a great privilege to receive this award, especially as somebody that has lived in Essex all of my life. I’m grateful to God for this opportunity, and thankful to all my friends, family and teammates, this couldn’t have been done without them.”
The Unsung Hero award voted for by the public, went to Lee Clark who was recognised for his significant efforts for charity. Despite managing work, family and personal health challenges, Lee runs a mental health walking group, a litter-picking team and a charity football club. Known for the creativity of his approach, Lee gives every spare moment to helping others and to date has raised nearly £500,000 for over 70 charities.
The Inspiring Young Lives award, a new category for this year was awarded to Rosedan Breakfast and After School Club. A vibrant and multicultural club that offers inclusive daily activities, summer programmes, all delivered by nurturing staff. Rosedan helps young people build confidence, creativity and friendships, all whilst encouraging healthy and active lifestyles.
Other categories that celebrated individuals during the ceremony included Young Sports Personality of the Year, awarded to Arsenals Max Dowman, and Move With Us Champion, another new category for this year, acknowledged young people aiming to inspire those around them. The coveted Find Your Active Wellbeing award, given out as part of the Find Your Active: Move for your Mind campaign, went to Sarah Clyne who uses physical activity as a tool to improve residents mental health.
The evening also recognised groups of people striving to make a difference, with awards like Sports Club of the Year and Active Employer of the Year. The Active Education Provider of the Year shined a spotlight on an education setting prioritising sport and physical activity in its setting, with TreeTops Free School coming out as winners.
Active Essex Chair Dr William Bird MBE said: “The Essex Activity Awards shine a spotlight on the incredible energy and commitment that drives physical activity across our county. From grassroots groups to elite performers, and from schools to parks and workplaces, these awards celebrate the people and teams who work tirelessly to create opportunities for everyone. Whether it’s inspiring someone to take their first step into finding their active or coaching the stars of tomorrow, this event recognises those who make movement accessible, enjoyable, and life-changing for our communities.”
A huge congratulations to all winners and highly commended for their outstanding accomplishments. The 2025 category winners are:
Active Employer of the year, Baker Labels – Brentwood
Education Provider of the year, Tree Tops Free School – Thurrock
Find Your Active Wellbeing Award, Sarah Clyne – Tendring

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Nominations now open for the Essex Activity Awards 2025!
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
The annual Essex Activity Awards is once again returning to celebrate those who have made incredible achievements through physical activity and wellbeing across Greater Essex.
With nominations now open, it is a chance to recognise inspiring individuals, clubs, schools, organisations and employers who are driving a more active, healthy, and vibrant county, bringing their stories and impact into the spotlight.
Dr William Bird MBE, Chair of Active Essex said:
“We believe that living a healthy, active life shouldn’t be out of reach for anyone. That’s why we are working together across the county to make physical activity a part of everyday life. So much of our work is inspired by incredible individuals whose actions motivate us to go further, by challenging ourselves, supporting each other, and using physical activity and sport as a force for positive change.”
New categories have been introduced this year such as the Find Your Active Wellbeing Award and the Move With Us Champion Award.
The Find Your Active Wellbeing Award recognises an instructor, organisation, or group that has made a meaningful impact on mental wellbeing through physical activity. This category, new for 2025 ties in closely with Active Essex and Essex Public Health’s campaign Find Your Active: Move for your Mind. It highlights how movement can support mental health and emotional wellbeing.
The Move With Us Champion category will celebrate a young person who inspires others to be active, whether that’s through volunteering, or promoting physical activity in their community, school or club.
Popular categories remain, such as ‘Unsung Hero’ and ‘Sports Club of the Year’ celebrating those who make a real difference through sport and physical activity in the community. Whether you want to nominate a motivating coach, a dedicated volunteer, an innovative school or a welcoming community group that use sport to bring people together, this is your chance to provide them with the recognition they deserve.
Nominations must be submitted by  midnight on Sunday, 28th September 2025 to ensure your nomination is counted.
View the full list of categories and submit your nomination here: activeessex.org/essex-activity-awards-2025

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: £9.8 million secured to build stronger Essex communities and tackle inactivity
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Significant investment from Sport England will transform lives through the power of sport and physical activity.
Almost £10 million funding has been secured to strengthen communities and tackle inequality in activity levels across Greater Essex. The investment, from Sport England, secured by Active Essex, will support the Place Partnership programme.
The Sport England funding will see £250 million of National Lottery and Exchequer funding invested in more than 90 new places across England until 2028.
The Place Partnership programme aims to:
increase physical activity
decrease physical inactivity
provide positive experiences of physical activity for children and young people
tackle inequalities in local communities
The latest investment into Greater Essex will see Castle Point, Harlow and Thurrock benefit.  Basildon, Colchester and Tendring have also received further funding support, following the work achieved through the Essex Local Delivery Pilot.
Aiming to break down the everyday barriers that prevent people from moving more and living well, this opportunity will focus on areas that need support the most, helping make physical activity a daily reality for everyone, regardless of their postcode or income.
Lisa Dodd-Mayne, Executive Director of Place at Sport England, said:
“Our recent investment into Essex reflects our continued commitment to ensure that interventions are rooted in the unique needs, cultures and priorities of local communities. Targeted investment in areas of greatest need can unlock participation and reduce health inequalities. The 3 new places in Essex, and the 3 already well on the journey, will be shining examples of how these types of approaches can drive real change locally to help create a more active, healthier nation.”
Opportunities will be co-designed with communities, in response to their specific needs. Local organisations and projects will be supported to deliver initiatives that help build capacity across the system, creating meaningful and lasting impact.
Councillor Louise McKinlay, Deputy Leader of Essex County Council and Cabinet Member for Communities, Economic Growth and Prosperity, said :
“Sport is incredibly powerful. It can literally change lives. I am very proud of the work that has been done with the Greater Essex Partnership over the past few years to support people to fulfil their potential and all through sport and being active.
“This additional funding will really help to drive the efforts of Active Essex. We know healthier people are happier people and working with our incredible local partners across the county, it will really make a difference to so many lives.”
As one of 43 Active Partnerships, which started as a legacy of the London 2012 Olympic Games, Active Essex are pioneers in place-based working. This has been expanded through the work of the Essex Local Delivery Pilot (LDP), which began in 2017.
Dr William Bird, Chair of Active Essex said:
“The success of the LDP has meant that Essex has received further funding to support three new areas. What we’ve learnt alongside our partners, is that we must create the conditions for our communities to thrive, and I have no doubt that this further investment will be capitalised on by all places in Greater Essex. Utilising learnings across the system from health and education to transport and recreation, we all have the ability to co-create physical activity opportunities for everyone.”
Across the six Place Partnerships, work has already taken place on identifying local needs. This has seen opportunities such as Essex Pedal Power, The Gunny Project on Canvey, and Rose Villa Surgery Community Garden in Basildon develop.
Find out more about Place Partnerships here: https://www.activeessex.org/place-partnerships/

Scott for Tiptree Jobserve was prepared to run with the ball and when he found space just inside the penalty area, his shot was blocked by Hymus. Harwich & Parkeston “A” opened the scoring on eleven minutes, LOGAN WOODWARD chased forward onto a defensive clearance, his first shot on the run was saved by keeper, Field but the follow up was despatched into the back of the net. Thorpe Athletic (three for Barnard), maintained their lead in the Premier Division with an away win over The Rodings & Waltham, Hatfield Peverel came from behind to beat Dedham Old Boys., Great Bentley were the highest goalscorers with five against Cressing United and a resurgent Gas Recreation moved up to fourth with a victory over lowly White Notley. https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.title: Peter Furley Obituary & Funeral Arrangements
https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.text:
Peter died peacefully at home on 13th October aged 88, with his daughter Jo and son Jon at
his side. He joined Southend Rugby club in 1955 when the home pitch was situated on the
slope in Priory Park, he also joined the Municipal College Cricket Club’s second eleven the
same year.
He originally played Flyhalf for a lower team at age 18 with his brother Michael, but
graduated to the Priors aged 24 where he played with Terry North. Aged 37 in 1974 he
became Captain of the ExA1: 4th Team. When he reached an age that he was too old to
actually play the game, aged 44 he moved on to being a referee which he did until the age of
75 and alongside that he was also a 4th official for the 1st team, he ended his active
involvement at the age of 77 and then became an avid supporter of the 1st team. He would
travel to home and away games when he could and in later years his daughter joined him
too.
He worked as an architect in London for his whole career and was very involved in the
clubhouse and later the stand design too.
His brother Roger Furley remembers one famous occasion when Roger was umpiring a
hockey game on the Old Southendian’s astro pitch, Peter was refereeing a game on the
rugby pitch on the other side of the fence and their other brother, Michael, was doing the
Priors game on the main pitch. Roger’s friend commented at the time, that the Furleys were
succeeding in ruining 84 peoples afternoon at the same time!
He had a very long and happy life for 88 years and it was only his body that gave out on him
in the end, his mind was as sharp as always even in his last hour. He will be missed dearly
by all his family and friends.
His funeral will take place at Southend Crematorium at 1pm on Friday 6th November 2026 followed by a wake at the club.
Please find below the link to the tribute page for dad, the page also contains the link for the live stream for those that cannot attend and also the address for the crematorium and details of the charity that we have chosen.

https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.title: Ken Baynes
https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.text:
Over three hundred people attended Kens Funeral on Friday 2nd October. They included past and present members of our club as well as members of Rochford Hundred Golf club and friends and collogues from the business world and beyond. The wake at the club after was bursting at the seams.
Kenneth 'Ken' Baynes
13 August 1961 – 13 September 2026
Kenneth Baynes died peacefully on 13 September 2026, aged 65, surrounded by his family, after living with myeloma. A devoted husband to Davina and a hugely proud father to Robert and Hannah, he will be deeply missed by them and his many friends.
He was born in Cardiff, the youngest of four children, and grew up in Hitchin and Southend. He went to Westcliff High School and then Felsted, where he became Head of House and played in the school's unbeaten rugby and hockey teams. After a year in Munich, where he was named Player of the Year for Munich Rugby Club, he came home and joined Southend Rugby Club, turning down an opportunity to play first class representative rugby at London Scottish. He played for SRFC 1st XV for over three decades, and kept going until he was 51.
He worked for Barclays for 33 years, 28 of them in the dealing room trading the sterling money markets, and was highly respected in the City. Alongside his career he took on charity treks along the Great Wall of China, in the Himalayas and in Brazil, raising hundreds of thousands of pounds for The Children's Society.
He retired in 2013 and immediately sailed across the Atlantic with Charles. He then set himself new goals, becoming a single-figure golfer and a fully qualified Level 3 international ski instructor, and he loved nothing more than skiing with his family. He became Treasurer and Co-Chairman of Southend Rugby Club and was made a Life Member in 2024. He was also a proud member of Rochford Hundred Golf Club for over 20 years and was honoured to be appointed RHGC Club Captain for 2026.
Competitive, funny, generous and fiercely determined, Ken faced his illness with the same spirit he brought to everything else. In his own words: "I would rather die on my feet than live on my knees."
FUNERAL
Friday 2 October 2026, 3pm
Southend Crematorium - 285 Sutton Road, Southend-on-Sea, SS2 5PX
WAKE
Southend Rugby Club, from after the service until late
(Warners Bridge Park, Sumpters Way, Southend-on-Sea SS2 5RE)
FLOWERS/DONATIONS
No flowers, please. Ken was passionate about supporting Myeloma UK to help find a cure, and the family warmly asks that you donate to the charity in his memory.
DRESS CODE
Traditional funeral wear, with club ties for members of RHGC and SRFC

https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.title: Saxons Ready For The Challenge Ahead
https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.text:
With pre-season complete and the opening league weekend finally upon us, there is a real sense of excitement and anticipation around the Southend Rugby Club senior playing group.
The summer has brought plenty of change. We have said goodbye to some experienced players who have contributed enormously to the group, but in their place we have welcomed a number of exciting new faces.
Some arrive with valuable experience from higher levels of the game, while others represent something equally important to us — talented young players who have progressed through our own junior and academy pathway and are now ready to take their opportunities in senior rugby.
With so many new faces coming together, one of the biggest challenges throughout pre-season was always going to be how quickly we could bond as a group.
In that respect, the extended pre-season has actually worked in our favour. It has given the players more time together, both on and off the pitch, and the response has been fantastic.
Throughout the summer, the group has continually pushed and challenged one another. There has been a real desire to improve, compete and strive for excellence, with standards being driven by the players themselves as much as by the coaching team.
Now, on the eve of the first league weekend for both the Saxons and Priors , you can feel the excitement levels rising.
Pre-season is done. Now the real challenge begins.
There is plenty of potential within this group, but potential alone means very little. What has been particularly encouraging is seeing the belief, trust and understanding between the players continuing to grow.
We also know that no season is straightforward.
There will be difficult Saturdays. There will be moments when things don’t go our way and occasions when this group will have to go to the well for one another , dig deep and show exactly what it stands for.
From everything we have seen throughout pre-season, there is every reason to believe that this is a group that will keep fighting, keep working and keep pushing for each other.
As we head into the new campaign, the focus isn’t on making big predictions or looking too far ahead. It is much simpler than that.
Be better each week.
Keep learning. Keep challenging each other. Keep raising our standards and take something from every performance — whether that comes from a win or a loss.
There is a long season ahead and plenty of rugby still to be played, but there is a genuine sense of excitement about what this group could achieve together.
Now it’s time to get started.
One Club. One Direction.

Southend Rugby Football Club is delighted to announce the continuation with a two-year partnership with Paul Robinson Solicitors, who are once again the club's Main Club and Shirt Sponsor for the next two seasons.

https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.title: Welcome From The Director Of Rugby
https://www.southendrugby.com/news?forma.text:
Director of Rugby Welcome
A very warm welcome to Warners Bridge, the home of Southend Rugby Club.
Having been a player here for over ten years and Head Coach for the previous eight, I am incredibly proud and honoured to be appointed Director of Rugby at this fantastic club. Southend RFC has been a huge part of my life and is built on strong values, passionate people and a proud rugby tradition. It is a privilege to lead the next chapter of our journey together.
My vision is simple: One Club. One Direction.
We will continue to build a culture where standards drive performance and performance drives success. I am excited to continue the work that Josh, myself, our coaching staff, players, volunteers and management have worked so hard to establish over many years. We have built strong foundations, but there is still much more to achieve. The challenges ahead are exciting, and I look forward to seeing what this talented group of players can accomplish together.
The work starts now.
Reflecting on Last Season
The 2025/26 season was one of highs and lows but ultimately the club's most successful campaign in recent years. Our Saxons finished 4th in Regional 1, producing some outstanding performances both home and away throughout the season.
The upcoming Regional 1 campaign promises to be even more competitive. New grounds await, fresh challenges lie ahead and the return of Eton Manor will reignite a healthy rivalry that many of us have enjoyed over the years. With a young, talented squad strengthened by some exciting additions, we are looking forward to seeing how far this group can go by playing ambitious, intelligent rugby.
Our Priors finished 9th in Counties 1 Hertfordshire. While the league position only tells part of the story, the squad once again proved its importance within our rugby programme by preparing players for senior rugby. Several players stepped up to make their Saxons debuts, highlighting the strength of the development pathway we continue to build.
We're also delighted that the Priors have now returned to the Essex league structure and will compete in Essex Counties 1 this season. This is something the club has worked towards for a long time and provides an even stronger platform for player development and progression.
Developing Home-Grown Talent
One of the areas I am most proud of is the continued development of our own players.
This season has once again shown that our academy pathway is thriving. Academy players have progressed into the Priors, first-year seniors have earned Saxons debuts and several Colts have represented both the Cardinals and Bishops. These achievements are a credit to our coaching staff, the commitment of our players and the pathway we have created throughout the club.
Our ambition is simple: to provide every player with a clear route through the club, giving them the opportunity to fulfil their potential and one day represent the Saxons.
What Success Looks Like
Success isn't measured solely by league tables.
Of course we all want to win rugby matches, but true success will also be measured by the environment we create, the players we develop, the standards we uphold and the pride people feel when pulling on a Southend shirt.
We want our players to enjoy their rugby, our supporters to feel connected to the club and everyone involved to contribute to a culture that people are proud to be part of.
The People Behind the Programme
No rugby club succeeds without the people working tirelessly behind the scenes, often without recognition.
Tracey Gilson is quite simply the backbone of our playing group and affectionately known as the club's "mum". Whether she's preparing food after training and on match days for our players and visiting teams, or feeding the hundreds of Mini and Youth players, parents and supporters who come through our doors each weekend, her dedication and care never go unnoticed.
Donna Munroe and her team behind the bar are equally integral to the club, providing a warm welcome

What does it actually mean for an event to feel festive?
Beyond the Christmas jumpers, how do we create that elusive feeling of being in the Christmas spirit? We all recognise the atmosphere of Christmas when we experience it, but translating that feeling into something we can deliberately create is a different challenge altogether.

https://firstsite.uk/feed/.title: Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards 2026
https://firstsite.uk/feed/.text:
The Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards scheme aims to support artists working in Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk and Cambridgeshire with their professional career development. These annual awards are made possible through the  Collectors’ Group continuing engagement and interest in contemporary visual art in the region.
Applications to the Bursary Awards scheme should demonstrate ambition, and a commitment to, or development of the applicant’s current artistic practice.
Proposals can be made to contribute towards the costs of making new artwork, purchase of equipment, research and travel, exhibition making and other forms of professional development.
To register, please fill out the form: Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards 2026 Application Form and send it to opportunities@firstsite.uk .
In 2025, 12 winners across East Anglia were awarded £5,000 between them.
Criteria:
Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards are open to individuals only.
Applicants must be based in Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk or Cambridgeshire.
The Collectors’ Group will consider applications for between £100 and £1,000.
Applications should be made using the Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards application form and emailing it back to opportunities@firstsite.uk .
Applications can be made as a word document or exported pdf, via a picture collage, a 5 minute (or less) raw video or audio files in response to the questions in the application form, and sent to opportunities@firstsite.uk .
The closing date for applications is 5pm, 22 November 2026. Applications received after this time will not be considered.
We are unlikely to fund a similar project that was previously awarded a bursary by the same artist in two consecutive years.
We do not fund the displaying of artwork (for example, framing, fabrication, display cases), unless it is inherent to the production of the artwork itself.
We do not fund documentaries or news-based films.
We do not fund photography intended to document the installation of shows and/or artwork, or for the purposes of portfolio development
We do not fund travel for overseas work.
If you have any questions, please get in touch at fundraising@firstsite.uk and we’ll be happy to help.
Please note due to the high number and calibre of applications we receive, applicants will be informed of the panel’s decision in January 2027.
The post Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Awards 2026 appeared first on Firstsite .

https://firstsite.uk/feed/.title: In Conversation with Your Work: Preparing for a Portfolio Review with Larain Briggs
https://firstsite.uk/feed/.text:
How do you prepare for a portfolio review, and what can you gain from the experience?
Artist and researcher Larain Briggs shares practical guidance on selecting and presenting work, reflecting on process, and approaching review as a space for dialogue and discovery.
Briggs is a multidisciplinary artist and Doctorate in Fine Art researcher whose practice explores transformation, symbolism, and psychological inquiry through creative practice.
Understanding the Portfolio Review Process
A portfolio review can be much more than an opportunity to present work.
It can provide a space to reflect on how work is selected, presented and understood, while testing ideas and identifying new directions within a developing practice. It can also help clarify the aims of a portfolio and what it is intended to communicate.
From this perspective, the review is not simply about receiving feedback; it is an opportunity for conversation, reflection and discovery.

https://firstsite.uk/feed/.title: Catching up with Rebecca Riess, artist behind her exhibition ‘Lossless’ at Firstsite
https://firstsite.uk/feed/.text:
With ‘Lossless’ entering its final days, we spoke with multimedia artist Rebecca Riess – winner of the Firstsite Collectors’ Group Bursary Award 2025 and the artist behind the exhibition – about the thinking, making, and instinct behind the show – and how you give shape to what can’t always be seen.
The exhibition invites us to explore how we cope with the noise of the modern world through a bold and immersive series of otherworldly large-scale sculptures and installations.
Her work reflects our emotional responses to the world around us – from the overload of digital life and technological waste, the growing ecological crisis, abuse of power, and the physical and emotional ways we experience these pressures internally.
Rather than offering fixed meanings, Rebecca leaves space for interpretation, curiosity, and instinct – whether that’s reading a shape as a beak, noticing a shadow, or simply being drawn to a colour.
