Colchester Borough Homes (CBH) celebrated a successful year at its Annual General Meeting (AGM) at the Innovation Centre, University of Essex, on Wednesday (23 September).
Attendees included tenants and leaseholders, alongside CBH Board Members, the Executive Team, and Colchester City Council cabinet member for Housing Cllr Rhys Smithson.
Attendees received a presentation on what CBH had achieved over the last 12 months and how the organisation has continued to grow and adapt to meet the changing external operating environment.
Despite these challenges, CBH recorded a 78% customer satisfaction score, completed 76% of repairs at the first visit and responded to 98.7% of complaints on time. The organisation also continued to invest in its homes by installing 303 new kitchens, 65 new bathrooms and 480 heating systems.
The annual resident engagement report was also received, demonstrating how CBH ensures the customer voice is involved and considered in its decision making
As part of the AGM, the winners of CBH’s Good Neighbour Awards, which celebrate those who go the extra mile for their community, were announced.
CBH Board Chair, Esme Cole, said : “Our AGM highlights the dedication and commitment of our staff, board members, tenants and leaseholders in helping us to continue providing high-quality services for residents.
“Although the housing sector continues to face a range of challenges, we remain focused on improving services, listening to our customers and investing in our homes and communities. These results show the progress we are making, while recognising there is always more we can do.”
CBH Chief Executive, Philip Sullivan, said : “I’m pleased to report another successful year for CBH. The achievements highlighted at the AGM reflect the hard work of our staff and the valuable contribution made by our involved tenants, leaseholders and City Council colleagues.
“From improving customer satisfaction and repairs performance to investing in residents’ homes, we remain committed to delivering services that make a real difference to people’s lives.”
Cllr Rhys Smithson, Colchester City Council Cabinet Member for Housing, added : “CBH plays a vital role in providing quality homes and services for residents across Colchester.
“It’s encouraging to see continued investment in tenants’ homes, improving customer satisfaction and a clear commitment to resident engagement. I would like to congratulate everyone involved on another successful year and thank them for their dedication to supporting our communities.”

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Provide Community invited to help pilot the UK’s first nursing and midwifery public health framework
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
We have been invited to help pilot the UK’s first Nursing and Midwifery Public Health Practice Framework. The framework recognises how nurses, midwives and nursing associates help people stay well, prevent illness and reduce health inequalities through the care they provide every day.
In community services, that might mean spotting early signs that someone’s health is getting worse, making health information easier to understand or working with local partners to help people get the support they need closer to home.
Professor Lucy Wightman, Chief Executive of Provide Health and Group Chief Nurse, said, “A routine appointment may be the first time someone tells us they are struggling to manage a condition at home or explains what’s making it difficult to get help.
“Listening and acting on what they tell us can help prevent problems from getting worse. The framework recognises the skill involved in that everyday work and gives teams a way to share what works.”
Published on Monday 16 November 2026, the framework was developed with contributions from all four UK nations and endorsed by their Chief Nursing Officers. It gives nurses and midwives across the UK, and nursing associates in England, a shared approach to five areas of practice: promoting wellbeing, protecting people from harm, preventing ill health, working in partnership to reduce inequalities and supporting environmentally sustainable care.
Mark Heasman, Group Chief Executive of Provide Community, added, “Our teams see first-hand what helps people get the care they need and where they still face barriers. Taking part in the pilot would give us a chance to share that experience, learn from other organisations and use what we learn to make our own services easier to access.”
We are due to meet with the Florence Nightingale Foundation, which supports the pilot programme, to discuss how the pilot could work. Activity could begin in January 2027, subject to those discussions.
Click here to read the Nursing and Midwifery Public Health Practice Framework

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Employee owners help ten charities benefit from Provide Community grants
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
In October 2026, ten charities and community groups supporting people in areas served by Provide Community have received funding through its partnership with Ormiston Families , with employee owners helping decide where the money goes.
The initiative originally offered up to six grants of up to £5,000 to support charities and community groups. But after a closely contested members’ vote, Provide Community extended the funding so that all ten shortlisted organisations would benefit.
The five groups receiving the most votes have been awarded up to £5,000 each, with the remaining five receiving £2,000 each.
Applications were reviewed by Provide Community’s charity panel, made up of Member Representatives, a Non-Executive Director and our Company Secretary, which agreed a shortlist before inviting members to vote for the causes they wanted to support.
As an employee-owned community interest company, Provide Community gives colleagues a voice in the organisation and how it supports its communities. This initiative put that ownership into practice, enabling members to help direct funding towards causes that matter to them.
The following organisations have been awarded up to £5,000 each:
Brave Futures
Brighter Opportunities for Special People (BOSP)
Taking Baby Steps CIC
Sanctus
Assure (Lighthouse Family Trust)
A further £2,000 each has been awarded to:
Breast Friends CIC
Footsteps Walking With You
The Pear Tree Fund
Open Country
Hackney Foodbank
The close voting reflected the strong support for causes across the shortlist. Extending the funding means every shortlisted organisation will receive a contribution towards its work.
Mark Heasman, Group Chief Executive at Provide Community, said: “Being employee owned means our colleagues have a real say in how we support our communities. This vote gave our members the opportunity to champion causes that matter to them.
“With the votes so close, we wanted to recognise the support for all ten shortlisted organisations. We are delighted to extend the funding so that every one of them can benefit and we look forward to hearing about the difference these grants make.”
Delivered through the partnership with Ormiston Families, the grants form part of Provide Community’s wider commitment as a Community Interest Company, to reinvesting in the communities where it delivers services, extending its support beyond the care it provides.
Thank you to every organisation that applied, to the charity panel for reviewing the applications and to all members who took part in the vote. Together, they have helped turn employee ownership into practical support for ten community causes.

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: One year, extraordinary impact: Provide Community Equipment celebrates £18.5 million in equipment value retained
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
More than 119,000 items delivered, over 78,000 collected and £4 million being returned to council partners, Provide Community Equipment is celebrating a remarkable first year of helping essential equipment reach the people who need it.
Since launching in October 2025, the service, based in Greenford, West London, has demonstrated what a different approach to community equipment can achieve, combining increasingly reliable delivery with exceptional levels of equipment reuse to make public resources go further.
Behind every delivery is someone who needs equipment to support their daily life. Behind every collection is an opportunity to help someone else.
In its first 12 months, Provide Community Equipment delivered over 119,000 items of equipment, collected over 78,000 items and answered over 96,000 telephone calls, retaining more than £18.5 million in equipment value for its system partners.
By recovering equipment and returning suitable items to use, the service has reduced the need to purchase new stock, keeping valuable resources available to support communities.
Joe Coogan, Chief Operating Officer at Provide Community Equipment, said: “Equipment reuse has been central to the service’s success, exceeding the expectations set when the contract began delivering equipment into eight London Boroughs for North London Equipment Partnership.
“Together with wider operational efficiencies, this performance means £4 million is being refunded to the service’s eight council partner, a substantial financial benefit at a time when making the most of public funding matters more than ever.
“The results demonstrate the potential of a service designed around getting equipment to people efficiently, recovering it when it is no longer needed and helping it support someone else.”
Provide Community Equipment is part of Provide Community, an employee-owned community interest company, where social value and a focus on public benefit sits at the heart of the group’s approach.
Joe added: “Our one-year anniversary also marks an extraordinary achievement for the colleagues who built the service.
“Before mobilisation, there were no staff onboarded, no vans, no working IT system, no stock and no access to a warehouse. Within a year, the team had established an operation delivering more than 119,000 items of equipment, with on-time job completion performance at around 95% in recent months.
“Customer service has also strengthened, with calls now answered in less than 30 seconds on average, giving a better experience for prescribers and customers.
“Listening to customers continues to shape improvements. Following successful trials across six routes, guaranteed morning and afternoon appointment slots are being extended across the service, giving customers greater certainty about when to expect a visit.”
Jacqueline Garraway Commissioning Manager at North London Equipment Partnership, said: “The transformation across the Provide Community Equipment site this last year has been clear to see. Every area reflected strong teamwork, collaboration and a shared commitment to delivering an excellent community equipment service.”
Provide Community Equipment enters its second year with ambitions to build on this progress, strengthen service resilience and continue improving the customer experience.
Deliveries are forecast to reach 125,000 to 150,000 items during the second year, while the team’s experience is already attracting interest from other councils seeking to understand and learn from its approach.
For now, the first anniversary is an opportunity to recognise everyone who has made this progress possible: colleagues, commissioners and partners working together to help essential equipment support more people.
One year on, the results show the difference that commitment can make, for individuals, communities and the public resources they depend on.
Find out more about Provide Community Equipment on their website.

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Provide Community among first organisations to achieve Smokefree Employer Award
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
Provide Community has become one of the first organisations to achieve a new Smokefree Employer Award, recognising its commitment to supporting colleagues to stop smoking and improve their health and wellbeing.
The award was launched by Essex Working Well in April 2026 and recognises employers taking practical steps to prevent tobacco dependency and provide effective support for employees who want to become smokefree.
Provide Community achieved the award after demonstrating a range of measures already embedded across the organisation, including trained Very Brief Advice Advisors, regular workplace and digital health checks which record smoking status and clear pathways into specialist stop smoking support.
Importantly, the approach is already making a difference. Three Provide Community colleagues have so far successfully become smokefree with support from the organisation’s in-house NHS smoking cessation service.
The achievement has particular significance for Provide Community as the lead provider of Essex Wellbeing Service, which includes Essex Working Well and provides health and wellbeing support to employers across Essex.
Mark Heasman, Group Chief Executive at Provide Community, said: “Achieving the Smokefree Employer Award is a fantastic recognition of the work taking place across Provide Community to support the health and wellbeing of our colleagues.
“What matters most is the difference that support can make to individuals. We are particularly proud that three of our colleagues have already successfully become smokefree with support from our in-house service.
“As lead provider of Essex Wellbeing Service, we also have an opportunity to lead by example, putting into practice within our own organisation the preventative health and wellbeing approaches that we encourage and support other employers to adopt.”
The award supports wider national ambitions to create a smokefree generation and reduce the health impacts associated with tobacco use.
Provide Community will continue to build on its approach to workplace health and wellbeing, ensuring colleagues have access to information, advice and practical support to make positive changes to their health.
Organisations interested in working towards the Smokefree Employer Award or requesting a copy of the Smokefree Employer Toolkit can contact essex.workingwell@nhs.net .

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Essex Wellbeing Service and partners come together to make a difference along Clacton seafront
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Wellbeing Service Outreach Team joined forces with local partners for a community litter pick along Clacton seafront, demonstrating the positive impact that collaboration and volunteering can have on local communities.
Representatives from HCRG Care Group, Essex Child and Family Wellbeing Services, Age Well East, Rural Community Council of Essex (RCCE ) and Kinder Essex came together with the Essex Wellbeing Service Outreach Team, united by a shared commitment to making a positive difference to the local environment and helping to create cleaner, healthier communities. Tendring District Council supported the initiative by providing litter pickers and bags, enabling the group to get to work clearing litter from the seafront.
As the bags began to fill, participants were able to see the visible difference their collective efforts were making. The team’s hard work did not go unnoticed, with local residents, visitors and even members of the local lifeguard team stopping to thank the volunteers and comment on the improvement to the area.
Alongside the environmental benefits, the litter pick provided an opportunity for participants to spend time outdoors, get active, connect with others and enjoy the sense of achievement that comes from contributing to something positive.
Speaking about the event, Georgina Stokes, Service Manager of Essex Wellbeing Service Outreach Team, said: “It was fantastic to see so many of our local partners come together with a shared commitment to making a positive difference. While we could clearly see the impact we had made on the seafront, the benefits of the day went much further than collecting litter.
“Getting outdoors, being active, connecting with others and doing something positive for the community are all important for our wellbeing. The event was a brilliant example of what can be achieved through collaboration and how volunteering can create genuine social value, bringing people together around a shared purpose while helping to create cleaner, healthier places for everyone to enjoy.”
The litter pick is a great example of social value in action, with organisations working together to deliver benefits that extend beyond their day-to-day services. By giving their time to improve a shared community space, participants helped enhance the local environment while strengthening relationships between partner organisations and the communities they support.
The event also highlighted the wider value of volunteering and how even relatively simple actions can have a meaningful impact. Whether improving a local environment, supporting wellbeing or creating stronger connections between people, volunteering can help transform communities and encourage others to play their part.
Through partnership working and a shared commitment to improving wellbeing, Essex Wellbeing Service and its local partners continue to look for opportunities to make a positive difference to the communities they serve.

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Suffolk Sexual Health Service launches new learning offer for Sexual Health Week 2026
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
Suffolk Sexual Health Service is supporting Sexual Health Week 2026 (Monday 14 to 20 September), encouraging people across Suffolk to connect, communicate and feel more confident talking about sexual health and relationships.
This year’s theme, ‘Let’s Connect’, highlights the importance of meaningful human connection, from our relationships with others to understanding our own bodies, emotions and needs.
To mark the week, Suffolk Sexual Health Service will launch a new sexual health eLearning platform, providing an accessible and free way for professionals across Suffolk, including those working with young people and those in public facing roles where sexual health and relationships may be discussed to build their knowledge and confidence around all things Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE).
The platform will consist of a variety of different courses and modules, with the first course available being ‘Sex, Consent and Confidentiality’. The service will then release a new learning course each month, including modules on areas such as ‘growing up in an online world, ‘pornography vs real life intimate relationships’ and ‘contraception and sexually transmitted infections.
The Outreach and Education Team will also be out and about across the county throughout the week engaging with students and young people to raise awareness of the week and ensure that people know how to access local sexual health and other relevant services.
Jessica Kirby, Outreach and Education Service Lead at Suffolk Sexual Health Service, said: “Sexual Health Week is a valuable opportunity to encourage more open conversations about sexual health and relationships and to remind people that support is available.
“Connection can mean many different things, from communicating with a partner and understanding our own needs, to feeling confident asking questions or reaching out for support when we need it.
“We want people across Suffolk to know that sexual health is an important part of our overall health and wellbeing, and that our team is here to provide confidential, non-judgemental advice and support.”
During Sexual Health Week, the service will be sharing information and resources across its digital channels, helping to challenge stigma and make conversations about sexual health and relationships feel more normal.
Suffolk Sexual Health Service is commissioned by Suffolk County Council and delivered by Provide Community, an employee-owned Community Interest Company delivering health and social care services.

https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.title: Essex Sexual Health Service launches new learning offer for Sexual Health Week 2026
https://providecommunity.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Sexual Health Service is supporting Sexual Health Week 2026 (Monday 14 to Sunday 20 September) by encouraging people across Essex to connect, communicate and feel more confident talking about sexual health and relationships.
This year’s national theme, ‘Let’s Connect’, explores the importance of meaningful human connection, from our relationships with others to understanding our own bodies, emotions and needs.
To mark the week, Essex Sexual Health Service has launched a new sexual health eLearning platform, providing an accessible and free way for professionals across Essex, including those working with young people and those in public facing roles where sexual health and relationships may be discussed to build their knowledge and confidence around all things Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE).
The platform will offer a range of courses made up of short, accessible modules. The first course, ‘Sex, Consent and Confidentiality’, will be available for users to access from September.
A new course will then be released each month. Future courses will include ‘Growing Up in an Online World’, which will include modules on pornography vs. real-life intimate relationships, online sexual harms, and the impact of AI and deepfakes.
Another course, ‘STIs, Contraception and Local Sexual Health Services’, will include modules focusing on the causes, treatment and prevention of STIs; contraception, including LARC and emergency contraception; and signposting to local sexual health services.
The service will also host its first live broadcast this September, providing educational settings across Essex to join live RSHE sessions delivered by the Essex Sexual Health Service. Students will be given the opportunity to submit anonymous questions and have these answered in real time by the presenter using the online platform ‘Ask Provide’.
The new digital learning offer forms part of the service’s wider commitment to making reliable sexual health information easier to access and supporting people across Essex to have open, informed conversations about their sexual health and wellbeing.
The Essex Sexual Health Service Outreach and Education Team will be visiting education settings this week, promoting the national awareness week.
Paige Evans, RSHE and Coproduction Coordinator at Essex Sexual Health Service, said: “Sexual Health Week is a great opportunity to get people talking about sexual health, relationships and wellbeing, and this year’s theme of connection really reflects the work we do across Essex.
“We are particularly excited to launch our new eLearning platform and our first live broadcast during the week. We want to make it easier for people to access trusted information, build their knowledge and feel more confident having conversations about sexual health.
“Sexual health is about much more than preventing sexually transmitted infections. It’s about consent, communication and how these support healthy relationships and self-confidence, as well as having the skills and knowledge to make informed choices that are right for you.”
Essex Sexual Health Service is commissioned by Essex County Council and delivered by Provide Community, providing sexual health support including STI testing and treatment, contraception, education, outreach and health promotion across the county.

https://cmsm.co.uk/feed.title: Zeppelins Over Essex: The Night the L32 and L33 Fell
https://cmsm.co.uk/feed.text:
Marking the 110th Anniversary of 23 rd and 24 th  September 1916
On the night of 24 September 1916 , the skies over Essex were lit by searchlights, tracer fire, and the glow of burning hydrogen. Two German airships — Zeppelin L32 and Zeppelin L33 — crossed the county on what would become their final missions. Today, 110 years later, their story still echoes across the villages where these giants of the air came down.
Combined Military Services Museum is marking the 110 th anniversary of the L32 and L33 Zeppelin crashes which took place over the night of 23 rd and 24 th September 1916 with a special display of  artefacts and souvenirs from these events, which led to the deaths of one crew, and the capture and imprisonment of the other, in the only known example of an enemy military force marching through England, during either world war.
Why Zeppelins Came to Britain
By 1916, the First World War had reached a brutal stalemate. Germany sought new ways to strike at Britain’s morale and industry. Under Korvettenkapitän Peter Strasser , the Imperial German Navy deployed long‑range Zeppelins to bomb towns and cities across the country. These “super‑Zeppelins” were extraordinary machines:
650 feet long ,
built from lightweight duralumin ,
lifted by millions of cubic feet of hydrogen ,
capable of flying above most British defences.
They were intended to be unstoppable.
The L32: Shot Down Over Great Burstead : A Mission Interrupted
The Zeppelin L32, commanded by Oberleutnant zur See Werner Peterson, crossed the Channel aiming for London. Searchlights and anti‑aircraft fire forced it off course, and it dropped bombs near Aveley and South Ockenden.
The Attack
Two Royal Flying Corps aircraft intercepted the airship. Second Lieutenant Frederick Sowrey fired into the mid‑section, igniting the hydrogen. The L32 became a blazing fireball, falling near Snail’s Hall Farm, Great Burstead. All 22 crew members were killed.
Local resident Frederick Rayner saw the burning airship pass low over Billericay High Street. He reached the wreckage first, helping to lay out the bodies in a nearby barn — later known as Dead Men’s Barn . The crew were buried at Great Burstead Churchyard, later reinterred at Cannock Chase German Military Cemetery.
The L33: Crash Landing at Little Wigborough: A Damaged Airship Over Essex
The L33, commanded by Kapitän‑Leutnant Alois Bocker, carried out a separate raid over Upminster, Hornchurch, Woolwich, and West Ham. Damaged by ground fire and losing gas rapidly, the crew threw out ballast, equipment, and weapons — many later found in gardens across Essex.
The Crash Landing
Shortly after midnight, the L33 crash‑landed near Little Wigborough, blocking the lane to the church and narrowly missing nearby homes. The crew set the airship alight to prevent British capture.
A Remarkable Surrender
In an extraordinary moment in British history, Bocker and his 21 crewmen marched in formation through local lanes seeking a boat. They were intercepted by Special Constable Edgar Nicholas, joined by other officers including PC Charles Smith, who later received a medal for his handling of the situation.
The crew were held overnight in West Mersea Church Hall — believed to be the only time a hostile force marched in formation on British soil during either World War.
Local Memories and Lasting Impact
The crash sites drew thousands of visitors. Children picked blackberries beside the fallen airship; families retrieved small souvenirs; and one local doctor even suggested naming a newborn baby “Zeppelina.”
For Essex communities, the events of that night brought the global conflict directly into quiet rural parishes. For Britain, the destruction of L32 and L33 marked a turning point: improved aircraft and defences made Zeppelin raids increasingly dangerous and ultimately unsustainable.
Further Reading
British Airships 1903–1930 — Ian Castle
The End of Zeppelin L33 — Douglas J. Gurton
The Last Flight of the L32 — R. L. Rimell
The Fate of Zeppelin L32

https://cmsm.co.uk/feed.title: Combined Military Services Museum Secures Rare Replacement Victoria Cross Linked to Maldon Hero
https://cmsm.co.uk/feed.text:
The Combined Military Services Museum is proud to announce the acquisition of a rare replacement Victoria Cross believed to have been made for Maldon-born VC recipient Frederick Corbett, also known by his birth name, David Embleton. The medal, now sits alongside Corbett’s Snider Mk III cavalry carbine, purchased by the museum in 2017, bringing together two remarkable artefacts from a turbulent and extraordinary life.
David Embleton was born in Maldon on 17 September 1853, one of thirteen children. By the age of seventeen he had joined the 23rd Essex Rifle Volunteers, and in 1872 he enlisted in the Royal Regiment of Artillery. Although his conduct was described as “very good,” his health deteriorated rapidly. After only five years he was pensioned off with chronic bronchitis and a persistent cough, later labelled tuberculosis. Yet this diagnosis may have been mistaken, as Embleton soon re-enlisted under a false identity: Frederick Corbett of the 60th Rifles, later the King’s Royal Rifle Corps.
It was under this assumed name that Corbett earned the Victoria Cross. During the 1882 Egyptian campaign, at Kafr Dowar, he displayed exceptional bravery when Lieutenant Howard Vyse fell mortally wounded under heavy fire. Corbett remained beside him, attempting to stem the bleeding, and later helped carry him from the field, an action that earned him Britain’s highest award for gallantry.
Health problems again interrupted his service, and as a decorated soldier he was transferred to the newly formed Military Foot Police and promoted to corporal. But after leaving the Army in 1883, Corbett’s life began to unravel. Struggling financially, he sold his Victoria Cross for just 15 guineas. Within months he re-enlisted once more, this time accepted as a Driver in the Royal Horse Artillery. He returned to Egypt in 1884, and earned further campaign honours. Known to wear a replacement VC, he may have crafted the replica himself, drawing on his training as a tinsmith, or it may have been made by his ironmonger brother Joseph.
Corbett’s later years were marked by repeated disciplinary issues, imprisonment, and eventual medical discharge in 1891. Today his behaviour might be recognised as consistent with PTSD, but in the nineteenth century such conditions were poorly understood. Returning to Maldon under his birth name, he drifted into destitution, repeatedly appearing in court for minor offences. In 1904 he was jailed for breaking a window at the War Office in an apparent attempt to reclaim his lost VC. He died in Maldon Workhouse in 1912 and was buried in a pauper’s grave, receiving a military headstone only in 2004.
Corbett’s original Victoria Cross is now held by the Royal Green Jackets (Rifles) Museum, though questions remain about its authenticity. Another copy was once recorded in the Royal Artillery collection.
Bringing this piece home to Maldon allows the museum to honour a local man whose courage was undeniable, even as his life took a tragic and troubled path.

CMSM has been proud to take part in a new series on Sky History, Battle Treasures with our patron Bruce Crompton, and SAS hero Jason Fox.
Battle Treasures tells the stories behind some of the rarest and most remarkable military artefacts ever discovered. Hosted by Jason Fox and Bruce Crompton, each episode explores three extraordinary items – revealing their provenance, the battlefield stories behind them, and little-known facts to bring each object to life. Bruce brings his encyclopaedic knowledge to each item while Jason draws on his experience as one of Britain’s most elite soldiers to offer vivid, first-hand context. The series also delivers world firsts, revealing artefacts never seen by the public.
This week’s episode featured our 10th Century Maldon Sword, found locally and believed to be a relic from the famous Battle of Maldon in 991.
10th century Maldon Sword (c) Combined Military Services Museum
With more episodes to come some of our other items will be featured and we are so excited to have been part of the program.
For more information see Battle Treasures with Foxy and Bruce | Sky HISTORY TV Channel

https://saffronscreen.com/feed/.title: Saffron Screen needs your help.
https://saffronscreen.com/feed/.text:
You may not know that Saffron Screen is a charity. We’ve been one since 2006, run from a school hall by a small team of part-time staff and nearly 50 local volunteers.
This year, we’ve been celebrating 20 years of Saffron Screen .
From our earliest screenings to our birthday celebrations this summer, thousands of people have come through our doors to enjoy great films, live performances and the shared experience of cinema.
DONATE NOW
But 2026 has also been a tough year for us.
Our day-to-day costs have continued to rise and, in the middle of it all, our projector failed. It was 15 years old and we had no choice but to replace it. It was the only decision we could make, but it has left us with a hole that ticket sales cannot fill.
It costs us around £800 to put on a single film, our screenings aren’t always full and a high percentage of every ticket sold goes directly to the film distributor.
Ticket sales matter enormously, but they aren’t enough on their own. That’s why we depend so heavily on the support of our wonderful community and supporters to keep us going.
So, we’re asking for your help to raise £50,000.
£5 could help us switch the lights on
£10 could help bring a big-screen experience to our community
£25 could help us maintain our projection equipment
£50 could help us design, print and distribute our monthly programme and posters
£200  could help towards specialist equipment such as captioning glasses, making our cinema more accessible
£800 could cover the average cost of putting on a film at Saffron Screen.
It’s an ambitious target, but every donation will take us closer.
If you are a UK taxpayer, Gift Aid adds 25p to every £1 you donate, at no extra cost to you.
We have a plan to maintain Saffron Screen’s future, but we need our community behind us to put it into practice.
Donate. Every contribution makes a difference.
Come to the cinema. Every ticket matters.
Become a Member. Regular support helps us plan ahead
Spread the word. Tell your friends and family that Saffron Screen is a charity and share our appeal.
DONATE NOW
Thank you in advance,
From all of us at Saffron Screen

Saturday 11th April – 7:00 pm
Book Now
Sinners Ryan Coogler’s atmospheric epic made history this year with a record-breaking 16 Oscar nominations. It dominated the technical and acting categories, proving that genre filmmaking can be high art.
Oscar Wins: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography.
BAFTA Wins: Best Supporting Actress (Wunmi Mosaku), Best Original Screenplay.
Golden Globe Wins: Best Original Score, Cinematic and Box Office Achievement.
Saturday 4th April – 7:30 pm
Book Now
Hamnet A “Triple Crown” year for Jessie Buckley! Her portrayal of Agnes Shakespeare was the performance of the year, earning her the Lead Actress trophy at every major ceremony.
Oscar Win: Best Actress (Jessie Buckley).
BAFTA Win: Outstanding British Film, Best Leading Actress.
Golden Globe Win: Best Motion Picture (Drama), Best Actress.
Sunday 5th April – 7:30 pm
Book Now
Global Gems & Homegrown Heroes
Sentimental Value The international sensation from Norway that has charmed critics worldwide. It’s a nuanced look at family and fame that deserves every bit of its success.

BAFTA Win: Best Film Not in the English Language.
Golden Globe Win: Best Supporting Actor (Stellan Skarsgård).
Sunday 12th April – 7:30 pm
Book Now

Tuesday 7th April – 7:30 pm
Book Now

Golden Globe Wins: Best Foreign Language Film, Best Actor – Drama (Wagner Moura).
Monday 6th April – 7:00 pm
Book Now
Marty Supreme Timothée Chalamet’s electric, stylish performance as a 1950s ping-pong pro was a standout of the season.
Golden Globe Win: Best Actor – Musical or Comedy (Timothée Chalamet).
Thursday 9th April – 7:00 pm

There is a unique magic in watching an Oscar-winning performance or a Best Picture winner in a room full of fellow film lovers. Whether it’s the pin-drop silence during a dramatic moment in Hamnet or the breathtaking visuals of Sinners , these films were designed for the big screen.

https://metalculture.com/feed/.title: The Unlonely City and Ten Years Since Olivia Laing’s The Lonely City
https://metalculture.com/feed/.text:
The Unlonely City , Metal’s programme of gatherings, celebrations and citizen-led initiatives, was born from the belief that we need ways to come together.
So far, it’s involved 20 artists and 70 local people shaping what matters to them, plus nine initiatives to disrupt loneliness across Liverpool, Peterborough and Southend.
Ten years ago, Olivia Laing wrote The Lonely City , an exploration through art of the loneliness they found in New York City. This month, to mark the launch of the book’s tenth-anniversary edition, Olivia Laing will join writer and curator Charlie Porter to discuss art, solitude and the relevance of the book ten years on. You can get tickets here .
“Loneliness is personal, and it is also political. Loneliness is collective; it is a city.” Olivia Laing
The title The Lonely City inspired the name of our programme, and it still resonates. Loneliness isn’t just an individual feeling; it’s shaped by the conditions we live in – housing, work, inequality, technology, public space and the loss of places where people can gather and belong.
We recently read Octavia Butler’s The Book of Martha in our anti-racist book club, where the idea of utopias, and the challenges of creating a universal utopia, sit at the heart of the story. We came away asking: What is your utopia? Could it work? Who would it work for? Who wouldn’t it work for?
An ‘unlonely’ city in Liverpool, Peterborough and Southend, where Metal is based, is one of our utopias. So far, we’ve had fun making scouse with a scouser, uncovering the magic left behind in art lockers, sharing banquets of hope, spinning yarns and watching a photography series develop among strangers. These moments of laughter, connection and unexpected joy, remind us that even small, surprise acts of gathering can begin to disrupt loneliness.
“A sense of lingering like the feeling of those conversations you have by the front door, when one of you is about to leave and you stay there for ages, and it means the most because it wasn’t meant to be a special moment but it really was and now it’s gone and you’ve hugged goodbye and closed the front door and one of you walks away smiling and the other pauses behind the front door savouring the moment.” – Luca Rutherford, The Unlonely City Power and Cultural Democracy Commission
We look forward to more moments like this.

https://metalculture.com/feed/.title: 10 Years of Connect & Create: Celebrating Creativity, Connection & Wellbeing
https://metalculture.com/feed/.text:
May marks both Mental Health Awareness Week and Dementia Action Week, making it a fitting time to reflect on 10 years of  Connect & Create   –   our creative wellbeing programme.
Since launching in 2016,  Connect & Create  has reached  more than 2000 people  across Southend, including people living with dementia, survivors of trauma, and those experiencing mental health challenges, through inclusive therapeutic arts practice, nurturing healing, confidence and joy through creativity.
Image credit: Anna Lukala
Image credit: Anna Lukala
A Decade of Impact
Over the last ten years, Connect & Create has delivered more than  25,500 hours of support , across over  100 groups , reaching  2,194 people .
This year alone,  49% of participants said they had reduced the use of crisis teams  or NHS and GP mental health services, with visits falling from 175 total visits before participation to 90 total visits afterwards.
Reflecting on the programme’s impact, Warren Harper, our Director of Southend said:
“Over the last decade, people in our community have been facing growing and complex mental health challenges. During this time, Connect & Create and its legacy has shown how the arts can play a crucial role in strengthening mental wellbeing at a time when such resilience is needed most.
We’re proud to be working with Southend City Council to provide free, safe and accessible sessions to strengthen connection and community, and it is much needed work I hope we can continue doing for the next ten years.”
Reflecting on the Programme
At its heart, the programme aims to be a welcoming space for people facing a wide range of challenges. As part of this anniversary year, we invited participants to reflect on what creativity and connection mean to them.
Mental Wellbeing Coordinator Emma Mills and Class Facilitator Ian Wilson spoke with some of the  Connect & Create  participants about how creative spaces can help people feel understood, valued and connected.
Connections through Creativity
Participants described the programme as a place where they can connect, feel safe and a sense of community.
“Connect & Create is like a big day out for me. It makes me feel a part and included, and like I am an artist rather than a person with ‘issues’. People talk about what’s important to them, and other times it goes very quiet as we get into our artwork. It makes me feel whole.”
“It makes me feel exposed but not in a bad way. I feel like I’m showing parts of myself that I would normally keep hidden and growing in confidence. I don’t have to hide here.”
Creativity without Pressure
Participants spoke passionately about the freedom and encouragement they experience through making art together in the sessions.
“What I like most about the art I create is that it doesn’t have to be ‘perfect’, but it’s appreciated.”
“It connects art, nature and local history to create a true sense of place and connection with others.”
Emma Mills, Art Psychotherapist, Mental Wellbeing Facilitator and our Connect & Create Coordinator said:
“We warmly welcome anyone facing mental health challenges—whether you’re feeling anxious, low, lonely, or simply in need of a safe space to breathe. Through the therapeutic power of creativity, we offer opportunities to reconnect with yourself, create meaningful artwork, build new friendships and enjoy the moment.”
Thank you to everyone who has been part of  Connect & Create  over the last decade and everyone who has supported the programme. A special thank you to the participants who generously shared their experiences with us.
If you’re interested in joining us or referring someone, we’d love to hear from you. Learn more  here .

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Clacton Airshow dates revealed for 2027
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
Clacton Airshow will return to the skies in 2027, with organisers confirming the dates as Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August.
The announcement follows another spectacular year for the seafront show, which once again brought fast jets, historic warbirds, twilight pyrotechnics and family entertainment to the Essex Sunshine Coast.
This year’s event marked Clacton Airshow’s 33rd year and celebrated the very best of aviation, entertainment and community spirit along Clacton’s seafront.
From the precision of the RAF Red Arrows to the sight and sound of Sally B, Spitfire MH434, the MiG-17F ‘Fresco’ and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, the 2026 flying programme delivered memorable moments for every generation of airshow fan.
The popular twilight display also provided a dramatic finale to the first day, while the West Greensward Airshow Village added to the festival atmosphere with exhibitors, traders, activities and attractions for visitors on the ground.
Organised by Tendring District Council (TDC), the free event remains one of the district’s biggest summer attractions and is estimated to be worth more than £12million to the local economy.
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism, said: “Clacton Airshow has just given us another brilliant reminder of what makes this event so special for our district.
“For two days, the seafront was full of people enjoying world-class flying displays, family entertainment and the atmosphere that only Clacton Airshow can create.
“It brings visitors into the heart of the Essex Sunshine Coast, supports businesses, showcases our seafront and creates shared memories for residents, families and visitors.
“That success is down to a huge team effort, and I would like to thank everyone who helped make this year’s show happen, from council staff and emergency services to sponsors, partners, traders, volunteers and everyone who supported the event.
“With the dates now confirmed for 2027, we can start looking ahead to welcoming people back for another unforgettable two days on Clacton seafront.”
Clacton Airshow 2027 will take place on Thursday 26 and Friday 27 August. To help keep the show in the skies, donations are welcomed via the official website at clactonairshow.com.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Everything you need to know about this week’s Clacton Airshow 2026 – As last flight revealed!
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
The countdown is on the biggest date in the Essex Sunshine Coast calendar, as Clacton Airshow prepares to return with two days of thrilling flying displays, ground attractions and family entertainment.
Staged by Tendring District Council (TDC), the 33rd Clacton Airshow takes place on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August, bringing together new aerobatic displays, much-loved heritage aircraft, classic jet noise, hands-on attractions and firm seafront favourites.
This year’s theme, A Celebration of Aviation, will be reflected across the programme, from iconic RAF displays and historic aircraft to modern aerobatics, STEM activities and live event coverage for visitors on the ground and those following from further afield.
A bonus flight has been unveiled today (Monday, 24 August) coming from G-Force Aerobatics, with pilot Chris Burkett really demonstrating that Celebration of Aviation.
Among the headline acts on the Clacton Airshow line-up will be the world-famous RAF Red Arrows, who will perform on both days, while the RAF Battle of Britain Memorial Flight will also return to the skies in the year marking the 90th anniversary of the Spitfire’s first flight.
The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight display is currently expected to feature a combination of the Spitfire, Hurricane and C-47 Dakota, subject to operational availability, offering visitors a powerful living tribute to British aviation history.
A classic Cold War-era jet will also bring speed, sound and spectacle to the seafront, with the MiG-17F ‘Fresco’ joining the flying programme. The aircraft is due to appear in both the Thursday evening twilight display and Friday’s daytime display.
Fresh displays for 2026 include The Starlings, a two-aircraft aerobatic team flown by former British Aerobatic Champions Tom Cassells and Michael Pickin.
They will be joined by the Flying Comrades, a Duxford-based three-ship Yak display team making its Clacton debut, combining disciplined close-formation work with smoke-filled aerobatic manoeuvres.
Returning favourites include the Bronco Demo Team’s distinctive OV-10 Bronco, Friday-only appearance P-51D Mustang ‘Moonbeam McSwine’, Spitfire MH434 and the Strikemaster Pair, adding further variety, heritage and classic jet noise to the flying line-up.
The RAF Grob Tutor T1 will also return, highlighting the training aircraft used to teach the next generation of RAF pilots, while the RAF Careers Engagement team will be on the West Greensward event site with a replica Typhoon cockpit and Batak reaction challenge.
Visitors will be able to step aboard the replica cockpit for a pilot’s-eye view of one of the RAF’s most advanced fighter jets, while the Batak reaction game will offer a fast-paced test of the reflexes used in high-pressure aviation environments.
On Thursday evening, the popular twilight display will return with a refreshed programme sponsored by Red Nova IT Solutions, blending heritage aircraft, high-energy aerobatics and pyrotechnics against the backdrop of Clacton seafront.
This year’s twilight line-up, sponsored by RedNova IT Solutions, will include Otto the Helicopter, the Firebirds Aerobatic Team, the Desert Spitfire and the MiG-17, bringing a spectacular mix of pyrotechnics, aerobatics and classic aircraft to the evening slot.
Actual Radio has been named as the official radio broadcast partner for Clacton Airshow 2026, with dedicated programming across both days from the Essex Sunshine Coast.
Radio Airshow will be available across multiple platforms for the first time, with listeners able to ask their smart speaker to “Play Radio Airshow”, stream through the free Actual Radio app, or listen online through the Actual Radio website by clicking the Radio Airshow button.
Other display sponsors include Actual Radio for the Flying Comrades’ three Yak aircraft, LocaliQ for the Strikemaster Pair, Black Jacket for the Bronco, Fisher Jones Greenwood LLP for The Starlings, and MRL Productions for Spitfire MH434.
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC

With Clacton Airshow now just days away, organisers have announced that one of the most famous Spitfires still flying today will join this year’s line-up, alongside an exciting programme of ground attractions on the Essex Sunshine Coast.

Spitfire MH434, sponsored by MRL Productions, is set to make a special appearance at the free seafront event, giving crowds the chance to see a true icon of British aviation with a remarkable wartime and display flying history.
Built at Vickers-Armstrong’s Castle Bromwich factory in 1943, MH434 first flew in the hands of celebrated test pilot Alex Henshaw before entering frontline service with 222 Squadron. The aircraft went on to complete 79 operational sorties during the Second World War and later became a familiar sight on screen in films including Operation Crossbow, Battle of Britain and A Bridge Too Far.
Visitors to the West Greensward Airshow site will have the chance to get up close to aviation technology and learn more about careers in the industry, with the RAF Careers Engagement team bringing a replica Typhoon cockpit and the RAF’s popular Batak reaction challenge.
The interactive attraction will allow visitors to step into the cockpit of one of the RAF’s most advanced fighter aircraft and test the reflexes needed in high-pressure aviation environments.
The RAF will also be represented on the ground with RAF Careers displays and aviation exhibits, while the flying programme will include the RAF Grob Tutor T1, the aircraft used to train the next generation of RAF pilots.
Alongside the aviation attractions, visitors can enjoy a wide range of trade stands, exhibitors and food concessions across the event site, with local and regional traders including Colchester-based Whippy Bro’s, Clacton-based Spud Box and Vintage Shakes among those serving visitors.

Actual Radio, the official radio broadcast partner of Clacton Airshow 2026, will also be broadcasting live throughout the event, bringing commentary, interviews, music and behind-the-scenes insight from the heart of the action.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Brand New Flights and Crowd Favourites Join Exciting Line-up for Clacton Airshow 2026
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
Brand new displays and returning crowd favourites have been added to this year’s Clacton Airshow, completing an exciting flying line-up over the Essex Sunshine Coast.
The 33rd Clacton Airshow, staged by Tendring District Council (TDC), takes place on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August, with the latest announcement bringing together new aerobatic displays, much-loved heritage aircraft, classic jet noise and firm seafront favourites.
Making their Clacton debut will be The Starlings, a two-aircraft aerobatic team flown by former British Aerobatic Champions Tom Cassells and Michael Pickin, and the Turbulent ‘Turb’ Team, who bring colourful, close-in formation flying in tiny Druine D.31 Turbulent aircraft.
They will be joined by the return of the Bronco Demo Team, an airshow favourite whose distinctive OV-10 Bronco is known for its unusual shape, strong manoeuvrability and short take-off and landing performance.
Bronco Demo Team Image Paul Johnson Flightline UK
The iconic Second World War-era P-51D Mustang ‘Moonbeam McSwine’ will also return to Clacton on the Friday following its twilight debut last year, as well as the Strikemaster Pair, adding more classic jet noise to the seafront programme.
The Starlings’ fast-paced routine combines close formation work, opposition manoeuvres, rolls, loops, stall turns and dramatic solo figures, giving spectators plenty to follow and photographers some striking moments over the coastline.
Tom flies the modern Extra 300NG, while Michael flies the classic CAP 232, creating a contrasting pairing of next-generation carbon-fibre aerobatic design and world championship-level display pedigree.
The Turbulent Team offers a very different style of entertainment, with its small, single-seat aircraft bringing charm, character and playful low-level theatre to the display alongside neat formation work and the barnstorming spirit of vintage sport aviation.
The Bronco Demo Team’s OV-10 Bronco, developed in the 1960s as a light attack and observation aircraft, remains one of the most recognisable aircraft on the display circuit, with its twin-boom layout, greenhouse-style cockpit and rugged design.
The Strikemaster Pair will add another burst of jet energy to the programme, with the classic BAC 167 Strikemaster expected to bring speed, sound and fast-jet theatre to the seafront.
The latest flights are supported by airshow sponsors, with Fisher Jones Greenwood sponsoring The Starlings, The Lifehouse Spa & Hotel sponsoring the Turbulent ‘Turb’ Team, Black Jacket sponsoring the Bronco, and LocaliQ sponsoring the Strikemaster Pair.
Councillor Mark Stephenson, Leader of TDC, said: “This final round of flight announcements captures what makes Clacton Airshow so special and a true Celebration of Aviation.
“There is great contrast in this line-up, from tight aerobatics and playful formation flying to heritage aircraft, distinctive display favourites and the unmistakable sound of classic jets.
“It is the kind of mix that keeps people looking up throughout the day, whether they are lifelong aviation fans or families enjoying the airshow from the beach for the first time.
“With the flying programme now coming together in full, excitement is building for what promises to be a fantastic two days on the Essex Sunshine Coast.”
The new additions join an already impressive flying line-up, including the world-famous RAF Red Arrows, the RAF Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, the Flying Comrades, the MiG-17F ‘Fresco’ and a refreshed twilight programme.
Clacton Airshow is the biggest event on the Essex Sunshine Coast calendar, attracting tens of thousands of visitors each year, with flying displays, ground attractions, food stalls and family-friendly entertainment along the seafront.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Historic MiG Fighter Jet to bring Cold War Roar to Clacton Airshow 2026
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
A classic Cold War-era jet fighter is set to bring speed, noise and spectacle to the skies above Clacton seafront this summer.
The MiG-17F ‘Fresco’ will join the flying line-up for the 33rd Clacton Airshow, staged by Tendring District Council (TDC) on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August.
The aircraft will appear in both the Thursday evening twilight display and Friday’s daytime programme, giving visitors two chances to experience one of aviation’s most distinctive historic jets.
Developed from the earlier MiG-15 and introduced in the early 1950s, the MiG-17F was designed for speed, climb performance and manoeuvrability, with swept wings, an afterburning engine and powerful nose-mounted cannons.
The aircraft displaying at Clacton carries side number 1211 and was built in Mielec, Poland, in 1958 as a Lim-5, the Polish licence-built version of the MiG-17F.
After service with the Polish Air Force, the aircraft returned to the skies in April this year following an extensive two-and-a-half-year restoration by FUBAR Aviation.
Its display is expected to feature aerobatics and low passes at speeds of up to 900km/h, with the aircraft pulling around 6–7G during its routine.
Councillor Mark Stephenson, TDC Leader, said: “The MiG-17F will be a real standout moment at this year’s Clacton Airshow, bringing a very different kind of sound, speed and atmosphere to the seafront.
“To see this historic jet flying in the Thursday twilight display will be something really special, and I am sure it will make a big impression on residents and visitors watching from the beach and greensward.
“This year’s theme is all about celebrating aviation, and the MiG is another exciting addition to what is shaping up to be a fantastic two days on the Essex Sunshine Coast.”
The MiG will be displayed by experienced display and airline pilot Bartosz Maciejczyk, chief executive of FUBAR Aviatio, who has accumulated more than 15,000 flying hours.
Based at Olsztyn-Mazury Airport in Poland, FUBAR operates the MiG-17F alongside other MiG aircraft, helping to keep these remarkable jets flying for future generations to enjoy.
The new display adds to an already impressive flying line-up, including the world-famous RAF Red Arrows, performing across both days, as well as the RAF Battle of Britain Memorial Flight and the refreshed twilight flights.
Clacton Airshow is the biggest events on the Essex Sunshine Coast calendar, attracting tens of thousands of visitors each year, with flying displays, ground attractions, food stalls and family-friendly entertainment along the seafront.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: High Court Order Secured to Help Protect Clacton Airshow from Unauthorised Camping
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
A High Court injunction has been granted to help keep this year’s Clacton Airshow running safely and smoothly by preventing unauthorised camping in designated seafront areas.
Tendring District Council (TDC), which organises the popular annual event, successfully applied for the order at the High Court of Justice in London last week (29 July).
The injunction will be in place from 00.01am on Thursday, 20 August, through to 11.59pm on Saturday, 5 September, and covers specified areas in Clacton.
It applies to anyone intending to park or place a caravan, campervan, mobile home or tent on the land or roads shown in the order’s schedule and plans.
The order prohibits all forms of camping, including overnight camping, within the restricted zones during the airshow period.
Anyone who breaches the injunction could face contempt of court proceedings, which may result in a fine, imprisonment or the seizure of assets.
The injunction, granted jointly to TDC and Essex County Council, follows similar orders secured in previous years and remains an important measure in supporting the safe delivery of the event.
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC’s Cabinet Member for Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism, said: “Clacton Airshow is a much-loved event which attracts huge crowds to our seafront and provides a real boost for the district.
“With so many people coming into the town, it is important we take sensible steps to protect the event site and keep key routes and public spaces clear.
“This injunction is a practical measure which has worked well in previous years, helping to prevent unauthorised camping and reduce the risk of disruption during the airshow period.
“Our aim is to make sure residents, visitors and businesses can enjoy the event safely, while helping everyone make the most of what promises to be another fantastic Clacton Airshow.”
The sites covered by the injunction include land on the south side of Marine Parade West from Clacton Pier to Collingwood Road, as well as the Martello Bay area.
Seafront roads covered include Hastings Avenue, between West Road and Selsey Avenue; Marine Parade West; and West Road, between the junction with Marine Parade West/Wash Lane and Hastings Avenue.
Car park land covered includes the Hastings Avenue, Hastings Bay and Martello Coach and Car Park sites.
Full details of the injunction and a schedule of the areas covered will be added to TDC’s website at https://www.tendringdc.gov.uk/airshow-injunction-2026 .
Airshow organisers have already revealed a host of aircraft that will be taking to the skies on Thursday, 27 August, and Friday, 28 August, including the RAF Red Arrows and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, as well as the return of the popular twilight display on the Thursday evening.
For updates and more information on the 2026 Clacton Airshow, people should visit  www.clactonairshow.com , follow  @clactonairshow  on X, or go to  the official Facebook event .

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Flying Comrades to bring Close-formation Aerobatics to Clacton Airshow 2026
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
A new display team is set to make its Clacton Airshow debut this summer, bringing close-formation flying, smoke trails and aerobatic skill to the Essex Sunshine Coast.
The Flying Comrades, a Duxford-based three-ship Yak display team, will join the line-up for the 33rd Clacton Airshow, staged by Tendring District Council (TDC) on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August.
Now in their fifth year together, the team is made up of friends brought together by a shared love of flying, with the word ‘comrade’ meaning friend at the heart of their name.
Their display will feature one Yak-18T and two Yak-52 aircraft, combining disciplined close-formation work with smoke-filled aerobatic manoeuvres in a distinctive routine over Clacton seafront.
The team has previously displayed at events including Blackpool, Old Buckenham and IWM Duxford, and will add another fresh element to this year’s flying programme.
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism, said: “It is fantastic to welcome the Flying Comrades to Clacton Airshow for the first time, adding another exciting new act to what is shaping up to be a brilliant programme.
“Their display is all about teamwork, precision and the joy of flying, and I am sure visitors will enjoy seeing these three distinctive aircraft working together above our seafront.
“Clacton Airshow is always about giving residents and visitors something memorable to enjoy, and this new display will help bring even more colour, variety and atmosphere to the Essex Sunshine Coast this August.”
Leading the formation will be Phil Hardisty in the Yak-18T G-HAHU, supported by Alex Lewton in the yellow and black Yak-52 G-BXJB and Tom Turner in the silver and red Yak-52 G-YAKF.
Phil, who established the Flying Comrades, is a professional pilot who has been flying since childhood and has several years of display flying experience, including with Clive Denney’s Red Sparrows team.
Alex, also a commercial pilot, first flew a Yak-52 in 2007 and is now in his fourth year of display flying, while Tom, Head of Airfield and Flying Display Director at Duxford, began flying at the age of 13 with the Air Training Corps and is now in his fifth year as a display pilot.
The new flight adds to an already impressive flying line-up, including the world-famous RAF Red Arrows, performing across both days, as well as the RAF Battle of Britain Memorial Flight – appearing in the year of the Spitfire’s 90th anniversary – and the ever-popular twilight flights.
The Clacton Airshow is one of the biggest events on the Essex Sunshine Coast calendar, attracting tens of thousands of visitors each year. Alongside the flying displays, visitors can enjoy ground-based attractions, food stalls and family-friendly entertainment along the seafront.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Twilight flights to light up the evening skies at Clacton Airshow 2026
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
Clacton Airshow’s dazzling twilight flights are set for a spectacular refresh this summer, with a bold new flight bringing even more drama, colour and excitement to the evening skies.
Staged by Tendring District Council (TDC), the 33rd Clacton Airshow returns on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August, when thousands of visitors are expected to head to the Essex Sunshine Coast for two days of thrilling flying displays, ground attractions and family entertainment.
Taking place on the opening day, this year’s twilight display will be an even more memorable evening experience, blending heritage aircraft, high-energy aerobatics and dazzling pyrotechnics against the backdrop of Clacton seafront.
The refreshed programme will feature the Desert Spitfire, appearing exclusively in the twilight slot on Thursday, alongside crowd favourite Otto the Helicopter’s pyrotechnic display and the ever-popular Firebirds Aerobatic Team.
This year’s twilight flights will be sponsored by Red Nova IT Solutions, helping to support one of the most popular and atmospheric parts of the Clacton Airshow programme.
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism, said: “The twilight programme is always one of the highlights of Clacton Airshow, and this year we are giving it a fresh twist to make it bigger, bolder and even more memorable.
“As part of our ‘Celebration of Aviation’ theme, the new-look programme will capture the imagination, bringing people together on our seafront to enjoy everything from iconic wartime aircraft to thrilling modern aerobatics and pyrotechnics.
“It is another reason for visitors to spend time on the Essex Sunshine Coast and enjoy the atmosphere, entertainment and spectacle that make Clacton Airshow such a fantastic event.”
At the heart of the new programme is the Desert Spitfire, which will take centre stage in the magical setting of twilight and offer a powerful tribute to one of aviation’s most recognisable aircraft.
The evening spectacle continues with Otto the Helicopter’s pyrotechnic display, combining precision flying with bursts of fire and light to illuminate the seafront sky in a truly distinctive performance.
Meanwhile, the Firebirds Aerobatic Team will bring pace, skill and teamwork to the twilight programme, with a high-energy routine showcasing the thrill of recreational and display flying.
The twilight programme adds to an already impressive flying line-up, including the RAF Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) – appearing in the year of the Spitfire’s 90th anniversary – and the world-famous RAF Red Arrows, performing across both days.
The Clacton Airshow is one of the biggest events on the Essex Sunshine Coast calendar, attracting tens of thousands of visitors each year. Alongside the flying displays, visitors can enjoy ground-based attractions, food stalls and family-friendly entertainment along the seafront.
For updates and more information about the 2026 Clacton Airshow, visit Clacton Airshow website, follow essexsunshinecoast on Instagram, or go to the official Facebook event.

https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.title: Replica RAF Typhoon cockpit and reaction challenge to inspire future STEM careers at Clacton Airshow
https://clactonairshow.com/feed/.text:
Visitors to Clacton Airshow will be able to step aboard a replica Typhoon cockpit and test their reflexes on the RAF’s Batak reaction game as part of a hands-on showcase designed to inspire future careers in aviation and science, technology, engineering and maths (STEM).
The RAF Careers Engagement team will be at the event site on West Greensward during the 33rd Clacton Airshow, staged by Tendring District Council (TDC) on Thursday 27 and Friday 28 August, giving people of all ages the chance to learn more about RAF heritage, career opportunities and the next generation of aviation talent.
On the ground, visitors will be able to experience a pilot’s-eye view from the seat of one of the RAF’s most advanced and manoeuvrable fighter jets through the Typhoon cockpit, while the Batak reaction game will offer a fun, fast-paced challenge testing the reflexes used in high-pressure aviation environments.
RAF Replica Typhoon Cockpit Ground Display
The STEM careers theme will also be reflected in the flying programme, with organisers confirming the return of the RAF Grob Tutor T1 – the aircraft used to train the next generation of RAF pilots – which will soar over the Essex Sunshine Coast this summer.
Fully aerobatic and highly manoeuvrable, the Tutor plays a vital role in teaching the fundamentals of military flying and helps show how training, engineering and technical skills come together to support a career in the air.
Squadron Leader Rach Collier, from RAF Recruiting and Selection, said: “As part of the Clacton Airshow, visitors will have a fantastic opportunity to get hands-on with the Royal Air Force.
“They can step aboard a Typhoon cockpit and experience a pilot’s-eye view from the seat of one of the RAF’s most advanced and manoeuvrable fighter jets.
“For those keen to test their reflexes, the RAF Careers Engagement team will be running the Batak reaction game – a fun and fast-paced challenge for all ages.
“It will be a unique chance to learn more about the RAF’s heritage, career opportunities, and the next generation of aviation talent.”
Councillor Ivan Henderson, TDC’s Cabinet Member for Economic Growth, Regeneration and Tourism, said the Tutor’s inclusion highlights the wider purpose of the airshow.
“The Grob Tutor may not be the biggest aircraft in the sky, but it represents something incredibly important – the future of aviation and the next generation of RAF pilots,” he said.
“It’s fantastic to have it back in the programme, demonstrating the skill, precision and discipline required to take those first steps in a flying career.
“This year’s theme, a ‘Celebration of Aviation’, is also a great opportunity to highlight how flying displays like the Grob Tutor can inspire people to think about careers in STEM and the many different roles that help keep the aviation industry moving.
“Clacton Airshow has always been about more than just spectacular displays – it’s about inspiring people, supporting our local economy and showcasing what’s possible.
“With the Red Arrows, the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight and more still to be announced, this is shaping up to be another fantastic event on the Essex Sunshine Coast.”
The Grob 115E, known in RAF service as the Tutor T1, was built specifically for military training and has been used since the early 2000s to provide elementary flying instruction.
Paul_Johnson_Flightline_UK_RAF_Tutor
Operated by No. 6 Flying Training School, it supports both University Air Squadrons and Air Cadet organisations, offering young people aged 12 to 20 the chance to experience flying and develop valuable life skills.

https://sanctus-home.com/feed/.text:
Remembering Our Founder, Stephen Turoff
It is with great sadness that we share the passing of Sanctus Founder, Stephen Turoff.
Stephen’s compassion for humankind, determination and unwavering belief in supporting people experiencing homelessness and vulnerability laid the foundations for everything Sanctus is today.
Without his vision, kindness and drive, there would be no Sanctus, and Chelmsford would be a much poorer place.
Stephen was truly a force to be reckoned with, and his legacy will continue through the lives changed, the people supported and the work of Sanctus every day.
We will remember him always. Our thoughts are with his family, friends and all those who knew and loved him.

Race the length of the River Chelmer
Thomas Capon is taking on an incredible challenge to raise money for Sanctus
On 1st June, Thomas will be swimming the River Chelmer to raise vital funds in support of the people we work with across our community.
Thomas has supported Sanctus previously and wanted to become even more involved in helping make a difference. As part of his fundraising story, he shared why supporting charities like Sanctus matters so much:
“Shelter reported in December last year that 382,618 people in England are now classified as homeless, including 175,025 children. Chelmsford isn’t isolated from this growing trend either, with the number of people on the housing register growing significantly in recent years.
But these aren’t statistics, they are people, families, sons, daughters, mothers, fathers and friends. Homelessness can affect anyone — all it takes is a turn in fortunes. Not everyone has a support system to catch them when they’re down, and that’s where a place like Sanctus comes in.”
Already, Thomas has raised over £500 towards his fundraising target — an amazing achievement that will help us continue providing meals, support and essential services to those facing homelessness and hardship.
If you’d like to support Thomas and follow his fundraising journey, you can donate here:
