https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: Remus Horse Sanctuary to celebrate World Animal Day at final Open Day of 2026
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Remus Horse Sanctuary will be opening its gates for the final Open Day of 2026 on Sunday 4 October from 1pm to 4pm, giving visitors one last opportunity this year to meet the Sanctuary’s beautiful rescue animals and learn more about the work that goes on behind the scenes. The event also coincides with World Animal Day, making it a particularly special day for everyone at Remus and the animals in its care.
World Animal Day is celebrated around the world every year on 4 October, raising awareness of animal welfare and encouraging people to take action to improve the lives of animals. For Remus, which provides a safe and loving home for more than 100 rescued horses, ponies, donkeys and other animals, it’s a fitting occasion to celebrate the animals who have found their way to the Sanctuary and the people who help make their continued care possible.
Visitors to the October Open Day will be able to meet many of the animals, find out more about their individual stories and see first-hand how Remus cares for its residents throughout the year. There will also be a range of stalls and activities to enjoy, making it a lovely day out for animal lovers of all ages. As the final Open Day of the year, it’s also a chance to say goodbye to the Sanctuary until the Open Days return in 2027, while continuing to support the vital work of the charity.
Sue Burton, Founder of Remus Horse Sanctuary, said: “It feels particularly fitting that our final Open Day of 2026 falls on World Animal Day. Every day at Remus is about putting the animals first, giving them the care, kindness and safe home they deserve.
“Our Open Days give people the opportunity to meet some of the animals, hear their stories and see why our work is so important. We’d love to welcome everyone to the Sanctuary on 4 October for what promises to be a very special day, and to celebrate the wonderful animals who are at the heart of everything we do.”
To find out more and book your tickets in advance, please visit the Sanctuary’s website at: www.remussanctuary.org/events/open-day-sanctuary-october/ or tel: 01277 356191.

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: September Birthday Celebrations at Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
September has been a busy month for birthday celebrations here at Remus, with three very special residents reaching another year older.
We may be halfway through the month already, but we couldn’t let September pass without wishing Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty a very happy birthday!
These are also the last of our birthday celebrations for 2026, as we don’t have any animals with birthdays in October, November or December. Of course, that doesn’t mean the celebrations stop. Every animal here at Remus is special to us, and they’re loved, cared for and celebrated every single day.
Happy 20th Birthday Winston!
Winston celebrated his 20th birthday on 4 September .
Winston was found at an illegal Traveller’s sale, standing alone in a dirty trailer hidden around the back. He was extremely thin and totally terrified.
When Winston arrived at Remus, blood tests revealed that he had severe liver problems caused by ragwort poisoning. He’d been kept in a field full of ragwort with nothing else available, so he was forced to eat it.
Thankfully, Winston came through this difficult time and he now thoroughly enjoys his life at Remus, surrounded by the care and companionship he deserves.
If you’d like to sponsor Winston , you can find out more by clicking on the web page with the link.
If you’d like to get Winston a birthday present as well, you can choose something from our animal treats section .
Happy 9th Birthday Marmite 2!
Marmite 2 celebrated his 9th birthday on 6 September .
Marmite had an awful start in life. He and Flint were kept in a cage for much of their early lives and were desperately thin, as well as being full of worms and covered in lice.
Thankfully, their lives are very different now. Marmite and Flint enjoy their freedom here at Remus, living happily with their field mates and receiving the care they need.
If you’d like to get Marmite 2 a birthday present , you can choose something from our animal treats section.
Happy 33rd Birthday Minty!
Minty celebrated his 33rd birthday on 22 September .
Minty came to us with three other ponies from a riding school after the owner and their 12 other horses were evicted. We were able to find homes for 12 of the horses, while the four oldest came into Remus’ care.
These ponies had been much loved and well cared for at the riding school, where they taught many youngsters in Essex how to ride and respect horses. Now Minty enjoys his retirement at Remus with his best friend and fellow riding school pony, Scotty.
Minty unfortunately has breathing problems and, during the summer, needs a respiratory pump with medication to help him breathe more easily. He takes his medication very well, and is well cared for by the Remus team.
Click on the link if you’d like to sponsor Minty .
If you’d also like to get Minty a birthday present, you can choose something from our animal treats section .
Celebrating our Remus residents every day
Birthdays are always a lovely opportunity to celebrate some of the individual characters who make up the Remus family and share a little more of their stories.
But while Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty have had their special birthday treats this month, every day is about giving all of our residents the care, kindness and security they deserve.
We’ll be back with our next birthday celebrations in January, but in the meantime, we’ll continue celebrating our wonderful herd and pack every day.
If you’d like to help us care for the animals at Remus, there are lots of ways you can support the Sanctuary, from sponsoring an animal to choosing a special treat for one of our residents.
If you’d like to meet Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty – and the rest of our darling rescues – our last Open Day of the season will take place on Sunday 4 October .

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: A Lasting Gift for the Future of Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Remember A Charity Week takes place from 7–13 September , providing a timely opportunity to think about the charities and causes that matter to you and how you might continue to support them in the future.
For Remus Horse Sanctuary, the future is something we think about every day.
Our animals rely on us for food, veterinary care, shelter and everything else they need to live happy and healthy lives. With over 100 horses, donkeys and other animals in our care, ensuring that we can continue providing that support for years to come is incredibly important.
One way you can help is by leaving a gift to Remus in your Will.
A gift in your Will, however large or small, can make a lasting difference to the animals at the Sanctuary. It could be a fixed amount, a particular item or asset, or a share of what remains of your estate after other gifts have been made.
There can also be Inheritance Tax benefits to leaving a gift to a registered charity. Charitable gifts are generally exempt from Inheritance Tax, and leaving at least 10% of your net estate to charity may reduce the rate of Inheritance Tax payable on the remainder of your estate. For the most up-to-date information, visit the [ GOV.UK guidance on leaving gifts to charity in your Will ].
Making a Will is a personal decision, and it’s important to make sure it reflects your wishes and circumstances. Remus has partnered with FreeWills , which provides a free Will-writing service, making it simple to put your wishes in writing without the usual cost of a solicitor.
If you already have a Will, it is also worth reviewing it from time to time to make sure it still reflects your wishes.
For Remus, a gift in your Will isn’t simply a donation. It is a way of helping to protect the future of animals who may need a safe home and lifelong care.
If Remus is a charity close to your heart, we would be incredibly grateful if you would consider remembering the Sanctuary in your Will.
Find out more about supporting Remus and leaving a lasting legacy on our website.
The post A Lasting Gift for the Future of Remus appeared first on Remus Horse Sanctuary .

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: September Open Day: Come and Meet the Animals at Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Join us at Remus Horse Sanctuary on Sunday 6 September for our penultimate Open Day of the year. From 1pm to 4pm, you can come and meet our wonderful horses, ponies, donkeys and other rescued animals, explore the Sanctuary, enjoy refreshments and browse the stalls. It’s a lovely afternoon out for all ages, and, importantly, your visit helps to support the vital work we do every day.
This year has been particularly challenging for the Sanctuary, with the ongoing drought putting additional pressure on our fields and meaning we are having to rely more heavily on bought-in hay and other resources to keep our animals well fed. With no government funding, the support we receive from our visitors, donors and supporters really does make a difference.
The dry conditions also mean that the Sanctuary is 100% smoking and vape free . With the fields and surrounding land so dry, the risk of a fire is something we simply cannot take. We ask everyone visiting the Sanctuary to respect this rule and help us keep our animals, team and visitors safe.
So, why not make a date for Sunday 6 September ? Come and meet the animals, enjoy a few hours at the Sanctuary and help support the work we do. And if you can’t make September, our final Open Day of the year is Sunday 4 October .
Book your tickets here >
We look forward to welcoming you!

https://basildon.foodbank.org.uk/feed/.title: Last Year, Basildon Food bank saw the highest ever levels of need
https://basildon.foodbank.org.uk/feed/.text:
On Wednesday 26 April 2023, we released our stats on the number of emergency food parcels that Basildon Food bank provided within our local community between April 2022 and March 2023.
The alarming new figures reveal that we have provided 3,362 emergency food parcels to people who couldn’t afford the essentials in Basildon over the last year – and 1,490 of these went to children.
In addition to this, food banks across the Trussell Trust network provided nearly 3 million (2,986,203) emergency food parcels to people experiencing hunger during this time – with over 1 million of these going to children.
This is the most parcels food banks in our network have ever distributed in a single year and represents a 37% increase compared to last year, and more than double the amount distributed by food banks in the same period five years ago.
This isn’t right and we can’t allow this to go on.
Together, with food banks across the Trussell Trust network, we are calling for MPs across the UK to support a social security system that guarantees our essentials, by making sure that the basic rate of Universal Credit is at least enough to afford the essentials we all need to live.
If you would like to support us by writing to your local MP, please click here to find out more.
No one should need the support of our food bank because everyone in our local community should be able to live lives free from hardship and poverty.
That’s why your support is needed now more than ever.
As we navigate these challenging times and do our utmost to meet the increasing need for our services, we would be most grateful if you could:
Please donate all types of non-perishable food items or toiletries at our usual donation points: Tesco Basildon Extra, Off Station Lane, SS13 3JU, Mayflower Retail Park, Gardiners Link, Basildon, SS14 3HZ, Pitsea Leisure Centre, Northlands Pavement, Basildon, SS13 3DU
Please make a financial donation online: https://app.goodhub.com/offerings/basildon-foodbank-operated-by-rccg-majesty-connections/donations/create , by cheque or in cash at Pitsea Leisure Centre, Northlands Pavement, Basildon, SS13 3DU
For additional support volunteering please contact us at info@basildon.foodbank.org.uk
We recognise how difficult times are right now, which is why we really appreciate all and any support you are able to offer. Together, we can ensure help is here for everyone who needs it in Basildon, whilst we also collectively work towards a more just future where no one needs our food bank to get by.
Thank you for all that you’re doing.

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Truro City 0 Billericay Town 0
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Truro City 0 – Billericay Town 0
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Jon Bird
Danny Scopes’ Billericay Town side produced a heroic defensive performance to earn a point on a wet and windy night in Cornwall against Truro City.
The home side immediately set about putting Billericay under pressure, and Luke Jephcott was brilliantly denied by Khari Ranson after Christian Oxlade-Chamberlain’s long throw caused havoc in the box.
Billericay ventured forward for the first time on nine minutes and saw a looping header from Elliot Long drop wide of the post.
Truro continued to have most of the play in the first half, with Jephcott again combining with Oxlade-Chamberlain, but the latter saw his header go just over the bar.
Town found chances hard to come by in the opening 45 minutes but put together their best move of the game on 36 minutes, though Callum Watts couldn’t keep his shot down from the edge of the box.
The Tinners dominated the final minutes of the half, and Ranson was called into action to claim multiple crosses and deal with Tyler Harvey’s header a minute before the break, ensuring it stayed level.
The second half started in dire conditions, with torrential rain and strong winds, though the hosts played on despite the weather and saw Jephcott fire just over the bar from 18 yards.
Billericay remained a danger on the break and saw a rare flurry into the box end with Jon Benton’s shot sailing over the top of Aidan Stone’s bar.
Truro’s best chance came on 65 minutes when Harvey’s header released Harvey Greenslade, but he dragged his shot wide with only Ranson to beat.
Taylor Clark then fired over at the other end as the game became stretched heading into the final 20 minutes.
City put Billericay under immense pressure in the closing stages with countless long throws from Oxlade-Chamberlain and set pieces, but Ranson and the Town back four stood up to the task well and denied any clear-cut chances.
The only chance the hosts mustered from this pressure came on 89 minutes, though Harvey’s header was straight into the hands of Ranson.
Billericay then had two chances of their own to snatch all three points in stoppage time, first when Jamie Mauge broke away only to be denied by a brilliant challenge from Jephcott.
And from the final corner in the game’s dying seconds, Paul Appiah’s goalbound shot was somehow cleared off the line by Jephcott before the referee’s whistle brought an end to an attritional contest.
The Blues move to ten league games unbeaten following the draw in Cornwall and welcome basement side Slough Town to Essex on Saturday afternoon.

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Billericay Town 3 Waltham Abbey 1
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Billericay Town 3 (Mauge 22, Benton 84, 86 pen) – Waltham Abbey 1 (Cawley 42)
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Stephen Mold of Photofold Camera Club
Jon Benton’s second brace of the week helped Billericay Town overcome a resolute Waltham Abbey side and progress to the last 64 of the FA Trophy at Pulse Stadium New Lodge.
The Step 4 visitors started the brighter and saw a shot from top scorer Prince William Domafriyie well saved by Khari Ranson in the Town goal.
Billericay’s first chance of the afternoon came on 11 minutes when Benton’s shot was deflected wide off an Abbey defender.
The away side thought they had taken the lead ten minutes later when an inswinging corner was fumbled by Ranson and dropped into the net, though referee Tommy Flemming ruled the goal out for a foul.
The Blues took the lead a minute later when Benton burst down the flank and crossed for Ipswich loanee Jamie Mauge to tap home his first Billericay goal.
Town looked for an immediate second and saw Benton weave into the box before firing just wide of the upright.
The Abbotts responded and twice forced Ranson into action with efforts from distance, the second coming from Maxwell Appauh, with the Billericay keeper pushing his shot wide.
From the resulting corner, Abbey levelled. Although the initial delivery was dealt with, Steve Cawley was on hand to turn home from close range after the ball was recycled into the area.
Billericay had a golden chance to regain the lead on 45 minutes when Mauge’s header was somehow saved by Hafed Al Droubi, before the visiting keeper then denied Elliot Long’s follow-up to ensure it was level at the interval.
The second half was delayed due to a medical incident in the crowd, with the half-time break lasting nearly 45 minutes before the sides took part in a short warm-up and the action resumed.
Town dominated possession early in the half and thought they should have had a penalty when Ryan Scott’s header struck an arm, though the officials were unmoved despite loud Billericay appeals.
The Blues continued to press for a second, seeing a shot from Benton saved by Al Droubi and Charlie Ruff’s dipping volley fall the wrong side of the post.
Waltham Abbey struggled to create chances in the second half, though they did fashion an opening that saw Appauh blaze over from inside the box on 70 minutes, before Aiden Read headed over the bar eight minutes later.
Billericay went ahead six minutes from time when some neat footwork from Benton saw him create space in the box before wrong-footing Al Droubi and finding the bottom corner.
Two minutes later, he had his second and his side’s third when Ruff was felled in the box, allowing Benton to step up and convert from 12 yards to ensure Billericay’s progression into Round Three.
Town are now unbeaten in eight games in all competitions and make the long trip to Truro City on Tuesday evening.

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Billericay Town 7 Little Oakley 0
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Billericay Town 7 (Long 7, 38, Martin Sorondo 8, Benton 23, 59, Scott 34, Ruff 79) – Little Oakley 0
Match Report by Ben Mapp
Match Photos by CGM Photography
Elliot Long and Jon Benton both netted braces as Billericay Town put Little Oakley to the sword to advance to the quarter-finals of the BBC Essex Senior Cup on a rainy night at Pulse Stadium New Lodge.
Billericay didn’t have to wait long to score the opener, as good work from Ipswich loanee Jamie Mauge allowed him to tee up Long, who swept home the Blues’ first of the evening on seven minutes.
The lead was doubled a minute later as Odei Martin Sorondo reacted quickest to turn home the rebound after Benton was denied by Acorns keeper James Askew.
The visitors looked for a route back into the cup tie and saw a long-range shot from Luke Hipkin comfortably saved by debutant Blues keeper Khari Ranson.
The Blues extended their lead on 23 minutes in somewhat comical fashion, as a mix-up between Askew and Dan Keeble allowed Benton to roll the ball into an empty net to take the game away from the visitors.
Billericay were in no mood to take their foot off the gas and made it four on 34 minutes when captain Ryan Scott headed home after Askew tipped Benton’s strike onto the bar.
The Acorns nearly grabbed a goal back soon after, but Keeble could only stab his effort over the bar from close range following a corner.
The first-half rout was completed on 38 minutes when Mauge beat two men down the right flank before squaring to Long, who netted his second and his side’s fifth.
Little Oakley had the final chance of the half when Josh McFall headed wide of the upright, but it was Billericay who headed into half-time with a comprehensive lead.
The Blues set about extending their advantage after the break, though Mauge saw his shot from the edge of the box saved by Askew.
The visitors then had a chance of their own when substitute Bobby Badham’s effort flew just over Ranson’s crossbar.
Benton grabbed his second of the game just before the hour mark when he combined with Charlie Ruff before curling his shot beyond Askew’s dive and into the far corner.
Ranson had been a spectator for much of his debut but was called into action on 66 minutes to deal with Dan Rowe’s shot from inside the area.
Town rounded off the scoring eleven minutes from time when Frankie Merrifield, making his 150th appearance for the Blues, raced away and set up Ruff to roll home Billericay’s seventh.
Despite enjoying plenty of late possession, the Acorns were unable to score a consolation as Billericay cruised into the last eight.
Danny Scopes’ side have now lost just one of their last twelve games and host Waltham Abbey in the FA Trophy on Saturday.

Referee: Joe Burgess

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Dagenham and Redbridge 2 Billericay Town 2
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Dagenham & Redbridge 2 (Hawkins 41, Beautyman 57 pen) – Billericay Town 2 (Long 26, 68)
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by CGM Photography
Elliot Long’s brace earned Billericay Town a hard-fought point in an entertaining affair against Dagenham & Redbridge at Victoria Road.
Billericay had the game’s first chance when Callum Watts looped an effort over, before Andy Carroll headed wide at the other end.
The away side looked the more likely to get the opener, and Watts saw a shot brilliantly saved by Nathan Ashmore on 12 minutes.
Another chance came and went for Billericay when Ashmore raced out to deny George Wind six minutes later.
It was one-way traffic, and Frankie Merrifield was next to go close when he dragged a deflected shot inches past the post.
The deadlock was broken on 26 minutes when Long controlled Jon Benton’s long ball before curling a shot beyond the dive of Ashmore.
Dagenham looked for a reply, and Carroll’s speculative volley from 25 yards dipped just over the bar.
The home side grew into the game approaching half-time, and Carroll forced a double save from Finley Woodham on 40 minutes.
From the resulting corner, Billericay failed to clear their lines, and Henry Hawkins headed home at the far post to level the scores at the break.
The Daggers started the second half well and saw Kayden Harrack’s long-range strike tipped onto the bar by Woodham.
The home side had the ball in the net on 55 minutes, but Josh Addae’s goal was ruled out for a foul on Woodham.
However, Dagenham went ahead two minutes later when Woodham felled Remaye Campbell in the box, and Harry Beautyman rolled the spot-kick down the middle.
The home side were now well on top and saw a shot from Liam Vincent flash wide, while Campbell headed over from six yards.
Billericay levelled against the run of play on 68 minutes when Benton rolled the ball into Long, who subsequently placed his shot through Ashmore’s legs and into the bottom corner.
The game turned scrappy as both sides searched for the winner, and Billericay came closest when Watts’ shot was blocked behind on 87 minutes.
There was to be no late drama though, as the spoils were shared after an excellent game of football.
The Blues are next in action on Tuesday night as they welcome Little Oakley in the Essex Senior Cup.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Men Claim First Victory Under Joshua Perkins in Thrilling Comeback Win
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Rebels Men secure their first win under recently appointed head coach, Joshua Perkins in a dramatic contest that went down to the wire.
Having played Nottingham just a month earlier and fallen to a narrow 79-77 defeat, the Rebels were determined to avenge the defeat and claim the important two points.
It was the Rebels who got off the mark first courtesy of a lay-up from Tyresse Hudson. Hudson’s early basket set the tone for a strong first quarter with the Rebels enjoying a good run of team play seeing contributions across the board from Ethan Conway, Tre Baumgardner and Michael Amako. Despite the visitors following the Rebels closely throughout the quarter due to a great performance from Cameron Kahn, it was the Rebels who took the lead after the opening 10 minutes holding a scoreline of 24-19.
The second quarter began in much of the same fashion. Tre Baumgardner continued his formidable form this season as he added 5 points in the opening 30 second extending the Rebels’ lead by 10.
However, around the mid-point of the quarter momentum began to swing in Nottingham’s favour. Tactical substitutions from the Hoods proved effective seeing Christian Moore and Camden Polak make an impact on the game closing the deficit and levelling the scores at 37-37.
After evening the scoreline, the Hoods continued to thrive heading into halftime, narrowly taking a 49-45 lead at the half-way point.
The third quarter continued to work in Nottingham’s favour producing their strongest spell of the game. Polak continued to dictate proceedings whilst Elliot Bailey came into the game contributing seven valuable points.
The Hoods led 80-68 heading into the final quarter but with Tre Baumgardner continuing his outstanding run this game, it was not an impossible task for the Rebels in the final quarter.
The final quarter brought the drama as momentum continued to swing back and forth. Free throws and a lay-up from Harry Gent allowed the Rebels to creep up on their visitors reducing the deficit to just 7 with four minutes left on the clock.
As the clock continued to run down, Baumgardner hit the hoops to level the score to 96-96. With just 38 seconds left overtime looked on the horizon, but Baumgarner was fouled and two free throws were awarded.
After rolling round the rim of the basket, the first free throw was missed. With everything riding on this throw, pressure was rising. Making the buzzer-beating shot Baumgardner became the hero as he secured the Rebels’ their two points and their first win since the beginning of the October.
As well as securing the win, Tre Baumgardner’s performance earned himself Player of the Match with 38 points, 4 rebounds and 8 assists.
The Rebels will hope to continue this form next weekend as they travel to Milton Keynes before returning to the Essex Sport Arena on the 28 November to face London Cavaliers.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Seek Revenge Against Nottingham Hoods
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels return to the Essex Sport Arena on Saturday 14 November with one thing on their minds: revenge.
Just a month ago, the Rebels suffered a narrow 79-77 defeat on the road against the Nottingham Hoods in a game that could have gone either way. Despite a spirited performance from Essex led by Aliou Cisse who finished with 29 points, the Hoods edged the contest late on, leaving the Rebels eager to even the score on home court this weekend.
One of the key factors in Nottingham’s victory was their balanced offensive display. Six different Hoods players finished in double figures, highlighting the depth and versatility of their offense. The Rebels will need to tighten up defensively and limit Nottingham’s scoring options if they are to come away with the win.
Essex enters the contest looking to snap a difficult run of late, having lost five consecutive games. However, with home support behind them and plenty of motivation following last month’s heartbreak, the Rebels will be determined to return to winning ways.
Led by the dynamic duo of Tre Baumgardner and Aliou Cisse, the Rebels will be hoping to deliver a strong response and secure a statement victory as they continue their push up the standings.
With the memory of the two-point defeat still fresh, all the ingredients are in place for an exciting contest between two sides with plenty to prove.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Men Fall on the Road to Worthing
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels fell 109-96 to Worthing Thunder despite an encouraging opening half that saw the visitors establish an early advantage and remain in contention through the opening twenty minutes.
The Rebels started brightly through Tre Baumgardner III who led the early scoring charge, knocking down back-to-back three-pointers in a 30 second period. Melchi Egbeyemi and Kyron Martin also enjoyed a successful spell which helped the Rebels build a narrow 30-26 lead at the end of the first quarter.
Essex continued to build momentum early in the second period, extending to an 8-point lead in the first two minutes. However, the momentum shifted dramatically later in the quarter when Worthing began to find their rhythm through Justin Hopkins and Manuel Hernandez, who combined to spark a strong run.
Hernandez repeatedly attacked the basket while Hopkins provided scoring both inside and outside the Arc. The hosts finished the half strongly to overturn the deficit and take a 59-49 lead into the break.
The decisive stretch arrived in the third quarter. Worthing’s offence exploded, with Hernandez, Craig and Ostrowsky all making major contributions. Punishing the Rebels defence, Worthing headed into the final quarter leading by 20 at 89-69.
Determined to make a comeback, the Rebels started the fourth quarter with a renewed energy, reducing the deficit to just 13 in the first two minutes. Baumgardner, Conway and Martin all connected to make crucial baskets to help reduce the deficit.
Despite the Rebels determination, Worthing continued to capitalise on the counter to ensure they kept their lead. A driving lay-up from Hernadez with 20 seconds on the clock, capped off a strong performance from the hosts who secured a 109-96 victory.
Perkins’ side will look to comeback from this defeat as they return home to the Essex Sport Arena next weekend as they host Nottingham Hoods on Saturday 14 November with a 6:30 Tip-off.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Women Secure Away Win Against Nottingham
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels take two points on the road as they secure an 88-80 win against the Nottingham Wildcats.
Tor Freeman’s side got back on track as they walked away with their second win of the Super League Basketball season this weekend.
After facing back-to-back losses to Manchester and Newcastle at home, the Rebels travelled to Nottingham to face the Wildcats, determined to turn their season around.
The hosts made a bright start immediately establishing control as they took a 12-5 advantage in the opening three minutes. However, at the midway point of the opening quarter the Rebels began to close the deficit with Olivia Forster acting as a catalyst. Forster’s 3-point jump shot came with 4 minutes on the clock and sparked successful spells from JaMya Robinson and Alexa Mikeska whose lay-ups gave the Rebels their first lead of the game.
This spur of momentum handed the Rebels a 26-22 advantage at the end of the first quarter.  The Rebels continued to stretch their advantage throughout the second quarter. Forster and Robinson continued their impressive form ensuring Rebels capitalised on the Wildcats’ mistake. Contributions also came from Lara Rohkohl and Alexa Mikeska who continued to work hard offensively and defensively.  The Rebels walked into half time ahead, extending their lead to 55-44.
The Rebels were determined to maintain their lead after half time. Whilst Rohkohl enjoyed an influential spell, the visitors endured their quietest offensive period of the game, working hard on the defence to ensure Nottingham were kept at bay.
Nottingham attempted to mount a comeback in the final quarter, Davids-Oboh and Basham helped the hosts reduce the deficit to single digits for the first time since the first quarter. Despite the Wildcats enjoying their strongest spell, consecutive 3-pointers from Rebels captain Claire Paxton halted Nottingham’s momentum.
As the clock wound down, the Rebels continued to apply the pressure. Alexa Mikeska stood out as she dominated defensively with key rebounds and steals which helped the Rebels maintain control in the closing stages.
Mikeska influence not only ensured the Rebels walked away with an 88-80 win, she also earned herself Player of the Match after registering a double-double in assists and 2 rebounds off a triple-double after adding a tally of 14 points, 8 rebounds 12 assists and 5 steals.
The Rebels will look to continue this form after the international break. Freeman’s Rebels will return to the Essex Sport Arena on 28 November where they will host the Braun Sheffield Hatters.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Essex Rebels Fall Short to the Eagles by a Single Point.
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Rebels Women endured a narrow 83-82 loss against Newcastle Eagles at the Essex Sport Arena.
The final scoreline reflected a tightly contested game, with momentum swinging between both sides from start to finish.
The opening quarter quickly set the tone for what proved to be a closely fought battle. Despite the Eagles getting off to the perfect start through summer signing Raven Thompson, who opened the scoring with a three-point jump shot, consecutive lay-ups from Rebels star Lara Rohkohl immediately levelled the scores.
With two minutes left on the clock, Claire Paxton fired the Rebels two points ahead, handing the hosts their first lead of the contest. The visitors, however, responded with a three-pointer of their own and carried that advantage into the closing stages of the quarter, leading 23-20 after the opening ten minutes.
The second quarter unfolded in much of the same fashion, with the lead changing hands repeatedly. Rohkohl remained influential throughout, scoring 10 points in the period. But the Eagles consistently found answers through Nala Williams and Alex Campbell whose efforts helped Newcastle edge into a narrow 40-39 lead at the half-time break.
The visitors produced their strongest spell of the game during the third quarter, opening their largest advantage of the evening as they built a seven-point lead.
However, the Rebels responded emphatically in the closing stages, with three consecutive three-pointers, two from Olivia Partridge and one from Cameron Taylor-Willis, halting the Eagles’ momentum and cutting the deficit to just two points heading into the final quarter at 64-62.
With the game finely poised, the Rebels seized control early in the fourth. Paxton caught fire from beyond the arc while Rohkohl continued to dominate at both ends of the floor, helping Essex establish a five-point advantage midway through the period.
Newcastle, however, produced a late surge, capitalising on second-chance opportunities and key defensive plays to claw their way back in front.
Despite Paxton drilling a buzzer-beating three-pointer to leave the Rebels just one point behind, the Eagles held on to secure a dramatic 83-82 victory.
The Rebels will travel to Nottingham next weekend to face Nottingham Wildcats.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Game Preview: Essex Rebels Women Vs Newcastle Eagles

The Rebels are home for their second consecutive weekend after hosting Manchester Basketball last Saturday. The Rebels will look to comeback after last weekend’s 101-66 defeat to league leaders, Manchester.
Despite a frustrating result, Cameron Taylor-Willis was a positive spark for the Rebels scoring 26 points including four 3-pointers adding to her tally of nine threes in just four games so far, this Super League Basketball season. After suffering defeats to Caledonia Gladiators and Braun Sheffield Hatters, Head Coach, Chloe Gaynor, will be determined to get her team back on track, marking a difficult test for the hosts.

Maddy Hinton is one to watch this Saturday. Hinton joined the Eagles this summer from Australia after playing in Australia’s National Basketball League Division One Central for the past three seasons.
The 5’6 guard has adapted well to the Super League despite never playing in England and has already registered a total of 72 points, 16 assists and 18 rebounds. Hinton had stand-out performances against Nottingham Wildcats and Leister Riders scoring a combined 39 points ranking first in points across both teams in both games.

This week should be an exciting matchup. We’ve been putting plenty of work in and are ready to show our best on Saturday.

https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.text:
Great Dunmow Town Council Completes Transfer of Brick Kiln Farm Open Space
Great Dunmow Town Council is pleased to announce that the transfer of the public open space at Brick Kiln Farm has now been completed and ownership of the land has passed to the Town Council. The transfer has been completed by the parties and submitted to HM Land Registry for formal registration.
The acquisition forms part of the long-standing planning obligations associated with the Brick Kiln Farm development and secures the open space as a community asset for the benefit of residents of Great Dunmow.
The transfer brings to completion a process that began with the submission of planning application UTT/13/0847/OP in July 2013. The application proposed the demolition of three dwellings, associated outbuildings and derelict farm buildings, and the construction of up to 68 dwellings together with associated infrastructure and approximately 9.4 hectares of public open space. The accompanying Section 106 Agreement required the developer to offer the public open space to Great Dunmow Town Council for transfer, with the land to be retained and managed for the recreational use and enjoyment of the general public.
In addition to the transfer of the land, a commuted maintenance sum has been received to support the future upkeep and management of the site.
The Council would like to thank all those involved in bringing the transfer to completion and looks forward to managing and enhancing the open space for the enjoyment of current and future generations.
Amanda Alexander, the Town Clerk, said:
“We are delighted that this important transfer has now been completed. The open space is a valuable community asset, and the Council is committed to ensuring it is maintained and managed for the benefit of residents both now and in the future.”
Further information regarding the future management of the site will be provided as plans are developed.
Amanda Alexander
Town Clerk
Great Dunmow Town Council

https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.title: PLANNING DEADLINE CLARIFICATION
https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.text:
Broadway Planning Response Deadline Clarification
UDC’s Website
Uttlesford District Council`s website states:
Neighbour consultation expiry date is Monday 24th August
Latest consultation expiry date is Wednesday 12th August
Town Council response
For a town council, the statutory deadline is the earliest of the published consultation dates, the “latest consultation expiry date” (12/08/26) not the neighbour consultation date of 24/08/26.
Latest consultation expiry date 12/08/26
This is the formal public consultation period under the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) Order.
It is the date used for statutory consultees, including town and parish councils.
Latest neighbour consultation date 24/08/26
This is the deadline for neighbours who received letters. Councils are not treated as neighbours: they are statutory consultees.
Town and Parish Councils must work to the formal consultation expiry date unless the Local Planning Authority explicitly extends the consultee period in writing.
Comments can still be submitted after the official deadline, LPAs often accept late representations, but they are not guaranteed to be taken into account.
Residents who are not neighbours, but wish to respond to the application
Residents who are not neighbours and did not receive letters from Uttlesford District Council should use the formal consultation expiry date (12/08/26) as their deadline.
Comments submitted on or before 12/08/26 are guaranteed to be treated as valid.
Comments submitted after this date are usually still accepted, but the case officer is not obliged to consider them.
If a resident wants to be absolutely safe, they should treat 12/08/26 as the deadline.

https://writtle-pc.gov.uk/feed/.title: Oak Processionary Moths
https://writtle-pc.gov.uk/feed/.text:
You may have noticed some of our oak trees on the Green have been fenced off.  This is due to oak processionary moths.  The Oak Processionary Moth (OPM) is a quarantine pest and is under official control and must be reported.  Although any tree can be infected they prefer mature oak trees.  The moths are becoming more common.
Why does it matter to me?
OPM caterpillars and nests contain hairs which cause itchy rashes, eye and throat irritations and can cause breathing difficulties in people and animals.  The caterpillars can shed hairs when they are disturbed.  The nests and the caterpillars should not be touched.  The greatest risk is between May to July when the caterpillars are most active.
What do they look like?
The nests are web like structure and are located on the boughs and branches of predominantly oak trees.  The hairy caterpillars process in formation when they are moving, hence their name.
What action have the Parish Council taken?
We have had our oak trees reviewed by tree professionals.  This years nests have been removed.  The Forestry Commission has determined Writtle is located in the buffer zone.  Currently they are actively treating sites in the buffer zone by spraying trees.  We have reported the trees we can see have nests to the Forestry Commission and the trees will be sprayed in the spring.  We will, as a precaution, relocate the two benches from under the large oak tree on the Green.
What action do I need to take?
Be vigilant.  If you have large oak trees in your garden check them.  If you spot a nest report it on Tree Alert – https://treealert.forestresearch.gov.uk/ .  Please do not touch the nests or caterpillars.  If you or your pet comes into contact with them, please seek medical advice.  The Forestry Commission have produced a useful leaflet with further information – https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6278d2a98fa8f5206c75d3ed/FC_OPMoth_Leaflet.pdf

https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.title: Open letter urges place-based focus in mental health strategy
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
An open letter to the government signed by close to 150 researchers, health chiefs and charities is calling for the new Mental Health Strategy for England to focus more on the places most affected by inequality.
Signatories, including the chief executives of Mind, YoungMinds, Place2Be and the Centre for Mental Health, are concerned the strategy will not fully reflect the challenges faced by coastal, rural and former industrial communities.
They warn that research, expertise and lived experience from these areas are being underrepresented in national policy discussions.
The letter to Social Care and Mental Health minister Alison McGovern MP is being coordinated by Professor Susan McPherson and Professor Victoria Bird from the Institute for Public Health and Wellbeing at the University of Essex.
Their research shows young adults in the most deprived coastal areas are three times more likely to experience undiagnosed mental distress than those in equally deprived inland areas.
Professor McPherson said: “Our research at Essex has shown that young people growing up in deprived coastal communities face particular disadvantages compared with their inland peers, highlighting that geography, as well as deprivation, can shape mental health outcomes.
“Excellent mental health research is taking place right across the country, and national policy should reflect that diversity of insight.”
The letter warns that mental health inequalities are shaped not only by individual characteristics and deprivation, but by access to local jobs, transport, housing, education, community infrastructure and other services.
It also notes that, based on publicly available affiliations, seven in ten contributors to the government’s Independent Review into mental health conditions, ADHD and autism were based in London, Oxford or Cambridge.
The letter’s signatories include more than 60 professors from universities across England, many of them leading experts in health inequalities.
Professor McPherson added: “To reduce inequalities effectively, England’s mental health strategy must draw on the full breadth of expertise, evidence and lived experience across the country, rather than being disproportionately influenced by a small number of places and institutions.”
The researchers are asking government to recognise geographical inequalities in the strategy and to consider insight from a more diverse range of research leaders, local partners and people with lived experience from the areas most affected.
They are also calling for funding for local authority public health teams to invest in community-led mental health work, and for the Prevention Concordat for Better Mental Health to be revived and refreshed.
Other signatories include former Minister for Care and Support Sir Norman Lamb and leaders from universities, councils and Healthwatch organisations across England.
The team, alongside Dr Emily Murray , Director of the Centre for Coastal Communities at Essex, also set out evidence on mental health in coastal areas in a response published in the BMJ this month.
Their research found that among young people in the most deprived fifth of areas in England, those who grew up on the coast reported mental functioning scores 3.7 points lower than their inland peers.

https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.title: Statement: Exploring the use of surplus accommodation
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
The University of Essex is currently considering a potential arrangement with the Ministry of Defence and Colchester Garrison regarding the use of a small section of our Colchester Campus. This would provide accommodation at The Houses for Ministry of Defence personnel for two years.
Due to lower student numbers, the University has surplus accommodation on its Campus so is looking at a variety of appropriate alternative uses.
Any revenue would be reinvested to support the University’s educational and research missions.
Deputy Vice-Chancellor Professor Chris Greer said: “No decision has been made on whether to proceed. Further work is being undertaken to understand its potential implications, practical requirements and suitability for the University community. As part of this process, we will continue discussions with the Ministry of Defence, the Students' Union and other relevant stakeholders.
“We have a proud history of working with civic and local partners, and this is one of several options we are exploring for the future use of surplus accommodation capacity. In doing so, we are seeking to balance our responsibilities to students and staff, our role as a civic institution, and the need to generate sustainable income to support our education and research activities.
“Any decision would be subject to careful consideration. We would only proceed if we were satisfied that the arrangement was in the best interests of the University community and will keep staff and students informed as these discussions progress.”
An Army spokesperson said: “We are committed to looking after our soldiers and will always strive to provide the best quality accommodation available. Colchester Garrison is exploring options to provide housing that delivers best value for money and relieves pressure on the local housing market. Discussions are being held with the University of Essex about the use of surplus student accommodation, but no agreement has been reached.”

https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.title: Scientist using AI to detect skin cancer named top 50 UK innovator
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
A computer scientist who is using AI to detect skin cancer has been named in a top 50 power list of innovative researchers in the UK.
Universities UK (UUK) has highlighted Dr Haider Raza’s work in its 50 Future Innovators list, which celebrates the groundbreaking innovations and scientific breakthroughs that are reshaping industries such as healthcare and engineering.
UUK, which represents more than 140 universities, has launched the list as part of a campaign to push for further investment into higher education research.
Dr Raza, a Senior Lecturer in the University of Essex’s School of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering, has worked with Check 4 Cancer through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) to create SKINTEL, a diagnostic tool that determines if suspicious lesions are malignant.
The tool, which is 99 per cent accurate, uses 22 patient characteristics and image analysis to deliver a diagnosis.
SKINTEL, designed to support clinicians and doctors rather than replace them, will speed up skin cancer diagnoses, reduce waiting times, and save lives by detecting the most dangerous skin lesions at the earliest opportunity.
Dr Raza said: “I'm honoured to be recognised as one of Universities UK's Future 50 Innovators.
“This recognition reflects the collaborative work undertaken with colleagues at the University of Essex, Check4Cancer and other partners to develop SKINTEL.
“What excites me most is the opportunity to demonstrate how trustworthy and explainable AI can deliver real-world impact in healthcare, helping clinicians and patients alike.”
UUK hopes its power list will inspire the next generation of innovators and secure more funding. It wants to see external investment in university innovation double to £100bn by 2035.
Professor Noam Lubell, Essex’s Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Research, said: “Dr Raza has deservedly been recognised for his dedication to using AI in healthcare and is a wonderful example of the power of research at Essex.
“His work with Check 4 Cancer has the potential to transform skin cancer diagnostics around the world and ensure interventions are made at the earliest opportunity.
“Investment in Essex’s research has allowed our academics to work with businesses and organisations to come up with innovative ideas like Dr Raza’s. It is this kind of investment that is driving change in industries and allowing universities to make a real impact in people’s everyday lives.”
Alongside his work on SKINTEL, Dr Raza is the co-founder of Seniswise AI, which helps organisations assess their AI readiness and build custom, ethical AI and agentic systems for measurable business impact.
He has also advised UK policymakers on the use of AI in healthcare, as well as trained National Emergency Department professionals in emerging technologies.
Dr Raza is able to share his expertise and knowledge with students at Essex, where he teaches Data Science and decision-making. He also mentors postgraduate researchers.
Dr Raza added: “Beyond healthcare, this recognition also highlights my broader mission through Sensiwise AI to support organisations in adopting AI responsibly and effectively. Whether working with clinicians, businesses or policymakers, my goal is to ensure that AI remains transparent, accessible and focused on delivering meaningful societal benefit.”
Malcolm Press, President of Universities UK, said “UK universities sit at the cutting edge of the breakthroughs that define our age, from life-saving treatments and clean energy to artificial intelligence. The innovations coming out of our world-leading universities anchor Britain’s leadership in the industries that will power the global economy.
“These 50 future innovators, supported by universities the length and breadth of the UK, are just the tip of the iceberg. By celebrating these individuals and their innovations we hope to inspire the next generation of founders right across the country.”

Two scientists named among the most influential researchers in the world
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
Two scientists whose work spans how crops cope with drought and how emotions shape learning have been named among the world’s most influential researchers.
Professor Tracy Lawson features on Clarivate’s Highly Cited Researchers list for the seventh year running, while Professor Reinhard Pekrun has been named in every edition since 2024.
Clarivate estimates that around one in every 1,000 scientists and social scientists worldwide is recognised on the annual list.
Professor Lawson, from the School of Life Sciences , develops ways to measure how plants photosynthesise and use water.
Her work helps researchers understand how crops respond to heat and drought and identify traits that could make them more resilient.
Earlier this year, she received the Innovation Award from the International Society of Photosynthesis Research .
Professor Lawson said: “I am delighted to be included in this list for another year - this is only possible due to the hard work and dedication of everyone in the lab and the support of colleagues and collaborators.”
Professor Pekrun, from the Department of Psychology , has pioneered research into the role of emotions in learning. His work explores how feelings such as enjoyment, anxiety and boredom affect students’ motivation and performance.
Professor Pekrun said: “I feel deeply honoured by receiving this recognition again. The recognition is based on teamwork and attests to the invaluable support I received from colleagues, students, and professional staff at Essex in pursuing our research on human emotions.”
Professor Noam Lubell , Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Research, said: “Having two academics named among the world’s Highly Cited Researchers is a brilliant achievement.
“Both Professor Lawson and Professor Pekrun are helping to shape what other researchers investigate and where their fields go next.
“They exemplify what makes the University of Essex so special and their work showcases our global reputation, reach and impact.
“I’m delighted to see both colleagues get the international recognition they deserve.”
Clarivate looks at how often other researchers cite their work, drawing on papers published between 2015 and 2025, and considers the breadth of their influence and the integrity of publication and citation patterns.
This year, Clarivate awarded 7,090 Highly Cited Researcher designations to 6,802 individuals from more than 1,200 institutions across 62 countries and regions. Some researchers were recognised in more than one field.

https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.title: Can fungus solve the British river water quality crisis?
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
The cleansing power of fungus is being trialled in a pioneering project which could help tackle Britain’s river water quality crisis.
Researchers from the School of Life Sciences are testing whether mycelium, the root-like network of Fungi can support wetlands in filtering polluted water before it flows into rivers and other systems.
The study could offer an environmentally friendly way to tackle water pollution, helping protect aquatic wildlife and people enjoying Britain's waterways.
PhD researcher Lucinda Robinson , has helped create a 'living lab' at the University's Colchester Campus to put the natural filtration system to the test.
The sacks packed with mycelium used in the experiment
Lucinda Robinson testing water quality in the 'living lab'
Six experimental wetlands, known as mesocosms, were constructed to investigate whether adding mycelium to constructed wetlands can remove harmful bacteria, including E. coli, and excess nutrients that contribute to damaging algal blooms.
Over 12 weeks, the wetlands were subjected to controlled contamination, with researchers regularly monitoring water quality across a series of experiments.
Lucinda said: "Everyone deserves to be able to swim in natural water ways and enjoy nature without the risk of getting ill.
"This natural filtration method could help to improve water quality in our waterways.
"This is an exciting project that could have real benefits on the environment and really highlights how versatile and useful mycelium could be.
"Wetlands can help with this, and we want to know whether by adding mycelium we can support them to further enhance safety for recreational users, restore currently damaged aquatic habitats, all while creating new wetland habitats where wildlife can thrive."
Looking to the future - Lucinda hopes her work will have real impact
As part of her research Lucinda has also tested river water quality
Previous laboratory studies suggest mycelium can remove pollutants and neutralise bacteria without the need for synthetic treatments.
The Essex project aims to establish whether these promising findings can be replicated in real-world conditions, potentially paving the way for wider use of the natural treatment.
Lucinda is now analysing the results to assess how effectively the mycelium-treated wetlands remove pollutants compared with conventional constructed wetlands.
If successful, the approach could eventually be scaled up to help tackle water pollution across the country.
Professor Tom Cameron , who is supervising the project, said: “It’s a very exciting area of research, where increasingly we find that the natural world already has the capacity to provide functions and services that let us live healthier lives, if only we give it room to do so.
“It may mean living differently and accepting more of nature on our doorstep so that it can provide for us.”

https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.title: Uncovering legacy of influential textile designer
https://www.essex.ac.uk/news.text:
A unique project exploring the life and legacy of one of Britain's most influential twentieth-century designers is being launched thanks to a partnership between the University of Essex and the Warner Textile Archive in Braintree.
The University’s School of Philosophical, Historical and Interdisciplinary Studies is seeking applicants for a fully funded doctoral studentship which will support a researcher to uncover the remarkable life and work of pioneering textile designer Marianne Straub, who worked for Warner & Sons in Essex for two decades from 1950 onwards.
Straub’s innovative designs helped shape everyday life in post-war Britain, appearing in London Underground trains, buses, airports, public buildings and homes nationwide, reflecting her belief that high-quality design should be accessible to everyone.
The successful applicant will become the first to study the Archive’s collection of design records, textile samples and business archives alongside her personal diaries and correspondence, helping to shed new light on the role of women, migration, industry and innovation in post-war Britain.
Dr Alix Green, who is lead supervisor alongside Dr Matthew Grant, said: “We’re delighted to be able to offer a studentship focused on a designer whose iconic fabrics furnished post-war Britain but whose life and work have been largely lost from view. It’s a project built on years of collaboration between historians at the University of Essex and the Warner Textile Archive – and one that will set Straub’s legacy within the county’s long weaving and design heritage.”
The new project, titled Fabric of Everyday Life: Marianne Straub, Textile Innovation and Design, 1950-1970, is supported by a prestigious Collaborative Doctoral Award and will give a doctoral researcher unprecedented access to a nationally significant collection of materials held by the Warner Textile Archive, alongside newly acquired personal papers that are yet to be fully catalogued.
As part of the project, the doctoral researcher will work closely with the Warner Textile Archive , the UK's largest publicly accessible archive of a single textile manufacturer. Located in Braintree, the archive preserves more than 150 years of textile manufacturing history and holds over 100,000 records, designs and artefacts linked to Warner & Sons and the wider British textile industry.
Straub's impact as a designer, innovator and educator will be explored through the project which will also examine wider themes of industrial decline and renewal, sustainability, globalisation, women's work, mass consumption and the changing nature of British identity after the Second World War.
Dr Sam Woodward, Digital Threads Project Manager at the Warner Textile Archive, said: “We are delighted to be working with the University of Essex to offer this postgraduate Collaborative Doctoral Award. As the first doctoral research project to explore the Marianne Straub Collection in such depth, it presents an exciting opportunity to generate new insights into the life and work of one of the twentieth century’s most significant, yet often overlooked, industrial designers.”
The research project forms part of Digital Threads, an ambitious programme at the Warner Textile Archive that is creating a comprehensive digital archive collection. The programme aims to transform access to the Archive’s collections, establish a nationally significant resource for design, education and research, and widen participation to help ensure their long-term sustainability.
Alongside their research, the doctoral candidate will gain hands-on professional experience in archival cataloguing, digitisation, conservation, public engagement and exhibition development. They will also contribute to educational and outreach activities designed to bring Straub's story to new audiences.
The deadline for applications is 10 February 2027.

https://hashtagunited.co.uk/feed/.text:
We’re delighted to welcome Ben Cole as the new Head Coach of Hashtag United Women!
Ben brings valuable experience in the women’s game, having spent two years at Southampton FC as Women’s Academy Technical Lead and U21 Head Coach. A UEFA A Licence holder, he worked across the club’s U14, U16 and U21 age groups, supporting player development and progression towards first-team football.
He now joins the Tags with a shared ambition for the team and a clear focus on building a culture of hard work, competitiveness and resilience.
Speaking about his appointment, Ben said:
“This is an exciting time to be joining Hashtag United Women, and I’m delighted to accept this role. From my first conversations with Jay and Spencer, it was clear that we shared the same values and ambition.”
“We have a fantastic opportunity to compete with anyone in the Women’s National League, and that starts with building a culture based on hard work, competitiveness and resilience.”
“My background in women’s U21 football has given me a good understanding of many of the players and teams in this division. I can’t wait to get started, work with the players and staff, and meet the supporters.”
Head of Football Jay Devereux explained why Ben stood out during the recruitment process:
“I’m delighted that Ben has agreed to join us as our new Head Coach. We were fortunate to have a strong field of applicants, but Ben stood out for his attention to detail, knowledge of our squad and enthusiasm for the challenge.”
Jay also thanked the players for their response during the transition:
“We’ve been able to take our time with the appointment, and I’d like to thank our players for their patience and positivity over the past few weeks. They really are a fantastic group and we’re all excited to see what the rest of the season brings under Ben’s leadership.”
Sunday’s game against Portsmouth marked Jay’s final match in interim charge. Everyone at the club would like to say a huge thank you to Jay for stepping up and leading the team during this period.
Welcome to the Tags, Ben!

https://hashtagunited.co.uk/feed/.title: A New Era Begins:Meet The Caretaker
https://hashtagunited.co.uk/feed/.text:
As part of our summer reshuffle, today we’re announcing that our founder, Spencer Carmichael-Brown, is stepping into a new temporary role known as The Caretaker . This role has been created to help guide us through an exciting period of change as we continue shaping the next chapter of Hashtag United. It’s all about making sure the direction we’re taking as a club is properly implemented across everything we do, while bringing our football and content teams even closer together. Our ambition is simple: to make football fun again. Every decision we make, from the football we play to the content we create and the experiences we deliver, will be driven by one thing: putting our fans first. As we announced earlier this summer, we won’t have a traditional men’s first team manager this season. Instead, Sammy Knott will lead the football side as Head Coach, taking responsibility for the team’s performances on the pitch while working closely with Spencer, and our Head of Football Jay Devereux, on areas such as recruitment, philosophy and the continued development of the squad. The Caretaker role will sit between football and content, helping ensure both departments work together with a clear identity and shared purpose. Spencer will also personally deliver a range of new innovations throughout the season, all designed to bring our fans closer to the action and maximise the entertainment, enjoyment and overall Hashtag United experience. From exclusive behind-the-scenes access to fresh content and new matchday ideas, there are plenty of exciting things to look forward to. Spencer takes up the role with immediate effect. As part of these changes, Joe Gorman will also be leaving his role as CEO. Joe joined us with some hugely important objectives: helping secure a permanent home for the club, overseeing the redevelopment of our new facilities and building our in-house commercial operation. He leaves the club in a much stronger position than when he joined us, and we’d like to thank Joe for everything he has done during his time with us and wish him every success in his new role. Above all, these changes are about making Hashtag United even more entertaining, accessible and enjoyable for our fans. With Spencer stepping into The Caretaker role, we’re looking forward to bringing new ideas to life throughout the season and creating even more ways for you to get closer to the club than ever before. This is just the headline. There’s much more to this than a new role. Read A Letter from The Caretaker to hear why. Want to meet The Caretaker? Your first chance will be at our First Look Invitational this Saturday, kicking off at 1pm at our new home, The Techsoc.com Stadium. Tickets are limited, so don’t miss out. The LiveScore Hashtag United partnership marks a major new chapter for the club, with LiveScore becoming our Principal Partner and front-of-shirt sponsor for both the men’s and women’s first teams.
Hashtag has always been built on partnerships.
Some of them changed everything.
Dan Brown and Ryan Adams, scoring on the pitch.
Devs and Keithy, building off it.
Harry and Shawrey, owning the virtual one.
Different people. Different eras. Different roles.
But every now and then, a partnership comes along that doesn’t just affect one team, one video, or one moment.
It affects the whole club. And this is a big one.
Introducing…
LiveScore our new Principal Partner and front-of-shirt sponsor for both our men’s and women’s first teams.
For the first time in our history, one sponsor will take the front-of-shirt position across both teams simultaneously, reflecting a shared commitment to equality, growth and the future of the game. But this is about much more than a logo on a shirt.
LiveScore have backed our vision from day one. They understand what makes Hashtag different, and they’re investing in every part of the club as we continue building our new home.
Over the next three years, the partnership will help us create new content, deliver bigger fan experiences, enhance matchdays and continue building something special on and off the pitch.
What makes this partnership feel right is that LiveScore are football fans too. Their platform connects millions of supporters around the world with the moments that matter most, the same moments we all live for every weekend.
Whether it’s a title race, a promotion push or checking results elsewhere on a crucial final day,  is built for football fans. That’s why this partnership feels like such a natural fit.
With a presence in more than 200 countries, LiveScore will help introduce Hashtag United to new audiences around the world while staying true to what has always made this club special: community, innovation and fan-first football.
LiveScore. Welcome to Hashtag.

https://hashtagunited.co.uk/feed/.title: Jay Devereux appointed as Hashtag United’s first-ever head of football
https://hashtagunited.co.uk/feed/.text:
We’re delighted to confirm that Jay Devereux, our very own Devs, has agreed terms to become Hashtag United’s new Head of Football, becoming the first person in the club’s history to take on the role.
As many of you will know, Devs recently stepped aside as Men’s First Team manager. But that certainly doesn’t mean he’s going anywhere. Hashtag United has always been built on people, and when someone has given as much to this club as Devs has, you do everything you can to keep them involved.
This appointment is a reflection of exactly that.
In his new role, Devs will oversee football operations and strategy across the entire club, including the Men’s and Women’s First Teams, recruitment, the pathway programme, and our youth teams. It’s a hugely important position within our structure, and one that will play a key role in shaping the future of football at Hashtag United.
There really is nobody better placed to take it on.
A New Role For A Club Legend
If anyone needed reminding of what Devs means to Hashtag United, his induction into the Hashtag United Hall of Fame in 2026 says everything.
For years, he has been at the heart of this football club. Through promotions, challenges, memorable moments and historic milestones, Devs has played a major role in helping build Hashtag United into what it is today. His understanding of our identity, values and ambitions is unmatched.
Moving into the Head of Football role feels like a natural progression.
His passion for the club is clear, his standards are high, and his knowledge of the game across every level of our football pathway makes him the ideal person to help drive the next stage of our journey.
This is not a farewell wrapped up in a new job title. It is an opportunity for Devs to make an even greater impact across the whole football club, helping support and develop every area of the game under the Hashtag United banner.
Word From Our Founder
Here’s what Spencer Owen had to say:
“As stressed when we announced his departure from the Men’s manager role, I’ve been very keen to keep Devs at the club, which is why I’m delighted he’s agreed to become our first ever Head of Football. This is a role that will see Devs oversee football operations and strategy across our Men’s, Women’s and Youth teams.
“He’s perfect; his passion for our club is undeniable, his understanding of our history and future runs very deep, and his knowledge, ethics and diligence are the exact traits we want spearheading our new-look structure. I’m over the moon that we get to continue our partnership working together.”
Word From Devs
And from the man himself:
“Although it’s the right time for me to step aside as manager, I really don’t feel ready to walk away from something I care so deeply about. This club, and being part of it, is incredibly important to me, which is why I’m delighted to have been asked to stay involved.
“I’m excited to be able to build on my involvement beyond the Men’s 1st Team, and I’m looking forward to supporting the management and their teams across the men’s, women’s and youth sections of our club.”
This appointment marks an exciting new chapter for Hashtag United.
As the club continues to evolve both on and off the pitch, strong foundations are being put in place to support long-term success across every level of the football programme. Bringing everything together under a clear football structure is an important step forward, and having someone with Devs’ experience, commitment and understanding of the club leading that process is invaluable.
Few people embody what Hashtag United is all about in the way Devs does.
Having a Hall of Famer with his passion, experience and deep connection to the club at the heart of our football operation is exactly the sort of move that demonstrates our ambition for the future while staying true to who we are.
Please join us in congratulating Devs on his new role.
Welcome to the role, Devs.
Let’s get right behind him.
Let’s go.
